# Build the macOS native editor SDK

Status: IN_PROGRESS

## Goal and entry conditions

Workspace: `core`. Deliver an embeddable macOS editor using real native controls, the shared Rust model and portable modules. Paths are relative to `core`; planned paths are created by their task. Read [native parity](../specs/native-sdk-parity.md), [client contracts](../specs/client-contracts.md), [extension library](../specs/extension-library.md), and only the active task's context.

Upstream entry gates: `12-client-contracts.md`, `07-extension-modules.md`, `13-change-diffs.md` and `21-extension-library.md` complete at the current revision with passing evidence.
The historical desktop filename now contains only the macOS branch. Windows is roadmap 22 and Linux is roadmap 23. Their probes are not entry gates for macOS.


## Execution rules

One parent per iteration, 15–45 minutes plus focused validation. Reuse qualified shared behavior. If a required primitive or boundary is larger, propose a concrete controller split before broad edits. Failed/skipped prerequisites stay unchecked; task counts are not delivery estimates.

Task 1 creates the real dispatcher/bootstrap suite. Later tasks create their named suites before use; unknown suites, missing tooling and zero tests fail. These are planned commands. Tests live in `native/macos/tests/`. Preserve commands, executed/passed/failed/skipped counts, revisions, fixture/artifact hashes and failures in separate progress; source checkmarks are controller-owned.

Use deterministic fixtures and mocked services; no provider calls, live credentials, production writes, WebViews or publication. Simulations cannot qualify real IMEs/accessibility. Roadmap 20 owns actual OS/device/manual qualification; this track delivers implementation/package readiness.

## Epic DSK-1 — Implement the native adapter

### Task DSK-1.1 — Bootstrap the native SDK test host

- [ ] DSK-1.1 Bootstrap the native SDK test host.

Purpose: bootstrap.
Context: `native/macos/` (project/test bootstrap only).
Dependencies: none.
Session scope: 15–45m; split if larger.
Acceptance: Pinned tooling builds a native control and runs a real bootstrap test; missing tools name an exact unblock condition.

Implementation:

- [ ] DSK-1.1-I1 Pin Xcode, Swift, macOS SDK, deployment range and CPU slices. Create an AppKit SDK target, native test host and dispatcher with one real XCTest bootstrap case. Initialize capability.json as unqualified.

Validation:

- [ ] DSK-1.1-V1 `bash native/macos/scripts/check.sh bootstrap`. Assert acceptance; require nonzero matching tests.

Evidence: Commands/counts/revisions in progress.
Handoff: Last substep and next action.
Blocked behavior: Unchecked; name owner/unblock condition.

### Task DSK-1.2 — Qualify the native control candidate

- [ ] DSK-1.2 Qualify the native control candidate.

Purpose: toolkit.
Context: `native/macos/probe/`.
Dependencies: DSK-1.1.
Session scope: 15–45m; split if larger.
Acceptance: A native fixture proves composition and editable cell/atom feasibility; unsupported required routes block dependents.

Implementation:

- [ ] DSK-1.2-I1 Probe AppKit NSTextView and the selected native TextKit path; record selected input/selection hooks and table/atom limitations. Choose real native child controls when needed; this is feasibility, not parity.

Validation:

- [ ] DSK-1.2-V1 `bash native/macos/scripts/check.sh toolkit`. Assert acceptance; require nonzero matching tests.

Evidence: Commands/counts/revisions in progress.

Blocked behavior: Unchecked; name owner/unblock condition.

# Build the Windows native editor SDK

Status: IN_PROGRESS

## Goal and entry conditions

Workspace: `core`. Deliver an embeddable Windows editor using real native controls, the shared Rust model and portable modules. Paths are relative to `core`; planned paths are created by their task. Read [native parity](../specs/native-sdk-parity.md), [client contracts](../specs/client-contracts.md), [extension library](../specs/extension-library.md), and only the active task's context.

Upstream entry gates: `12-client-contracts.md`, `07-extension-modules.md`, `13-change-diffs.md` and `21-extension-library.md` complete at the current revision with passing evidence.
This OS branch runs independently of the other desktop roadmaps. Missing hosts or failed probes on another OS do not block its dependency-ready tasks.


## Execution rules

One parent per iteration, 15–45 minutes plus focused validation. Reuse qualified shared behavior. If a required primitive or boundary is larger, propose a concrete controller split before broad edits. Failed/skipped prerequisites stay unchecked; task counts are not delivery estimates.

Task 1 creates the real dispatcher/bootstrap suite. Later tasks create their named suites before use; unknown suites, missing tooling and zero tests fail. These are planned commands. Tests live in `native/windows/tests/`. Preserve commands, executed/passed/failed/skipped counts, revisions, fixture/artifact hashes and failures in separate progress; source checkmarks are controller-owned.

Use deterministic fixtures and mocked services; no provider calls, live credentials, production writes, WebViews or publication. Simulations cannot qualify real IMEs/accessibility. Roadmap 20 owns actual OS/device/manual qualification; this track delivers implementation/package readiness.

## Epic WIN-1 — Implement the native adapter

### Task WIN-1.1 — Bootstrap the native SDK test host

Context: `native/windows/` (project/test bootstrap only).

# Build a local-first Markdown editor client

Status: IN_PROGRESS

## Goal and entry conditions

Workspace: `cli` (sibling of `architecture`). Deliver local Markdown/literal-text editing and optional online hosted document editing through the same client, as defined in [the CLI contract](../specs/cli.md). Read `../architecture/specs/packages-release.md`, `../architecture/specs/verification.md` and the active task's named context. Paths below are relative to `cli` unless explicitly prefixed with `../architecture/`. Planned files are created by their task. Source is controller-owned; write state/evidence in the separate progress file.

Base upstream entry gates: `02-engine.md` and `05-markdown-content.md` complete at the current source revision with passing artifact evidence, including FMT-1.12 source reconciliation. These base gates also appear in the manifest. Additional hosted gate: tasks CLI-1.7 through CLI-1.9 and CLI-1.12 require `06-synchronization.md` complete at the current revision with qualified protocol/receipt evidence. This task-specific gate is explicit here because the manifest models whole-track entry edges only. Local tasks CLI-1.1 through CLI-1.6, secondary diagnostics CLI-1.10 and local qualification/packaging CLI-1.11 can proceed without hosted readiness.

## Execution rules

Each iteration may implement at most one parent task, including all its implementation and validation substeps. Target 15–45 minutes plus validation; if a boundary is too large, stop with a precise proposed split for the controller. Pick a task only when every named dependency and applicable upstream gate is implemented and validated. Other ready tasks are permitted independent work. Do not launch implementation while its entry gate is unavailable.

Create named checks before invoking them. Record nonzero executed/passed/failed/skipped counts; missing tests and zero-match Rust filters fail acceptance. Run the narrow check, then relevant integration checks. Use prepared fixtures, fake editor executables and mocked service/auth/receipt transports only. No model API tests, live credential loading, production hosted writes, live dogfood, background runner startup or publication outside an explicit release task.

Local editing is the first deliverable. Hosted connectivity adds to that client; it must never make local file editing require a network or account. The historical filename is retained for existing links/configuration; it no longer limits this track to diagnostics.

# Qualify optional extensions on mobile browsers

Status: IN_PROGRESS

## Goal and entry conditions

Workspace: `core`. Read `../architecture/specs/mobile-web.md` and only the active task's named context. Paths below are workspace-relative unless explicitly prefixed `../architecture/`. Planned implementation paths, suites and commands are created by their owning task. This is a delivery contract, not evidence of implemented mobile support.

Required upstream tracks: `40-mobile-web.md`, `25-rich-content-extensions.md`, `26-link-resolution.md`, `27-document-conversion.md` and `30-architecture-fitness.md` complete at reviewed immutable source/implementation revisions with passing artifacts. These gates supply baseline mobile editing and existing optional semantic capabilities. AIN-1.2, AIN-1.3 and AIN-1.10 from track 39 gate only MWX-1.7; this track does not wait for native assistance tasks or all of track 39. Local Dependencies fields refer only to this file.

Rust continues to own content, commands, validation, anchors and history. This track adapts browser presenters and consumes existing portable modules; it adds no native SDK implementation, document schema, alternate selection/history model or browser policy to Rust. Baseline editing and portable extension work remain independently owned. Missing portable commands are reported to their owner rather than recreated in a mobile presenter.

## Execution rules

The controller owns this source. Record checkmarks, exact commands, counts, evidence and interruption handoff in the separate progress file. Run at most one parent per iteration. Each parent targets 15–45 minutes plus focused validation; if its implementation or actual-device matrix cannot fit, propose a stable controller-reviewed split before implementation and retain its full acceptance. Required failed/skipped prerequisites remain locked.

The [mobile extension catalog](../tests/mobile-extension-cases.md) contains 32 planned cases. MWX-1.1 creates its executable index; each owner adds its assertions; MWX-1.8 records final actual-device observations and measured overhead. Create named suites and dispatcher entries before invoking them. Unknown suites, missing assertions and zero matches fail acceptance. Record automated, actual-device and evidence-validator counts separately. Deterministic fixtures and mocked transports cover all automated checks; no paid inference, provider calls, credential loading or automatic fixture recording is authorized.

Preserve OS text selection, scrolling and pinch zoom. Controls are discoverable without hover; every gesture operation has a simple tap/control alternative and an accessible keyboard route where applicable. Meet the scoped WCAG 2.2 AA target-size rule: at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, or a recorded applicable spacing/exception condition; aim for 44 by 44 CSS pixels for primary touch controls. A compact document or fine pointer is not a blanket exception. Feature-detect optional APIs, handle rejection and retain the catalog's fallback paths. Reuse track 40 geometry/focus/lifecycle primitives. Stop only verified task-owned test browsers/servers and preserve other tasks' services and retained evidence.

## Epic MWX-1 — Adapt and qualify existing extension presenters for mobile web

### Task MWX-1.1 — Establish extension capability and absence checks

- [ ] MWX-1.1 Establish extension capability and absence checks.

Purpose: Make mobile-extension qualification consume existing feature contracts and a measurable disabled baseline.
Context: `tests/browser/mobile-extensions/index.ts`; `tests/browser/mobile-extensions/capabilities.spec.ts`; `tests/consumers/mobile-extensions/`; `../architecture/specs/mobile-web.md`; `../architecture/specs/ecosystem-maintainability.md`; [case catalog](../tests/mobile-extension-cases.md).
Dependencies: none.
Session scope: One capability/index boundary, normally 15–45 minutes plus focused checks; propose a controller-reviewed split if necessary.
Acceptance: MWX-C01–MWX-C04 map to executable assertions with fixture hashes and named feature/platform capabilities. Minimal packed consumers omit disabled mobile-extension JS/CSS/assets and install zero extension-owned listeners, observers, timers, workers or network activity. Baseline mobile editing stays available; registering a disabled capability does not mutate content/history or read browser globals at import.

Implementation:

- [ ] MWX-1.1-I1 Create the case index and packed-consumer harness using existing FIT capability/loading profiles. Record available/enabled/authorized/qualified states separately, ownership of every measured resource and byte contribution, and absent/rejected optional API fixtures. Declare profile limits before measuring; retain existing baseline performance limits.

Validation:

- [ ] MWX-1.1-V1 `npm run test:mobile-extensions -- --group capabilities`; `node --test tests/consumers/mobile-extensions/disabled.test.mjs`. Create these checks here. Assert import/asset graphs, zero disabled extension work and nonmutating unsupported states; count baseline resources separately. Record exact commands/exits, nonzero executed/passed/failed/skipped counts, source/implementation/fixture revisions and artifact hashes.

Evidence: Separate progress entry `MWX-1.1` links immutable inputs, per-case counts and production bundle/resource artifacts; retain failed evidence.
Handoff: Last completed substep, changed paths/symbols, unresolved capability or failing case, and next bounded action.
Blocked behavior: Leave `MWX-1.1` unchecked; record BLOCKED/PROBLEM/NEEDS_INFO with owner, unblock condition and retry trigger. Select another dependency-ready task; otherwise stop and report.

### Task MWX-1.2 — Adapt command and reference controls for touch

Purpose: Make existing slash, command and reference presenters usable around the mobile keyboard and native selection.
Context: `packages/web/src/modules/slash/`; `packages/web/src/modules/references/`; `tests/browser/mobile-extensions/menus.spec.ts`; `../architecture/specs/editor-interactions.md`; `../architecture/specs/link-resolution.md`; [case catalog](../tests/mobile-extension-cases.md).

Acceptance: MWX-C05–MWX-C08 pass. Named tap controls expose commands without typing slash or hovering; anchored menus remain reachable after keyboard/viewport changes and internal focus transfer. Selection, composing text and one-command history semantics survive activation, dismissal and stale results. References retain permission-checked preview/activation and no implicit fetch policy.

## Goal and entry conditions

Workspace: `core`; only AIN-1.9 implements in sibling `cli`. Paths below are workspace-relative unless explicitly prefixed `../cli/` or `../architecture/`. # Build the iOS native editor SDK

Status: IN_PROGRESS

## Goal and entry conditions

Workspace: `core`. Deliver an embeddable iOS editor using real native controls, the shared Rust model and portable modules. Paths are relative to `core`; planned paths are created by their task. Read [native parity](../specs/native-sdk-parity.md), [client contracts](../specs/client-contracts.md), [extension library](../specs/extension-library.md), and only the active task's context.

Upstream entry gates: `12-client-contracts.md`, `07-extension-modules.md`, `13-change-diffs.md` and `21-extension-library.md` complete at the current revision with passing evidence.

Platform preparation gate from [roadmap 09](09-native-preparation.md): `NAT-1.1` (portable engine entry), `NAT-1.2` (bounded native bindings), `NAT-1.3` (Swift headless round-trip host) and `NAT-1.5` (iOS text-control patch) must have passing evidence for the consumed engine/binding revisions. Read those task records and their individual artifacts. Completion of the whole preparation roadmap, joined follow-up `NAT-1.7`, and Android tasks are not prerequisites.

## Execution rules

One parent per iteration, 15–45 minutes plus focused validation. Reuse qualified shared behavior. If a required primitive or boundary is larger, propose a concrete controller split before broad edits. Failed/skipped prerequisites stay unchecked; task counts are not delivery estimates.

Task 1 creates the real dispatcher/bootstrap suite. Later tasks create their named suites before use; unknown suites, missing tooling and zero tests fail. These are planned commands. Tests live in `native/ios/tests/`. Preserve commands, executed/passed/failed/skipped counts, revisions, fixture/artifact hashes and failures in separate progress; source checkmarks are controller-owned.

Use deterministic fixtures and mocked services; no provider calls, live credentials, production writes, WebViews or publication. Simulations cannot qualify real IMEs/accessibility. Roadmap 20 owns actual OS/device/manual qualification; this track delivers implementation/package readiness.

## Epic IOS-1 — Implement the native adapter

Purpose: bootstrap.

Session scope: 15–45m; split if larger.

Implementation:

- [ ] IOS-1.1-I1 Verify the four preparation records and artifact revisions, without requiring Android or the joined follow-up. Pin Xcode, Swift, iOS SDK, deployment range and supported device/simulator slices. Create a Swift SDK target, native test host and dispatcher with one real XCTest bootstrap case. Initialize capability.json as unqualified.

Validation:

# Deliver rich content extensions with bounded work

Status: IN_PROGRESS

## Goal and entry conditions

Workspace: `core` (sibling of `architecture`). Read [the owning contract](../specs/rich-content-extensions.md), [verification](../specs/verification.md) and the active task context. Paths are relative to `core` unless prefixed with `../architecture/`. Planned implementation/test files are created by their task. Source is controller-owned; write checkmarks, state and evidence only in the separate progress file.

Upstream entry gates: `05-markdown-content.md`, `07-extension-modules.md`, `12-client-contracts.md`, `13-change-diffs.md`, `21-extension-library.md` complete at current source revisions with passing artifact evidence. Dependencies below name only parents in this file. Do not launch implementation while an upstream gate is unavailable.

Reuse qualified roadmap07/21 implementations and shared client ownership. This track delivers portable/backend contracts and browser implementations; full native/TUI wiring belongs to roadmaps31–36 and is not a prerequisite. Any use of another future feature is through the owning typed contract and prepared fixtures until downstream integration.

## Execution rules

Each iteration implements at most one parent, including all its substeps. Target 15–45 minutes plus focused validation. Locate actual symbols before editing and reuse their owning implementation. If the boundary is larger, record the remaining acceptance and a precise controller split. Keep unmet prerequisites unchecked.

Create named checks before invoking them; missing tests and zero-case filters are failures. Capture full logs locally, then record exact commands/results, nonzero executed/passed/failed/skipped counts, fixture/artifact hashes and source/implementation revisions. Use prepared network/auth/media responses and deterministic local fixtures. No model/provider calls, real credentials, private-site probes, production writes, background runner startup or publication are authorized. Follow process/disk teardown in the verification contract.

# Deliver the native Rust terminal editor

Status: IN_PROGRESS

## Goal and entry conditions

Workspace: `cli` (sibling of `architecture`). Read [the owning contract](../specs/tui-client.md), [shared client contracts](../specs/client-contracts.md) and the active task's named context. Paths below are relative to `cli` unless explicitly prefixed with `../architecture/`. Planned implementation/test files are created by their task. Source is controller-owned; write checkmarks, state and evidence only in the separate progress file.

Upstream entry gates: `11-offline-cli.md`, `12-client-contracts.md`, `13-change-diffs.md` complete at current source revisions with passing artifact evidence. Cross-roadmap IDs are context references; dependencies below name only parents in this file. Do not launch implementation while an upstream gate is unavailable.

The terminal UI consumes the existing local/hosted CLI services and shared source-buffer API. MCP is an app-owned optional feature, not a prerequisite for terminal editing. Local targets remain usable without a network/account; configured host adapters add online synchronization. This track produces qualified artifacts; final publication and cross-client claims belong to their release owner.

## Execution rules

Each iteration may implement at most one parent task, including all its implementation and validation substeps. Target 15–45 minutes plus focused validation. Inspect actual symbols before editing; reuse the qualified owning implementation. If the named boundary is larger, record the exact remaining acceptance and a proposed controller split rather than silently expanding scope or weakening it. Other dependency-ready parents in this track are permitted independent work; unmet prerequisites remain unchecked.

Create the named tests before invoking them. Capture full logs locally; record nonzero executed/passed/failed/skipped counts, exact commands, fixture/artifact hashes and revisions in progress. Missing tests, zero-match filters, failed checks and skipped required cases never prove completion. Use deterministic fixtures and mocked host/auth/receipt transports. No model/provider calls, live credential loading, production document writes, background runner startup or publication are authorized by this implementation track.

## Epic TUI-1 — Deliver the native Rust terminal editor

# Build the Android native editor SDK

Status: IN_PROGRESS

## Goal and entry conditions

Workspace: `core`. Deliver an embeddable Android editor using real native controls, the shared Rust model and portable modules. Paths are relative to `core`; planned paths are created by their task. Read [native parity](../specs/native-sdk-parity.md), [client contracts](../specs/client-contracts.md), [extension library](../specs/extension-library.md), and only the active task's context.

Upstream entry gates: `12-client-contracts.md`, `07-extension-modules.md`, `13-change-diffs.md` and `21-extension-library.md` complete at the current revision with passing evidence.

Platform preparation gate from [roadmap 09](09-native-preparation.md): `NAT-1.1` (portable engine entry), `NAT-1.2` (bounded native bindings), `NAT-1.4` (Kotlin headless round-trip host) and `NAT-1.6` (Android text-control patch) must have passing evidence for the consumed engine/binding revisions. Read those task records and their individual artifacts. Completion of the whole preparation roadmap, joined follow-up `NAT-1.7`, and iOS tasks are not prerequisites.

## Execution rules

One parent per iteration, 15–45 minutes plus focused validation. Reuse qualified shared behavior. If a required primitive or boundary is larger, propose a concrete controller split before broad edits. Failed/skipped prerequisites stay unchecked; task counts are not delivery estimates.

Task 1 creates the real dispatcher/bootstrap suite. Later tasks create their named suites before use; unknown suites, missing tooling and zero tests fail. These are planned commands. Tests live in `native/android/tests/`. Preserve commands, executed/passed/failed/skipped counts, revisions, fixture/artifact hashes and failures in separate progress; source checkmarks are controller-owned.

Use deterministic fixtures and mocked services; no provider calls, live credentials, production writes, WebViews or publication. Simulations cannot qualify real IMEs/accessibility. Roadmap 20 owns actual OS/device/manual qualification; this track delivers implementation/package readiness.

## Epic AND-1 — Implement the native adapter

Session scope: 15–45m; split if larger.
Acceptance: The four named preparation tasks have passing fixture/build evidence matching the consumed engine/binding revisions. Pinned tooling builds a native control and runs a real bootstrap test; missing evidence/tools name an exact unblock condition.

Implementation:

- [ ] AND-1.1-I1 Verify the four preparation records and artifact revisions, without requiring iOS or the joined follow-up. Pin Gradle wrapper, Android plugin, Kotlin, JDK, NDK, API range and supported ABIs. Create an Android library, native test host and dispatcher with one real instrumented bootstrap case. Initialize capability.json as unqualified.

Validation:

- [ ] AND-1.1-V1 `bash native/android/scripts/check.sh bootstrap`. Assert acceptance; require nonzero matching tests.

# Deliver a cloud document store reference host

Status: IN_PROGRESS

## Goal and entry conditions

Workspace: `core`; paths are core-relative unless prefixed `../architecture/`. Follow `../architecture/specs/cloud-document-store.md`. This track implements one deployable host with provider-neutral ports and a real local durable adapter; SYN's prepared-auth loopback relay is insufficient.

Required upstream tracks: `06-synchronization.md`, `12-client-contracts.md`, `25-rich-content-extensions.md` complete at reviewed revisions with passing evidence, including actual blob/attachment ports. Whole-track gates are checked before launch; dependencies below are local to this file.

## Execution rules

One parent per iteration, 15–45 minutes plus checks. If a boundary is larger, the controller must split it before implementation. Controller owns source checkboxes; workers write progress in the separate configured file. Planned paths/test targets are created by their named task. Each named Rust integration target must execute nonzero cases; missing targets, zero matches, failures and skips cannot pass acceptance. Reuse upstream semantic cases; do not implement another CRDT.

All automated checks use deterministic credentials, local durable stores, fault fixtures and mocked external transports; no paid inference, `.secrets`, live-provider writes or automatic fixture recording. This track selects implementation libraries, not a hosting provider. Reference tests do not establish configured-provider durability or public deployment readiness. Production encrypted profiles require tracks19/24 and the final server/profile release gate; their absence does not block baseline reference delivery. Do not provision or publish as an implicit check.

# Prove native portability without claiming native SDK parity

Status: IN_PROGRESS

## Goal and entry conditions

Workspace: `core` (sibling of `architecture`). Deliver only the outcomes below. Read `../architecture/specs/modules-native.md`, `../architecture/specs/verification.md` and the active task's named context. Paths below are relative to `core` unless explicitly prefixed with `../architecture/`. Planned files are created by their task. Source is controller-owned; write state/evidence in the separate progress file.

Upstream entry gates: `02-engine.md` complete at current source revision with passing artifact evidence.

## Execution rules

Each iteration may implement at most one parent task, including all its implementation and validation substeps. Target 15–45 minutes plus validation; if a boundary is too large, stop with a precise proposed split for the controller. Pick a task only when every named dependency is implemented and validated. Other ready tasks are permitted independent work; a roadmap entry gate remains mandatory for its dependents. Do not launch this roadmap while its upstream gate is unavailable.

Create named checks before invoking them. Record nonzero executed/passed/failed/skipped counts; missing tests and zero-match Rust filters fail acceptance. Run the narrow check, then relevant integration checks. Use prepared fixtures and transports only. No model API tests, live dogfood, background runner startup or publication outside an explicit release task.

Each iteration may implement at most one parent task, including all its implementation and validation substeps. Target 15–45 minutes plus validation; if a boundary is too large, stop with a precise proposed split for the controller. Pick a task only when every named dependency is implemented and validated. # Complete everyday typing and editing behavior

Status: IN_PROGRESS

## Goal and entry conditions

Workspace: `core` (sibling of `architecture`). Read [editor interactions](../specs/editor-interactions.md), the active task's rows in the [case catalog](../tests/editor-interaction-cases.md), and its named paths. Paths are relative to `core` unless prefixed `../architecture/`. Planned implementation files and commands are created by their owner. This roadmap extends existing behavior; it does not claim a shipped browser editor.

Upstream entry gates: `04-browser-input.md`, `05-markdown-content.md`, `07-extension-modules.md` and `42-editing-regression-suite.md` complete at reviewed current source/implementation revisions with passing evidence. Baseline tasks remain responsible for basic input; this track closes concrete context and regression gaps. A missing engine primitive needs a qualified upstream schema/command change before its dependent task. Roadmap 10 requires this track; the optional assistance extension is separate in 39.

## Execution rules

The controller owns this source; workers write progress and evidence separately. Implement at most one parent per iteration, normally 15–45 minutes plus validation. If a boundary outgrows that limit, propose a controller split rather than weaken acceptance. Local Dependencies refer only to this file. Create named checks before running them and ensure filters match nonzero intended cases. Record exact commands, executed/passed/failed/skipped counts, revisions and fixture hashes; preserve failures. All automated input/provider cases use deterministic prepared fixtures and mocked external transports, with real engine/adapters. No paid inference, `.secrets`, automatic fixture recording or background runner launch is authorized. Actual OS/AT qualification is a separately recorded manual workflow.

After the in-flight fixed-pair ENG-1.7 boundary, prefer ready ENG-1.16, then finish ENG-1.6. ENG-1.17 selects/qualifies general ownership and ENG-1.18 integrates it before downstream structural work. These new parents split profile qualification from command integration to preserve bounded sessions. Preserve prior marks/foundation evidence and all original acceptance; do not claim the new profiles pass before their own receipts. Workers adopt this source between sessions and reconcile the stale ENG-1.6 mapping deferral against the new fact without the controller rewriting their progress file.

Controller structural unblock 2026-10-11: `../architecture/specs/schema-v4.md` now supplies the exact nested list/quote, check/numbering, code/separator, versioned place and reversible history-control contract. Preserve completed v3 work and ENG-1.8-P1; retire the old unspecified ENG-1.8/1.9 mapping deferrals against this new source. Ready order is ENG-1.19, ENG-1.20, ENG-1.21, then the original ENG-1.8/1.9 boundaries. Qualifications are separate from production integration and original command acceptance. Implement these authorized contracts; if a concrete contradiction/failure remains, provide the exact failing rule, a deterministic reproducer and a bounded repair/split rather than repeatedly asking whether schema work is authorized. All original acceptance remains mandatory. If no ready implementation or unfinished material prerequisite exists, report BLOCKED with a precise controller handoff and stop instead of spending further iterations on unchanged hashes or summaries.

Controller retained-join resolution 2026-10-12: `../architecture/specs/schema-v5.md` supplies the exact ENG-1.9-F1 resolution. Compatibility/editability is captured in immutable split/join preparation witnesses; replay does not re-evaluate it from mutable presentation. Preserve frozen v4 and its positive failure/guard evidence. New profile/tuple qualification ENG-1.22 is ready from completed ENG-1.21; then integrate ENG-1.23 and close full ENG-1.9 acceptance. The previous unspecified contract wait is replaced by these authorized gates. Do not repeat unchanged blocked recovery or feature failures while the new prerequisite is ready. Existing 15 checked parents remain bounded evidence; future consumers use the qualified v5 correction without automatic migration. Reuse matching final checks when only closing a bookkeeping parent: identify the original executed command/counts/receipt and revalidate source hashes instead of rerunning unchanged broad suites.

## Execution rules

Each iteration may implement at most one parent task, including all its implementation and validation substeps. Target 15–45 minutes plus validation; if a boundary is too large, stop with a precise proposed split for the controller. Pick a task only when every named dependency is implemented and validated. Other ready tasks are permitted independent work; a roadmap entry gate remains mandatory for its dependents. Do not launch this roadmap while its upstream gate is unavailable.

Create named checks before invoking them. Record nonzero executed/passed/failed/skipped counts; missing tests and zero-match Rust filters fail acceptance. Run the narrow check, then relevant integration checks. Use prepared fixtures and transports only. No model API tests, live dogfood, background runner startup or publication outside an explicit release task.

Toolchain preflight: before Node/npm or Rust/Yjs exchange checks, explicitly select the installed Node 24.19.0 runtime in the command environment and verify `node --version`. # Build the continuous browser editing surface

Status: IN_PROGRESS

## Goal and entry conditions

Workspace: `core` (sibling of `architecture`). Deliver only the outcomes below. Read `../architecture/specs/web.md`, `../architecture/specs/verification.md` and the active task's named context. Paths below are relative to `core` unless explicitly prefixed with `../architecture/`. Planned files are created by their task. Source is controller-owned; write state/evidence in the separate progress file.

Upstream entry gates: `02-engine.md` complete at current source revision with passing artifact evidence, `03-local-storage.md` complete at current source revision with passing artifact evidence.

## Execution rules

Each iteration may implement at most one parent task, including all its implementation and validation substeps. Target 15–45 minutes plus validation; if a boundary is too large, stop with a precise proposed split for the controller. Pick a task only when every named dependency is implemented and validated. Other ready tasks are permitted independent work; a roadmap entry gate remains mandatory for its dependents. Do not launch this roadmap while its upstream gate is unavailable.

Create named checks before invoking them. Record nonzero executed/passed/failed/skipped counts; missing tests and zero-match Rust filters fail acceptance. Run the narrow check, then relevant integration checks. Use prepared fixtures and transports only. No model API tests, live dogfood, background runner startup or publication outside an explicit release task.

# Local document import and export extensions

Status: planned capability contract. Format names below are targets, not claims
that the current scaffold imports or exports them.

Conversion is explicit and local. Optional Rust format adapters produce a bounded
prepared semantic batch or an output artifact from a fixed document revision.
They consume the [base formats](formats.md), [shared client](client-contracts.md),
[extension library](extension-library.md) and [rich-content/attachment](rich-content-extensions.md)
contracts. They never become another writable document or a replacement for CRDT
checkpoints, history, encryption policy or host authorization.

## Direction and fidelity profiles

Every capability record includes format/version, direction, enabled feature set,
tested target, input limits, fidelity tier, diagnostics and required optional
dependencies. `import` and `export` are independent claims. A recognizer or text
extractor must not advertise full document editing or round-trip fidelity.

| Profile | Import | Export | Qualified fidelity boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Existing baseline | Markdown, safe HTML, UTF-8 text, versioned semantic JSON | Same named formats | Existing semantic/source rules; snapshots do not retain collaborative history |
| DOCX | Supported paragraphs/runs/styles, lists, bounded tables and admitted media | Supported editor semantics and embedded admitted assets | Semantic subset; no Word pagination, arbitrary style/theme or package-byte round-trip promise |
| PDF publication | Rejected: export-only | Paginated PDF with selectable/shaped text, admitted assets, links and semantic tags where qualified | Visual publication artifact; generated output is not the original authoring source |
| ODT | Supported text/marks/lists/tables/assets | Same declared semantic subset | Unsupported styles, fields, layouts and encrypted packages are explicit |
| RTF | Bounded supported text/format/table subset | Same declared semantic subset | Code-page/control-word policy; no OLE, embedded application or arbitrary layout fidelity |
| EPUB | Ordered supported chapters and sanitized content/assets | Reflowable publication with navigation/metadata | No scripts, remote-resource fetch, fixed-layout or DRM fidelity claim |
| CSV/TSV | One bounded table using an explicit dialect | One chosen table using an explicit dialect | Cell text only; no workbook, formula evaluation, rich marks or type-inference claim |

Legacy binary DOC/PPT/XLS, presentation/workbook fidelity, arbitrary Office
macros, PDF forms/signatures, fixed-layout EPUB and unrestricted converter support
are outside the initial qualified profile. A future isolated local converter may
add individually tested capabilities. No generic “all formats” promise or silent
cloud fallback is permitted. Unsupported content yields an actionable report and
retains the original input under host retention policy; discarding it requires an
explicit lossy action.

## Adapter and execution boundary

Keep the minimum engine/WASM bundle unchanged. A lightweight capability registry
and prepared-batch contract may be shared; ZIP/XML codecs, layout engines, PDF
libraries and fonts load only through optional worker/native
conversion subsystems. Format feature flags, browser assets and native dependencies
are independently measurable. The app advertises unavailable adapters honestly;
opening a private file never uploads it or downloads document-selected code/fonts.

A conversion request fixes input identity/hash, direction/profile, resource
budget, output representation and relative insertion target or export revision.
Preparation cannot mutate the live replica. On import, revalidate target/capability
and commit through the shared session API once; cancellation, stale anchors,
rejected diagnostics and failed asset preparation leave the live document intact.
Export works from the captured revision and labels it; later edits cannot produce
a mixed-revision artifact. Re-import creates an explicit new session or prepared
insertion, never silently overwrites live CRDT identity/history.

Use the attachment service for staged embedded assets, hashes, authorization,
encryption and cleanup. A failed import removes only its uncommitted temporary
assets. Remote relationships, images, templates, fonts and hyperlinks remain
unfetched unless a separate explicit host-authorized operation allows access.
Password-protected inputs return a typed locked/unsupported result; any supported
unlock uses an explicitly provided secret held outside logs, URIs and documents.

Browser workers and isolated native jobs have bounded input/output bytes, active
jobs, wall time, memory where enforceable, decoded pixels, pages/nodes and nesting.
Cancellation disposes the worker/job and staged buffers. Native converters receive
only approved input/assets and output destinations, with no arbitrary filesystem
or network access. A missing required isolation/resource capability is a typed
unavailable profile, not permission to run unrestricted. Platform-specific wiring
and native/TUI integration belong to roadmaps 31–36; final ecosystem qualification belongs to roadmap 37.

## Hostile containers and documents

DOCX/ODT/EPUB ingestion validates signatures, package part names, relationships
and declared types before mapping content. Bound entry count, per-entry and total
**actual decompressed** bytes, compression ratio, XML depth/attributes/text and
decoded media dimensions; archive headers alone do not establish safe size.
Reject traversal, absolute/duplicate/conflicting paths, unexpected encryption and
symlink extraction. Prefer bounded in-memory part access; do not extract arbitrary
archive paths. Reject DTD/external-entity resolution, malformed encodings and
unapproved nested packages. Never execute macros, OLE objects, active content or
HTML import fragments from a document. Unsupported features have diagnostics.

PDF is export-only by user decision. Every PDF import request returns a clear
`FORMAT_EXPORT_ONLY` result before any converter, page renderer or semantic
mutation; filename, MIME and bounded content-signature checks must not route a
PDF renamed as another format into an importer. Do not add PDF text extraction,
tagged-PDF import or scanned-document recognition as a fallback. Generic file
attachment behavior, if supported by the host, remains separate from editable
content import.

PDF export jobs receive captured semantic content and authorized local assets,
not a source PDF. Bound layout time, pages, fonts, decoded images and output
allocation. Escape text and use trusted layouts rather than evaluating
user-supplied templates/scripts. Font/resource lookup is allowlisted; no
arbitrary filesystem or external fetch is permitted. Signatures/authenticity of
an imported authoring document are not transferred to a newly generated PDF.

CSV/TSV ingestion specifies delimiter, quote/escape, encoding, line endings and
ragged-row policy; it never executes formulas. Export discloses text/type loss and
offers an explicit spreadsheet-safe policy for formula-like cells without silently
changing the exact-data profile. EPUB content is sanitized through the existing
semantic HTML importer, not rendered as an active hidden webpage.

## Candidate and licensing gates

No candidate is approved or pinned by this document. Before adding a dependency,
verify the exact release, official API, target/toolchain support, license and
transitive/native/font/data notices, feature flags, known security advisories,
offline operation and representative compile/resource results. Record rejected
candidates. Never replace a bounded Rust adapter with a hosted conversion service.

- `docx-rs` is a Rust/WASM read/write candidate with MIT licensing and explicitly
  non-exhaustive OOXML support. Its default image previews decode/re-encode images;
  disable them when original admitted bytes suffice. These are library features,
  not proof of edit.ac fidelity. [Official repository](https://github.com/bokuweb/docx-rs)
- PDF export needs a layout engine or a deliberately limited layout policy.
  `krilla` is MIT/Apache-2.0 and offers PDF graphics/text/tagging primitives but
  explicitly excludes document layout, tables and pagination. Typst is an
  Apache-2.0 typesetting candidate; its PDF exporter supports tagging and declared
  conformance modes. Preserve semantic input and validate actual outputs rather
  than inferring PDF/UA compliance from the library choice.
  [krilla](https://github.com/LaurenzV/krilla), [Typst licensing](https://github.com/typst/typst/blob/main/Cargo.toml),
  [Typst PDF export](https://typst.app/docs/reference/pdf/)

## Qualification and truthful output

Hand-authored fixtures cover semantic content, unknown features, Unicode/shaping,
styles/tables/assets, malformed inputs, container bombs, cancellation and recovery.
Import acceptance compares supported semantic projections and complete diagnostics;
export acceptance uses independent readers and rendered-page inspection where
layout matters. ZIP/PDF byte identity is not a semantic round-trip oracle. PDF validation concerns generated artifacts only; it does not add a PDF import feature.

Measure complete cold/warm conversion: optional asset transfer/loading, inflate,
parse, mapping, font/image work, prepared-batch commit, peak memory and output size.
Keep imports off the edit hot path; never run export on each keystroke. Report
measured limits per target and preserve failed/skipped cases. Native adapter wiring,
real viewer/OS checks and release support claims remain gated by the platform tracks 31–36 and final qualification in roadmap 37.
Local prepared fixtures and mocked host transports suffice for automated checks;
private user documents, live credentials and paid models are not test fixtures.

## Format references

[ECMA-376 OOXML](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/)
defines the DOCX package vocabulary; [ZIP path-safety API](https://docs.rs/zip/latest/zip/read/struct.ZipFile.html#method.enclosed_name)
documents why archive names cannot be written directly. PDF output tagging and
accessibility must be checked against generated content and its declared
semantics, as explained by the [Typst accessibility guide](https://typst.app/docs/guides/accessibility/).
This is an export quality requirement, not a PDF reader/import contract.

Secondary adapters name their supported subsets against
[OpenDocument 1.3 packages](https://docs.oasis-open.org/office/OpenDocument/v1.3/OpenDocument-v1.3-part2-packages.html),
[EPUB 3.3](https://www.w3.org/TR/epub-33/) and
[CSV RFC 4180](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc4180/).
TSV and RTF dialect/encoding behavior must be explicitly pinned by their adapter
selection tasks; a filename extension is not a complete format contract.

specs/tui-client.md.text:
# Native terminal editor client

Status: development contract; the terminal UI is planned, not implemented by the scaffold.

The Rust `editac` client gains a built-in terminal UI using the same document
sessions, commands, source reconciliation and persistence as its external-editor
mode. The terminal UI is a presenter over those services. It does not maintain a
second authoritative document and does not require an MCP connection to edit.
The [CLI contract](cli.md), [shared client contracts](client-contracts.md) and
[change/diff contract](change-diffs.md) own their respective behavior.

## Targets and opening

The intended entry point is `editac tui <target>`, preserving existing CLI
commands. Targets include local Markdown files, explicit literal UTF-8 files,
authorized hosted URLs supported by configured adapters, and `ac://DOC_ID`
references as specified by the shared URI contract. Missing files require an
explicit creation action. The local catalog resolves document identities before
optional service discovery; an existing cached document opens offline. An
uncached remote identity gives an unavailable result without creating an empty
replacement. Local file editing never uploads content merely because an online
profile is configured.

An `ac://` reference identifies a mutable document. It is neither a bearer
credential nor a promise of immutable content hashes. An authority profile is
configuration for an authorized host adapter; neither a URI nor an arbitrary
web-page URL grants read or write authority. The adapter supplies authorization,
document/epoch/schema identity and receipt capabilities. Do not reinterpret
unrecognized HTTP pages as editable hosted documents or put credentials in
references, document buffers, terminal output or diagnostic artifacts.

## Interaction and terminal ownership

Use a maintained Rust terminal backend only after a bounded decision records its
official documentation, exact versions, compiler requirements, platform support,
license, input/PTY behavior and compatibility with the pinned workspace. The
choice is uncommitted until that task passes. Reuse the selected backend's event
and drawing primitives; implement product session behavior in this repository.

The first interface contains a source buffer, selection/caret, target and save
status, command/help surface and optional change/conflict view. Support keyboard
navigation, multiline editing, bracketed paste, resize and clear focus ownership.
Decode terminal input separately from engine offsets: screen columns, Unicode
scalar values, grapheme clusters, source byte offsets and UTF-16 units are not
interchangeable. Combining characters, emoji/ZWJ, wide characters, tabs, CRLF,
zero-width content and bidirectional source need explicit rendering/caret rules.
Rendering must not emit untrusted document text as terminal control sequences.

Plain-text editing keeps text literal. Markdown editing retains the user's source
spelling and uses the shared prepared source-reconciliation API. No-op commits
preserve source bytes. Unsupported module content remains recoverable and is
displayed with an honest source/opaque fallback; viewing a fallback does not
authorize destructive normalization. Unknown data cannot disappear during copy,
save, diff, undo or reconnect.

## Prepared changes, history and review

Each editable buffer names its opening revision, exact source/projection and
identity/anchor mapping. On commit, prepare and validate changes through the
shared session API before one semantic history group and its local persistence
barrier. Rejected preparation preserves the live replica and edited source.
Undo/redo uses the shared origin-aware history, including explicit grouping
boundaries; terminal key handling never mutates the document independently.

Change views consume the shared diff result and disclose whether the comparison
is local source bytes, a hosted Markdown projection or semantic data. Show base
and current revision labels, unchanged context, added/deleted ranges and any
opaque-content limitation. The view is a review surface, not a second patch
engine. Applying a reviewed edit revalidates its baseline; stale previews cannot
authorize writes. Read-only capability disables all mutation routes, including
paste, undo/redo and command shortcuts, while allowing copy/export according to
host permissions.

## Concurrent updates and recoverability

Remote structured updates apply to the existing shared replica. A clean source
buffer may refresh from the new projection while restoring mapped selection.
For a dirty buffer, retain opening source, local candidate and current remote
projection. Reconcile provably disjoint changes using the shared FMT-1.12
identity/anchor rules; never silently replace the user's draft or submit stale
whole-document text. Overlap, deleted targets, incompatible epoch and ambiguous
mapping open a bounded three-way conflict view. An explicit resolution becomes
a newly prepared change against current state, with another stale check before
commit. Keep unresolved drafts exportable and recoverable across exit/crash.

Display locally committed, pending upload, remotely committed, remote durability
unknown, conflict, authorization failure and incompatible-state results
separately. Network absence or revocation does not discard local work. Reuse the
native journal/checkpoint/outbox and actual receipt matching; no terminal-specific
saved flag may outrun those services.

Raw mode, alternate screen, cursor visibility, event tasks and adapter sessions
have one owner and idempotent teardown. Normal quit, failed startup, I/O error,
interrupt and supported suspend/resume paths restore the terminal. A flush
failure exposes recoverable unsaved work and an explicit exit choice; quitting
cannot imply remote durability. Forced termination is covered by journal/draft
recovery rather than a promise to run signal handlers in every circumstance.

## Qualification and artifacts

Use deterministic screen/event tests and PTY-driven packaged-client tests with
fixed dimensions, scripted keys, prepared engine updates and mocked host/auth/
receipt transports. Cover local Markdown/text, no-op, cancel, source preservation,
diff/read-only, undo/redo, dirty-buffer remote edits, three-way resolution, offline
restart, storage failure, resize and teardown. Test terminal-control injection and
Unicode position conversions without relying on network access or credentials.

Declare the actual terminal/OS capability matrix. PTY simulation proves only its
tested behavior; real terminal and accessibility support claims need their own
recorded evidence. Package the existing Rust client with immutable shared-engine
dependencies and executable help/examples. TUI delivery does not require an
MCP server, mobile SDK or desktop publication. Publishing and final cross-client
qualification follow their owning release track; no paid provider calls or
production document writes are automated checks.

specs/formats.md.text:
# Import, export and Markdown contract

Status: development contract; parser conformance and schema qualification are implementation gates.
Scope: semantic interchange, browser clipboard behavior and the [CLI's Markdown editing representation](cli.md).
The Rust implementation must remain reusable by CLI and future native adapters.

## Supported profile

The base grammar is CommonMark 0.31.2.
Name the extension profile `edit-ac-gfm-v1`; do not claim all GitHub behavior without evidence.
Its required extensions are task lists, strikethrough, basic rectangular tables and extended autolinks.
CommonMark links, images, fenced code and reference links belong to the declared base behavior.
The published GFM specification is version 0.29-gfm; record differences from the newer base grammar.
Pin official fixture versions and report pass/fail/unsupported outcomes per construct.
Document disabled syntax explicitly; optional math/reference syntax must not silently alter ordinary Markdown.
Raw HTML syntax is recognized as input but admitted only through the safe semantic import policy.
The parser does not define a plugin marketplace or execute document-supplied code.

## Parser qualification gate

Start with pulldown-cmark 0.13.4 as the candidate event parser.
Consume parse events into a prepared semantic batch; do not generate HTML just to parse it again.
Enable only the declared extension flags.
`ENABLE_GFM` is not a full-conformance switch: its documented feature is GitHub callout tags.
Qualify extended autolinks explicitly, including URL/email boundaries, punctuation and code exclusions.
The parser spike must compare actual fixture output to the complete required profile.
If a required feature fails, either add a bounded qualified extension or select another parser through an ADR.
Do not quietly rename missing syntax as supported or accept silent plain-text conversion.
Record whole-pipeline bytes, preparation time and memory, not parser throughput alone.
Parser selection blocks production Markdown import/export work, while fixture authoring can proceed independently.

## Semantic mapping

Map paragraphs, headings, marks, links, breaks, separators, lists, quotes and code to shared schema primitives.
Preserve code whitespace, list nesting/order, checked state, link destinations and alt text.
Map images/tables only through registered portable descriptors with explicit fallback behavior.
Do not split input into independent paragraph parses: references and block structure cross paragraph boundaries.
Maintain source ranges for diagnostics when the parser exposes them.
Unsupported constructs must retain recoverable source and report an actionable diagnostic.
Unknown atoms/marks retain namespaced type/version and validated data even without a renderer.
No Markdown export may silently erase unknown content to make a round-trip assertion pass.
Validate target schema and resource limits before committing any prepared import.

## Clipboard precedence

1. A valid supported edit-ac fragment with declared schema/version.
2. Explicit Markdown clipboard flavor or the user's paste-as-Markdown action.
3. Sanitized rich HTML admitted through the semantic importer.
4. Plain text processed under the host's declared Markdown-paste policy.

Malformed internal fragments fall back to the next safe available flavor with diagnostics.
An unsupported fragment version is not reinterpreted as a current internal structure.
The task-editor preset formats plain-text Markdown by default.
A minimal host chooses and documents its plain-text policy during configuration.
Provide an accessible literal/plain-text paste command; do not rely on undocumented heuristics or AI.
Pasting into a code block or inline-code editing context is literal under the declared target policy.
Only user paste/import actions parse Markdown; remote structured updates are never reparsed.

## Transaction and asynchronous paste behavior

Capture clipboard data and selection once; sanitize/parse/validate outside live mutation.
For ordinary pastes, commit one prepared semantic operation before showing the formatted result.
Insert-raw-then-reformat is not the ordinary paste implementation.
Add explicit history boundaries so one undo removes the complete paste and one redo restores it.
For oversized preparation, retain source data, stable target anchors and a cancellation token.
Record the initiating document/session; results cannot cross into a replaced editor/document.
Revalidate current target and schema before commit; stale/deleted targets produce a recoverable result.
Cancellation creates no content/history/persistence update.
Asynchronous completion must preserve the user's subsequent selection unless policy explicitly follows insertion.
Measure preparation, transfer and main-thread application separately; a worker does not make application free.

## HTML and URL safety

Use an allowlisted HTML-to-semantics importer distinct from Markdown parsing.
Drop executable elements/attributes and report unsupported content using safe source/text fallbacks.
Never admit script, event-handler attributes, embedded browsing contexts or executable URL schemes.
Validate link/image URLs after decoding and normalization; escaping output is not URL validation.
Specify permitted URL schemes and relative-URL resolution in the importer configuration/schema.
Images do not upload or fetch automatically during parsing; loading policy belongs to the host renderer.
Do not insert source HTML directly into the live document or hidden active page as an import shortcut.
Bound bytes, nesting, attribute lengths, table dimensions and prepared node count before commit.
Test malformed encodings, nested tags, misleading MIME flavors and adversarial link/image values.
Untrusted internal fragments follow the same safety/resource checks as external formats.

## Export and representability

Markdown export is deterministic semantic serialization, not recovery of the author's original spelling.
Specify escaping, fence length, list indentation, line endings and trailing newline once in fixtures.
Keep text/marks/nesting meaning and code whitespace stable through supported semantic round trips.
Underline has no standard CommonMark syntax; choose a declared safe HTML extension or explicit diagnostic/fallback.
For unsupported atoms, preserve an agreed text/source fallback and return diagnostics alongside output.
Do not claim a fallback exports an editable table, native math rendering or full-fidelity unknown content.
Versioned JSON export preserves semantic types/data without pretending to be collaborative history.
HTML export emits only the declared safe semantic vocabulary with escaped text/attributes.
Export requires an explicit request and never runs on each keystroke or save notification.

CLI source editing retains an exact source baseline and prepares semantic changes through the shared engine. Unchanged source must not be normalized or rewritten. Hosted document edits preserve unchanged semantic identities, anchors and unsupported data; replacing the document with a fresh Markdown import is not an editing/synchronization strategy. See the [CLI contract](cli.md) for source preservation, concurrent edit conflicts and literal-text mode. This does not change the deterministic semantic export contract or make Markdown a CRDT checkpoint.

## CRDT persistence and migration

Yjs/Yrs binary updates and checkpoints are the live collaborative persistence format.
JSON/Markdown/HTML snapshots are interchange content, not substitutes for CRDT identity/history.
Importing a snapshot into a fresh replica creates a new explicit session/epoch.
Do not merge stale offline updates from the old identity space into the new session.
Tiptap JSON migration covers a named supported node/mark set with fixture-by-fixture reporting.
Do not claim ProseMirror/Tiptap collaborative schema or plugin compatibility.
Migration preserves original input and emits diagnostics for every unsupported construct.
Existing documents are restored once; network delay must not cause repeated initialization/import.
A future container format is outside this release and must not block ordinary export/recovery.

## Required qualification fixtures

- CommonMark official examples plus the named extension corpus and documented deviations.
- Nested fences, code spans, escapes, reference links, nested lists and task states.
- Extended autolinks, tables, images, raw HTML and unknown module data.
- Unicode/RTL, empty documents, long single paragraphs and deeply nested content.
- Fragment/version corruption and each clipboard precedence/fallback branch.
- Paste/undo/redo with concurrent edits and target deletion during asynchronous preparation.
- Semantic parse/export/parse stability without requiring byte-for-byte source spelling.
- Sanitization/resource limits, rejected commands and canceled work leaving the core unchanged.
- Equivalent Rust and WASM fixture results; native bindings reuse the same corpus later.

Record failures, skips and diagnostics. Fixtures establish the supported profile; marketing names do not.

## Primary references

- [CommonMark 0.31.2](https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/)
- [GFM 0.29-gfm](https://github.github.com/gfm/)
- [pulldown-cmark event parser](https://docs.rs/pulldown-cmark/latest/pulldown_cmark/)
- [pulldown-cmark option semantics](https://docs.rs/pulldown-cmark/0.13.4/pulldown_cmark/struct.Options.html)

## Optional broad-format services

[Document conversion](document-conversion.md) defines independent DOCX/ODT/RTF/EPUB/CSV/TSV import and export profiles alongside the baseline formats. PDF is **export-only** by explicit user decision; reject PDF imports, and do not add PDF-reader/OCR dependencies. Converters return bounded prepared edits or output artifacts with fidelity reports; they do not replace source reconciliation or CRDT storage.

## Interaction regression coverage

Use [editor interactions](editor-interactions.md) for literal-paste newline/whitespace policy, typing-rule eligibility and reversal, alternate formatting and clipboard command behavior. The [case catalog](../tests/editor-interaction-cases.md) separates pasted Markdown, literal text, imported HTML and local typing; INT-1.10/INT-1.11 own integrated regressions alongside the existing parser conformance fixtures. Markdown source soft breaks and CLI source preservation remain governed by this format contract, not by the browser's literal-paste presentation policy.

specs/editor-interactions.md.text:
# Everyday editing behavior

Status: development contract; behavior is unimplemented until the owning task and its evidence pass.
Scope: the default rich editor, with explicit code, list, table and literal-text contexts. Hosts may publish named keyboard profiles; silent platform-dependent content semantics are unsupported.

The [research](../evidence/editor-interaction-research.md) records primary documentation and historical regressions. The [case catalog](../tests/editor-interaction-cases.md) supplies stable IDs and expected outcomes. [Track 38](../roadmaps/38-editor-interactions.md) owns implementation and regression qualification after the baseline tracks; it is a browser release prerequisite. Existing engine, browser and format contracts remain authoritative for schema, transactions, event reconciliation and parsing. If a behavior needs an unqualified primitive, record the engine/schema dependency and qualify it before implementing that behavior; a DOM-only workaround cannot satisfy it.

## State and command ownership

Rust owns text, marks, blocks, structural changes and semantic undo. Browser/native controls own temporary composition, layout-dependent caret movement and OS input integration. Public offsets remain UTF-16; user-facing character deletion uses qualified grapheme boundaries. An edit includes its resulting selection: assert anchor, focus, direction and affinity as well as content. Cursor movement alone produces no content/history/persistence update.

One user intent commits once, regardless of whether it arrives as keydown, beforeinput, input, composition or an observer notification. Route keyboard, toolbar, menu, touch and assistive actions to the same applicability-checked command. Consume an event only when the editor handles it; preserve platform shortcuts, AltGraph, dead keys and composing Enter. Resolve conflicts in order: active composition/OS input, active popup, context-specific command, editor command, native navigation/focus. Read-only policy applies at the command boundary as well as the UI.

Expanded selections use stable endpoints, including backward selections. A toolbar must capture selection before focus moves, revalidate it at activation, and return focus predictably. Asynchronous actions carry session identity, cancellation and relative anchors; a deleted target returns a recoverable result. Never redirect an old action to the current caret.

## Enter and line breaks

| Context | Enter | Shift+Enter |
|---|---|---|
| Paragraph | Split at selection into sibling paragraphs; caret at new start | Insert a semantic hard break inside the same block |
| Heading | Split in the middle retaining heading level; at the end create a paragraph; an empty heading becomes a paragraph | Hard break inside the heading |
| Nonempty list item | Split item and continue list; new task item is unchecked | Hard break inside the item's text, without creating another item |
| Empty list item | Outdent one level; at outer level exit to paragraph | Insert an in-item hard break |
| Quote | Split a nonempty quoted paragraph; empty final quoted paragraph exits one quote level | Hard break in the quoted paragraph |
| Code block | Insert literal LF; do not create another block | Insert literal LF |
| Table cell | Insert an in-cell hard break; do not split the table | Insert an in-cell hard break |

Selected text is replaced before the above action in the same transaction. A cross-block replacement retains unselected prefixes/suffixes under the engine's prepared structural policy. A hard break is distinct from a new paragraph and a Markdown source soft break; its wire/storage representation must pass schema admission and round-trip tests. Repeated/trailing hard breaks and the caret after the last break must survive rendering, copy, export and restore. Renderer filler nodes are never document content. Portable marks continue across a hard break where applicable; inline code is literal and link-boundary behavior follows the formatting policy below.

## Formatting and alternative representations

Selected formatting transforms exactly the selected semantic text, including backward and multi-block ranges; it preserves selection direction, unrelated marks and surrounding content. Applying a toggle to a mixed selection applies the mark uniformly; toggling a uniformly marked range removes it. Toolbar state is on/off/mixed/disabled rather than inferred from a single DOM ancestor.

A collapsed mark toggle changes local pending typing marks without inserting empty spans or a document/history transaction. Moving to another selection recomputes pending marks; typing applies them once. Bold/italic/strike survive hard breaks and remain pending for immediate typing after ordinary Enter where the destination permits them. An empty destination does not persist these pending marks as content: moving away and returning recomputes marks from that destination. Structural splits filter inherited pending marks by the destination block's allowed marks. At the end of a link, ordinary continued typing defaults outside the link; typing inside a link retains it. Inline code suppresses Markdown shortcuts and incompatible marks. Clear-formatting removes supported presentational inline marks, preserves text and links, and leaves block kind unchanged; removing a link is a separate command. Unsupported/custom marks are preserved unless the named command explicitly targets them.

Formatting actions, including links, colors and future underline/highlight/subscript/superscript, must declare schema capability, applicability, serialization and fallback. Disabled features are not approximated with Unicode lookalikes. Grammar-equivalent CommonMark spellings (eligible emphasis delimiters, backtick/tilde block fences, ATX/setext headings at supported levels, and equivalent list delimiters) import to equivalent supported semantics; inline code and fenced code blocks remain different structures; serialization may use canonical spelling. Underline, color and other non-Markdown semantics require a documented preservation format or an explicit loss diagnostic. Locale casing, Unicode normalization, smart punctuation and emoji substitution are not implicit formatting.

## Deletion, navigation and tabs

Backspace/Delete remove the selection or one qualified user-perceived character backward/forward. Cover combining sequences, variation selectors, emoji modifiers, ZWJ families, flags, CRLF import and Indic clusters. No operation leaves a half surrogate. Word/line deletion uses the platform profile; do not implement it as repeated UTF-16 deletion. At a block boundary, structural join/outdent/exit follows applicability and preserves marks; at the document boundary it is a no-op. A noneditable atom adjacent to a collapsed caret is selected first, then deleted on the next deletion; a selection already containing it deletes it once. Unsupported joins reject without partial mutation.

Retain native visual navigation when it is correct: arrows, Shift+arrows, Home/End, PageUp/PageDown, platform word/line/document modifiers, Select All and selection collapse. Test wrapped lines, vertical movement's preferred x position, RTL/bidi visual order, empty blocks, atoms and scroll-to-caret. Logical storage order does not define visual left/right. Keyboard shortcuts use semantic keys and platform conventions, not US physical-key assumptions. Browser find, zoom, navigation and OS/screen-reader commands remain available. Escape closes the highest active editor popup, then returns to ordinary editing without deleting text.

Tab in ordinary prose moves focus; Shift+Tab moves backward. Lists indent/outdent only when a structural action is applicable. Code Tab inserts one literal tab at a collapsed caret; a selection indents touched lines by one tab and Shift+Tab removes at most one leading tab or the configured indentation width. Existing whitespace is preserved. Table Tab/Shift+Tab moves among cells; forward Tab at the final editable cell creates one bounded row if allowed, otherwise exits; Shift+Tab at the first cell exits. Code/list/table profiles expose visible keyboard help and a one-shot focus escape: Escape dismisses the active editor popup if present and arms the next Tab/Shift+Tab to leave the editor forward/backward. Any other edit/navigation clears that escape state. IME-owned Escape is not intercepted. No exit route requires a mouse. Switching focus or opening menus must not strand composition.

The default shortcut profile uses `Primary` = Command on macOS and Control on Windows/Linux. Bind only while the relevant editor control owns focus and an applicable command exists; hosts may remap explicitly and expose the mapping in keyboard help.

| Keys/action | Required dispatch |
|---|---|
| Primary+B / Primary+I / Primary+K | Bold, italic and link editor using captured semantic selection |
| Primary+Z / Primary+Shift+Z; Windows Control+Y | Semantic undo/redo; deduplicate browser history input events |
| Primary+A / C / X / V | Scoped Select All and native clipboard operations with the declared import policy |
| Platform plain-text paste shortcut | Same operation as visible Paste as plain text; unsupported shortcut still has command access |
| Primary+U and other optional formatting bindings | Consume only when the registered formatting capability and profile support that binding; expose disabled reason through controls |
| Primary+Enter, Escape and host submit bindings | A host explicitly configures submit behavior; ordinary Enter never implicitly submits. IME/popup ownership is resolved first |

Qualify macOS Option+arrows/Backspace (word), Command+Left/Right/Up/Down (line/document), and Windows/Linux Control+arrows/Backspace, Home/End and Control+Home/End under each platform's actual profile. Shift extends the corresponding range. Platform/screen-reader remapping takes precedence over an assumed universal key table.

## Input, whitespace and Unicode

Use observed input events and target ranges, not the assumption that all edits produce keydown. Reconcile noncancelable/missing beforeinput through input/DOM fallback. Dictation, autocorrection, spelling replacement, handwriting and virtual keyboards may insert or replace arbitrary ranges. Do not invent an `insertFromDictation` inputType or infer microphone state from text events. Defer composing/commit Enter to the OS/IME before editor split/menu actions. Account for observed sequences where compositionend occurs before the final Enter or isComposing is already false; use the qualified composition-session state and narrowly bounded event correlation, not a blanket time-based swallowing of the next deliberate Enter. The desired intermediate composition model is temporary; commit/cancel/undo policy must be fixed in the qualified input ADR before adapter implementation. The ADR is a required development output, not assumed existing evidence; any platform exception updates its fixtures and acceptance together.

Preserve typed leading/trailing/repeated U+0020 spaces, tabs, NBSP, narrow NBSP and user-supplied zero-width/bidi characters. Layout filler spaces and placeholder breaks must be distinguishable from authored content. Literal import normalizes CRLF/CR to LF once; it does not trim, collapse whitespace, normalize Unicode, expand tabs or apply Markdown. Preserve precomposed and decomposed text byte/code-point distinctions where the format permits. Offer optional visible-invisibles diagnostics without rewriting the content. Reject malformed encoding or unsupported controls using explicit diagnostics; preserve recoverable source. Keyboard modifier handling must allow Hungarian accented letters, AltGraph punctuation, dead keys and non-Latin layouts.

## Slash commands

Open only from a local, noncomposing typed slash at a valid text boundary (start of block or after whitespace), with a collapsed selection and no literal/code/link-target context. A URL/path slash, escaped slash, pasted slash, imported content and remote updates do not auto-open it. Preserve the literal query until a command actually succeeds.

Arrow Up/Down moves among enabled results; Home/End moves to first/last result while the popup owns those keys. Enter commits exactly once; Shift+Enter closes the popup and inserts a same-block hard break. Tab dismisses and follows normal focus/context policy; it does not silently accept a suggestion. Escape dismisses with query intact and does not immediately reopen. Backspace filters the query and deleting the trigger closes it. Enter with no results or all-disabled results is consumed by the active popup without mutation; it must not fall through to paragraph splitting. Pointer and keyboard selection execute the same command and restore its resulting caret.

Use an anchored trigger/query range, cancel outdated lookups, and recheck the current query/session before accepting a response. Caret movement outside the range, incompatible selection, read-only transition, focus leaving the editor/popup composite and destruction dismiss the popup. Internal pointerdown → editor blur → item activation and assistive focus transitions must preserve the anchored command until activation or explicit cancellation; do not cancel an item click merely because the editor blurred. Only a successful command replaces its own trigger/query range in one undo group. Async errors preserve the user's query. The presenter must name its control, expose active/disabled result state and announce bounded result changes; choose the appropriate listbox/combobox or menu pattern and qualify it with actual assistive technology rather than mixing incompatible ARIA roles.

## Clipboard and parsing

Keep the precedence and explicit host Markdown-paste policy in [formats.md](formats.md). Paste-as-plain-text is a discoverable command usable without a platform-specific shortcut. Capture data/range once and commit once; permission denial, cancellation, parse failure and stale anchors preserve the original document. Cut modifies content only after a successful clipboard operation under the supported browser path. Cross-block cut/paste restores text, supported marks, breaks and selection with one undo.

Fixtures include same-editor fragments; unsupported/malformed fragments; HTML from Word/Google Docs/Apple Notes; plain text from terminals/PDF extraction; Markdown; TSV tables; URL/email punctuation; code; and nested lists. Store sanitized synthetic payloads with provenance, never private clipboard captures. Compare semantic fidelity and explicit fallback, not proprietary source markup. Multi-line literal paste maps LF to hard breaks within a text block and to LF in code; table-cell literal paste stays in the target cell. Formatted/Markdown import determines paragraph/list structure through the parser. Inline-code paste retains literal characters and uses the schema's declared multiline fallback with a diagnostic if multiline code spans cannot be represented.

Typing shortcuts are a finite local rule set with exact triggers and context exclusions. Slash auto-open and typing rules require positively identified eligible direct typing from a qualified event sequence. Input with ambiguous provenance, including identical insertText without a correlated eligible typing/composition-commit policy, remains literal; visible commands stay available on keyboards/platforms that cannot safely establish eligibility. Never infer dictation identity from a fabricated source flag. They run after committed local text, never during IME, paste, dictation/replacement or remote replay. Escape, literal mode and code contexts preserve delimiter text. Backspace immediately after an automatic conversion reverses that conversion according to a recorded input-rule history boundary; normal undo then reverses the preceding typing. Partial syntax, unmatched delimiters and invalid links remain literal. Rules and paste parsing have separate switches.

## Acceptance and extension boundary

The case catalog is a minimum regression set, not a claim to enumerate every browser/OS interaction.
