Each case asserts document state, caret/selection, history behavior and emitted mutation count; rejected/canceled/navigation actions assert zero mutations. Pair high-risk cases with read-only, remote edits, empty/end positions and undo. Record exact engine/browser/OS/locale and fixture revisions. Preserve failures and explicit unsupported cases.

Baseline keyboard access, screen-reader editing and native dictation belong to the editor with no extension enabled. The [assistive-input extension](assistive-input.md) adds host-controlled status, discoverable commands and optional assistance UI; it cannot repair missing baseline semantics by maintaining another text model. Real OS/screen-reader/voice checks qualify support separately from deterministic event replays. [Track 39](../roadmaps/39-assistive-input.md) owns optional extension integration and its evidence.

## Mobile browser profiles

For touch selection, software keyboards without modifier keys, browser viewport/occlusion and platform APIs, apply [mobile web](mobile-web.md) and the [mobile case catalog](../tests/mobile-web-cases.md). Track 40 builds on the semantics here without changing the Rust character/selection model. Explicit touch controls keep commands reachable when conservative input provenance suppresses automatic shortcuts.

## Regression prevention and shared suite

[The editing suite](editing-regression-suite.md) defines guards for atomic compound edits, intent correlation, semantic selection results, history origins and post-transaction callbacks. Pending marks distinguish context-derived state (null) from explicit no marks (empty set); selected formatting is not a persisted default for an empty block. Use the shared real-engine driver and independently authored snapshots from track 42. Catalog references and valid fixture files are planned coverage, not runtime passes.

specs/storage-sync.md.text:
# Storage and synchronization contract

The engine emits immutable update bytes and document/epoch/schema/origin metadata. Browser and native CLI storage/transport adapters consume these independently. Baseline versions and wire layout are frozen by the foundation protocol task, using the [engine contract](engine.md). The [CLI contract](cli.md) defines filesystem durability, Markdown working buffers and hosted target resolution; browser-specific storage mechanisms are not native filesystem guarantees.

## Local durability

Journal key: document ID, epoch, writer ID and monotonic per-writer sequence. Store immutable update bytes, checksum, schema version and pending receipt identity. Generate distinct live CRDT client IDs and writer IDs for simultaneous tabs. Restoring document bytes never restores a shared active client identity.

`localCommitted(updateId)` means the transaction containing that update completed. Queueing, creating a request and scheduling a timer are insufficient. Request strict durability where supported and report actual capability. The guarantee covers tested process crashes; browser eviction, user deletion and arbitrary hardware/power failures remain outside it. No unload-handler dependency.

A checkpoint consists of CRDT state, coverage metadata and hash. Publish checkpoint/coverage atomically. Keep the previous valid point and a recoverable tail until replacement is safely published. A checkpoint may cover unacknowledged local updates, but the outbox must still retain their identities and retransmittable bytes. JSON export is never used as a checkpoint that silently changes CRDT identity.

`flush({target:'local'})` captures the pending set and resolves once all those updates complete storage; later updates need not extend the barrier. A failed transaction rejects the barrier, clears saved status and exposes a recoverable error. Keep in-memory state/export available. Destroy policy explicitly flushes or reports unsaved state; destruction must not imply saving.

Use deterministic failure injection before/after each write/transaction/publication boundary, plus actual browser process termination after acknowledgment. Test two tab writers, duplicate/reordered replay, corrupt latest checkpoint, quota/permission rejection, schema mismatch and missing document identity. Preserve failures in evidence.

## Network

Transport is optional and attaches to the existing engine. It must not reinitialize the document, import a second snapshot or replace selection/history on connection. Use transaction origins to avoid echo. Define bounded receive/send queues, frame sizes, retry/backoff and reconnection behavior. Defer unauthorized uploads but retain recoverable local edits.

Profile four independently versioned contracts: v1 update bytes, baseline sync messages, awareness messages, and edit.ac document schema. The pinned JS fixture operates on the same schema. A Yrs handle is not a JS `Y.Doc`; use a direct wire adapter or an explicitly tested provider adapter. Yjs compatibility does not imply Tiptap/ProseMirror schema compatibility.

Awareness is ephemeral, expiring and throttled. It cannot advance document durability. Relative peer selections resolve against current state and fail safely when targets disappear. Presence remains optional and is never journaled as document state.

## Durable receipts

`remoteCommitted(updateId)` requires an explicit negotiated application receipt, emitted after the service's durable storage commit. A synced event, state vector or socket delivery does not meet this contract. Receipt identity includes document, epoch, writer/sequence and content identity; wrong identity cannot prune the outbox. Receipt capability absence means remote durability is unknown.

The local reference service is integration infrastructure: loopback by default, prepared auth fixtures, transactional storage, duplicate handling and restart recovery. Do not deploy it as a production service by implication. Host/service is responsible for authentication, authorization, rate limits and retention. Revocation leaves local work exportable and does not erase it.

Remote schema/epoch mismatch returns an explicit incompatibility state. Migrations use a declared new epoch and session transition; old offline updates cannot be silently applied after a rewrite. Checkpoint compaction retains reconnect identity according to the pinned protocol.

Sources: [IndexedDB durability](https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/), [Yjs updates](https://docs.yjs.dev/api/document-updates), [Yrs sync protocol](https://docs.rs/yrs/0.28.0/yrs/sync/protocol/trait.Protocol.html).

## Additional clients and protected profiles

[Client contracts](client-contracts.md) extend these ports to native/CLI sessions and explicit cross-tab/process delivery; sharing storage alone is not live synchronization. [Security profiles](security-encryption.md) can wrap local storage and transport while preserving acknowledgment identity. Ciphertext receipts certify stored bytes, not plaintext schema validation or endpoint authorization. Agent requests add durable request/result deduplication in the host/session boundary.

specs/schema-evolution.md.text:
# Engine ownership qualification beyond the foundation

Status: development requirements for ENG-1.17/1.18, not a frozen wire layout or passing interoperability claim.

## Authority and scope

[Schema v1](schema-v1.md) qualifies one fixed pair transforming only from `original`. [Block metadata v2](schema-v2.md) deliberately preserves that limitation while qualifying empty paragraph/heading state. Those receipts remain valid for their recorded bounds. Neither proves an editor can split/join arbitrary blocks repeatedly.

ENG-1.17 must select and specify an ownership representation for schema `editac.registry.structure.v3`, profile `editac.yrs-yjs.structure.v3`, using the same pinned libraries, protocol version 1, update encoding 1 and UTF-16 offsets. Its normative layout belongs in `schema-v3.md`, created by that task before the qualification tests. Keep the v2 block-tuple semantics and independent empty-block metadata. Do not mutate v1/v2 roots or describe an untested layout as frozen. Exact profile admission, separate epochs, preserved recovery and no automatic migration remain mandatory.

## Representation obligations

The selected layout must support newly allocated logical IDs rather than the reserved fixture aliases; disjoint pairs; multiple splits of the same live owner; joins after splits; splits after joins, including an owner containing spans from multiple original texts; empty spans; and retained block formatting. At least three sequential transformations must work without resetting/reseeding the document or inventing an unrelated operation when the current owner is unsupported.

Each original nested rich text keeps its integrated identity. Structural commands cannot implement these operations by deleting/reinserting or cloning original text. The specification must define exact roots/shared types/value shapes, owner IDs and allocation, span/relative-cut representation, operation or descriptor conflict ordering, placement, metadata inheritance, deletion/recovery and unsupported-input behavior. If operation history is used, define dependency ordering and treatment of incomplete/concurrent branches; if descriptors are used, define atomic replacement and overlapping ownership. Do not pick a policy from arrival order or independently merged descriptor fields.

Every retained character belongs to exactly one visible or explicitly recoverable span owner. Relative anchors remain attached to original text identities and resolve to the current owner or a typed deleted/unresolvable result. Concurrent edits at both sides of a cut, concurrent overlapping split/join choices and deleted targets must have a documented deterministic outcome. Losing structural intentions and their content remain recoverable; projections emit no repair writes. Bound decode, projection and command preparation resources, including malformed or adversarial operation graphs.

## Qualification boundary: ENG-1.17

Create a disposable but faithful Rust/Yjs fixture mapping under `core/fixtures/schema-v3/` and `core/crates/editac-core/tests/ownership_profile.rs`. It must build the exact proposed roots in both languages and prove the obligations above with seeded replicas, real binary updates, both exchange directions, duplicate/reordered permutations, checkpoint restore, stable identities/anchors, marks, heading/empty-block metadata, deletion and malformed input. Include two independent pairs with non-reserved IDs and at least three sequential transformations on one lineage. Compare semantic visible and recovery snapshots, not state-vector/byte agreement alone.

Record rejected alternatives, the selected layout and its remaining resource envelope in `architecture/evidence/engine-ownership-profile/`. A precise bounded split proposal is required if the selection/probe cannot fit a session; no narrowing to a fixed pair or omission of original requirements clears this gate. No production representation is approved until its exact descriptor, matching source hashes and nonzero zero-failure/zero-skip receipt exist.

## Command integration boundary: ENG-1.18

Use the qualified v3 mapping in document creation/restore, projection, anchors, prepared text/format edits and structural commands. Preserve legacy profile readers/tests and explicit unsupported-profile results; never merge schemas/epochs. The ENG-1.7 fixed-pair implementation remains bounded evidence, not a substitute for this integration.

Production split/join tests must repeat the complete beginning/middle/end/empty, Unicode, mark retention, remote insertion race and deleted-target acceptance using arbitrary pairs and repeated transformations, including split-after-join across original sources. Test mixed mark/block batches and inherited/overridden heading state on these owners. Rerun the v3 interoperability probe and relevant initialization/projection/anchor/text/format suites. Subsequent list/code/move/history/patch/WASM gates consume this qualified mapping; they cannot bypass it by using the foundation aliases.

specs/change-diffs.md.text:
# Exact change and revision views

Status: planned, roadmap 13. “Exact” identifies what is compared; it does not claim a unique diff algorithm or byte-preserving rich-text serialization.

## Three representations

1. **Source diff:** immutable original and edited UTF-8 bytes for a file/source session, including newline style, final newline and source spelling. Retain both hashes and explicit decode limits. Binary/invalid UTF-8 input returns a diagnostic.
2. **Projected Markdown diff:** deterministic serialized before/after rich documents, tagged with serializer/dialect versions. Show that serialization may normalize author spelling. Never label this the original source diff.
3. **Semantic diff:** stable node IDs, insertion/deletion/move, attributed text, marks, attributes and unknown/opaque content changes. Formatting, link targets and table structure remain visible even where Markdown cannot represent them.

CRDT binary update exchange is a fourth, internal transport representation; it is never substituted for these review views. Review can align text and semantic changes, but if alignment is ambiguous it must show separate views rather than fabricate correspondence.

## Immutable revisions and retention

Revision requests bind document/epoch/schema/module profile, observed-state token, representation type and hash. Store snapshots or reconstructable immutable history in a separate bounded HistoryStore. Capture named revisions/checkpoints on demand and materialize incremental history outside the typing path; do not serialize the entire document every keystroke.

A locally monotonic generation may label revisions but must be persisted and scoped; it is not a cross-replica total order. Deletion effects participate in exact revision validation. Availability after pruning, encryption key rotation or schema migration is explicit. Return unavailable/locked/incompatible for a missing revision, never approximate it from the current document. Yrs GC and UndoManager are not an archival history API.

## Patch contract

Pin deterministic line/word diff algorithms and options. A patch carries before/after hashes, representation/profile, limits and hunk ranges. Applying it to the exact baseline must yield byte-for-byte expected output and the expected hash. Wrong baseline, overlapping hunks, malformed lengths, missing context or output-limit violations fail without mutation. Git-like unified output is an interoperability format, not a promise that tie-breaking matches every Git version/options combination.

Use fixed `git diff --no-index` golden cases to validate conventional unified output; exit 1 means differences. Test repeated lines, CRLF/LF, missing final newline, Unicode/emoji/combining text, large replacements and moves. Text offsets exposed to the editor convert through UTF-16/anchor validation; terminal columns and UTF-8 bytes are distinct units.

Applying a reviewed hunk to a live collaborative document uses source reconciliation or stable semantic commands and current revision checks. It never patches serialized Markdown and re-imports the whole live document. “Accept all” means apply the validated proposal. Partial hunk application recomputes a valid semantic plan and rejects unsafe fragments (for example half a fenced block).

## Views and attribution

Provide accessible unified, inline and side-by-side web views; a portable changes model feeds native and terminal presenters. Readonly current, readonly historical and writable live modes are distinct. History checkout cannot rewind the live replica. “Restore this version” produces a new authorized edit against the current state with a preview and conflict result.

Show authenticated operation attribution only when supplied by a trusted host, otherwise mark it unknown/unverified. Separate human/agent/import/replay origins and semantic undo groups. A reconstructed snapshot diff says what differs, not necessarily who typed each character; concurrent history cannot be turned into a single causal narrative without evidence.

No-loss criteria cover content, marks, URLs, unknown modules, whitespace and structural identity. Bounded review history, source files and recovery artifacts inherit optional encryption/access policies. Logs do not contain confidential source by default.

Sources and implementation examples: [Yjs updates](https://docs.yjs.dev/api/document-updates), [Loro diff API](https://www.loro.dev/docs/api/js), [Git diff](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff), [research](../evidence/followup-research.md).

specs/cloud-document-store.md.text:
# Cloud document store and reference host

Status: planned delivery contract. No cloud service, provider, deployment, or durability claim is established by this document.

This companion service lets authorized clients locate documents, exchange durable updates, and store their assets. The Rust document/session contracts remain authoritative. A single deployable reference host lives in `core/services/document-store/`; provider adapters implement its ports. Keep catalog, update storage, authorization, relay, and asset modules in that host initially. Separate services require measured operational need, not an anticipated scale claim.

Entry gates are `06-synchronization.md`, `12-client-contracts.md`, and `25-rich-content-extensions.md`, including actual blob ports. Follow [storage-sync](storage-sync.md), [client-contracts](client-contracts.md), [rich-content-extensions](rich-content-extensions.md), and [security-encryption](security-encryption.md). The prepared-auth loopback relay from SYN-1.5 is a protocol fixture; it does not satisfy this service contract.

## Ownership and adapters

The reference host must run locally against a real durable transactional backend and immutable blob storage. CLD-1.1 selects and records the smallest maintained backend/library combination that meets the contract, verifies versions, license, migrations, and restart behavior, then creates the harness. This is an implementation dependency decision, not cloud-provider provisioning. In-memory and fault-injected adapters supplement the real backend; they cannot be the sole delivery evidence.

| Port | Owns | Required invariant |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `IdentityVerifier` / `AuthorizationPolicy` | Verified principals, tenant membership, document actions | Untrusted tenant/document selectors never grant access; current policy is checked at admission |
| `CatalogStore` | Tenant-scoped document identity, authority mapping, epoch, ACL references, lifecycle, catalog revision | Atomic conditional metadata changes; no CRDT payload in catalog records |
| `UpdateStore` | Immutable updates, operation ledger, checkpoints, coverage, publication records | Acknowledged content survives the backend's declared failure class |
| `BlobStore` | Staging, immutable versioned objects, byte integrity, finalized-object receipts | A published reference identifies verified immutable bytes; upload completion alone is insufficient |
| `CommitCoordinator` | Serialized publication of catalog changes, update identities, finalized blob references, request outcomes | One authoritative durable commit record; failed publication cannot emit success |
| `Relay` | Negotiated wire profile, bounded subscriptions, awareness, resume | Uses durable commits for replay; ephemeral presence never establishes durability |

Interfaces use owned buffers, explicit cancellation/deadlines, bounded pagination, typed retryability, document/tenant context, and capability declarations. Adapter errors preserve whether a commit was definitely rejected or its outcome is unknown. Drivers stay outside `editac-core`; provider SDK objects do not cross these ports. Ship one working adapter set first and reusable conformance tests for future sets.

## Identity, authorization, and control plane

Document identity is `(tenant_id, document_id, epoch)`. Catalog revisions and content revisions are separate values. Human titles, paths, aliases, and source locators are metadata, not identity; list/search results are scoped before pagination and counting. Catalog discovery, document reads/writes, asset downloads, upload intents, history, exports, and deletion each require authorization. Do not leak existence through another tenant's errors, counts, object keys, caches, queues, or metrics.

The deployable host needs a real credential-verification adapter. For a JWT adapter, pin allowed algorithms, trusted issuer/audience and key discovery policy; validate signatures, expiry and token purpose using maintained libraries. Prepared signed tokens and a local key fixture cover automated tests. Tenant membership and document roles remain server-authoritative and revocable; possession of a document ID or valid login token is insufficient. Trust proxy headers only from explicitly configured proxies. Never log tokens or place them in `ac://` locators.

Catalog mutations require an exact expected catalog revision, checked inside the same transaction as mutation and operation-ledger publication. Content preconditions use the CAP content revision and serialized admission boundary; a Yjs state vector does not detect every deletion. A rejected precondition returns a typed conflict and performs no mutation. HTTP `If-Match`, when exposed, maps a strong validator to the selected representation's exact server revision. An object-store ETag, modification timestamp, or upload checksum is not automatically a catalog/content revision or transaction fence. See [RFC 9110 validators and conditional requests](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#name-if-match).

## Durable publication and idempotency

An admitted operation binds verified actor, tenant/document/epoch, writer sequence or request ID, profile, input digest, expected revisions, and intended effects. Repeating the same key and input returns the same recorded outcome; the same key with different input rejects. Authorization is rechecked before an old result is disclosed. Deduplication retention and resume floors are advertised; expired operation keys reject or use an explicit reconciliation flow, never silently become a new mutation.

Document-update receipts and asset-finalization receipts remain distinct, matching RCH. Ordinary CRDT updates may describe local/queued assets; their receipt does not make those assets remotely available or block local editing. A document commit may refer to a pending descriptor, but only a finalized asset receipt may establish availability.

For an operation explicitly publishing available assets, first finalize immutable object versions and obtain backend evidence that their bytes meet the declared durability class. Then atomically publish catalog effects, update identities, finalized asset references, new revisions, and the operation outcome in the authoritative transactional store. That transaction is the logical commit boundary. Object stores generally cannot join it: staged/finalized unreferenced bytes may become recoverable orphans, but references must never point to unverified or mutable objects. The adapter must prevent overwrite/deletion of referenced versions under its qualified ownership and retention policy.

Only after commit confirmation may the host send a remote receipt or relay a committed publication. Bind receipts to tenant/document/epoch, immutable update identity/digest, operation and commit revision, profile, finalized asset receipt references where relevant, and the promised durability class. A combined publication manifest links these distinct receipts without merging their promises. A lost response permits idempotent recovery. An uncertain commit outcome requires ledger lookup before retry publication. No receipt follows enqueueing, socket send, cache acknowledgment, upload request success, or a transaction that later rolls back. Checkpoints and relay replay cannot expose an uncommitted predecessor.

`remoteCommitted` proves only the negotiated service/backend promise. Record process-crash, host-loss, replica-loss, and disaster-recovery guarantees separately with evidence; never infer them from a successful local transaction. Backup policy and receipt durability are related but distinct.

## Assets and resource limits

Use the actual RCH blob/attachment ports. Upload intents bind tenant, actor, document/epoch, size bound, expiry, allowed content handling, and an unguessable staging key. A provider may issue a narrowly scoped direct-upload capability; the reference host uses the same stage/finalize protocol. Do not expose credentials or accept arbitrary remote fetch URLs. Reserve quota atomically before upload; release or expire reservations safely.

Finalize verifies object existence, immutable version, measured length and integrity according to the selected profile; do not trust client declarations or confuse provider ETags with digests. Finalization is idempotent and reauthorizes the actor. Object keys and capabilities are tenant scoped. Failed checks leave no document reference. Only published attachments may be fetched through authorized download grants; failed, expired, and abandoned stages are reclaimed after the documented grace period. Serving user content uses safe disposition, media handling, and origin policy. Encrypted objects remain opaque; plaintext scanning cannot be claimed for them.

Bound frame size, decoded updates, uploads, documents, per-tenant bytes, connections, in-flight operations, subscription buffers and pagination. Quotas include reservations, journals, checkpoints, asset versions, exports, and retained backups where charged to a tenant. Durable usage accounting reconciles after crashes. Apply per-principal and per-tenant rate limits, fair scheduling and typed retry hints. A slow consumer reconnects from a durable resume cursor; an overflowing queue does not drop an acknowledged update or clear a client outbox.

## Relay, compaction, and document lifecycle

Each connection negotiates supported schema/wire/security profiles. Browser-origin validation complements authentication; every action checks document authority. Expiry, logout, membership changes, and tenant changes invalidate access during a long-lived connection. Bound handshake time and unauthenticated traffic. Relay updates come from the durable commit log; awareness remains ephemeral. The client retains pending writes until matching receipts.

Compaction publishes a verified checkpoint and exact coverage atomically, retaining the recovery tail and deduplication/resume evidence needed by declared offline windows. Peer state vectors alone are not permission to remove tombstones, replay barriers, or unpublished data. A peer below the supported resume floor receives an explicit resnapshot/reconciliation response preserving its unacknowledged local changes. Epoch migration has an explicit old-epoch admission policy; silent merge or reset is forbidden.

Lifecycle is explicit: active, tombstoned, retention-held, purge-eligible, purged. Tombstones/retired epochs prevent stale offline clients from resurrecting deleted documents. IDs are not recycled within the retained admission domain. A client facing deletion can export/recover its local draft through a new authorized document, never silently recreate the old one. Keep minimal rejection markers for the advertised offline window; if markers expire, require a new admission token/epoch so an old request cannot become creation.

Export captures an authorized, stable manifest revision with document bytes, catalog metadata appropriate to the caller, attachment versions and integrity metadata; pagination/retry does not mix revisions. Protected profiles export ciphertext unless an explicitly authorized endpoint owns keys. Retention holds, deletion deadlines, backups, legal/operator policy and restore restrictions are documented capabilities. Purge invalidates access immediately, then removes scoped data and unreferenced objects with resumable audit evidence. Historical backups may retain data until their stated expiry; a deletion ledger must prevent restore from republishing deleted content. Do not promise immediate physical erasure from third-party backups.

## Operations and qualification

Backup captures a mutually consistent catalog/journal/checkpoint/asset manifest and versioned configuration. Restore runs into an isolated destination, validates hashes and commit coverage, applies deletion/epoch barriers, and demonstrates that acknowledged operations and required assets remain usable. Never overwrite an active store to test restore. State recovery-point and recovery-time objectives separately from measured drill results. Include schema migration rollback/forward-recovery and failed partial restores.

The first deployment may be a single writer with fenced ownership and durable storage; the capability manifest must say so. Test restart, crash during commit, duplicate delivery, storage exhaustion, dependency timeout, stale writer, slow reader and lost receipt. If multiple hosts are supported, prove fencing/CAS and committed-log fanout under concurrent publication before enabling replicas; an in-process mutex cannot establish distributed exclusion. Scale limits come from deterministic local load fixtures and separately qualified provider evidence, not extrapolation.

Expose readiness/liveness, commit latency, queue depth, rejected admission, quota pressure, replay lag and recovery failures without document contents, tokens or unbounded identifier labels. Trace one operation across upload/finalize/commit/receipt using a non-secret correlation ID. Define alert thresholds, drain/shutdown behavior and a small operator runbook.

Package one runnable service, migrations, example non-secret configuration, capability manifest, and a local consumer example. A versioned deployment manifest binds build digest, adapter versions, schema/profile support, trusted identity issuers, allowed origins, limits, retention and secret references. Verify its signature against an operator-established trust root before startup; disallow silent override/downgrade. Plan key rotation and emergency rollback explicitly. Secret values live in the deployment's secret facility, not signed public files or test fixtures. Development unsigned mode is explicit, loopback-only, and cannot report deployment-qualified status.

Evidence levels must remain distinct:

1. **Reference-ready:** real local backend, reusable adapter contracts, restart/fault tests, packaged consumer and restore drill pass at recorded revisions. Mocked transports and prepared identities are labeled.
2. **Configured-provider qualified:** separately authorized testing of the exact selected backend, credentials/roles, region, consistency settings, encryption/retention, signed config and deployment topology proves the same contracts and failure guarantees. Local emulators cannot establish this claim. No provider is selected or provisioned by this roadmap preparation.
3. **Public deployment approved:** operator-owned service, budget, data policy, monitoring, rollback and qualified artifacts are reviewed in the final release gate. Provisioning and publication need their concrete delivery scope; this roadmap does not incur charges.

Opaque envelope storage/transport is a compatibility requirement, not E2EE qualification. Baseline CLD work may use prepared opaque bytes and must reject unsupported profile IDs. Actual protected clients/server combinations require tracks19/24 plus the final server/profile release gate; key custody, membership, metadata leakage and authorized plaintext endpoints remain governed by their security contracts.

## Primary guidance checked

- [OWASP authorization](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.html) and [multi-tenant security](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Multi_Tenant_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html) support per-action authorization and server-verified tenant context. They do not certify an adapter.
- [OWASP WebSocket security](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/WebSocket_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html) covers origin checks, session expiry and per-message authority for long-lived connections.
- [JWT best current practices, RFC 8725](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8725.html) informs issuer/audience/algorithm verification; it does not supply tenant membership policy.
- [HTTP semantics, RFC 9110](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html) distinguishes representation validators and conditional requests. Storage transactions and crash durability remain adapter obligations.

specs/packages-release.md.text:
# Packages, repositories and release contract

## Canonical ownership

| Repository | Contents | Distribution |
|---|---|---|
| `edit-ac/core` | Rust crates, WASM, browser SDK, React integration, fixtures and native probes | npm SDKs; Rust crates later if useful |
| `edit-ac/architecture` | Contracts, roadmaps and evidence | Documentation; private npm tooling package only |
| `edit-ac/docs` | Public guides, generated references and release-backed demo consumers | Static documentation/demo site; no editor implementation |
| `edit-ac/cli` | Local-first Markdown/text editor client with optional hosted document sync | Native CLI artifacts, separately qualified |

Cargo names in the current scaffold use `editac-*` (Rust imports `editac_*`). npm names use `@edit-ac/*`. Preserve these established names. The draft's `@editac` imports are superseded.

Initial npm packages are `@edit-ac/core`, `@edit-ac/web`, `@edit-ac/react`. The core package owns one WASM engine, the web package owns imperative DOM plus storage/sync/module subpaths, and React owns lifecycle bindings. Additional packages require a real independently consumed boundary. Markdown is a portable Rust crate initially compiled into the task preset engine; moving parser preparation into an isolated worker cannot create another authoritative writable document.

## Current scaffold and future release

Scaffold packages deliberately export no editor API and have `private:true`; Rust crates have `publish=false`. They can be built, typechecked and packed locally but are not registry releases. Do not reserve names by publishing empty editor packages. The organization already owns its scope. Release work makes the flags public only after documented functionality and tarball-consumer validation exist.

Use exact direct tooling pins and lockfiles. Current compiler/tooling provenance and candidate runtime pins live in [dependency verification](../evidence/dependencies.md). Evaluate transitive licenses and advisories at installation/release; current metadata alone is not a compatibility or security proof. Prefer package-manager lockfile checks and immutable action commit references; retain Apache license and third-party notices in distributed artifacts.

## Artifact requirements

Build ESM and declarations into real exported paths. Package only dist, required WASM assets, README/license/notices. Test `npm pack` outputs by installing them into isolated plain browser and React/SSR examples without workspace symlinks. Verify asynchronous init, explicit asset URL, CSP/CDN loading, SSR import without DOM access, types, one runtime state owner and cleanup.

Keep WASM code generation separate from hand-maintained package metadata. Pin wasm-bindgen crate/CLI together and verify wasm-pack output target; do not assume bundler and browser-native outputs are interchangeable. Wasm binary/API changes participate in package versioning and compatibility tests.

## Publishing

Use public scoped packages, a `next` tag for the first qualified prerelease, a reviewed immutable revision, clean artifacts and declared version. Publish in dependency order core → web → react. Test exact registry versions in isolated consumer fixtures and record tarball integrity/provenance. Promotion to latest is a later release decision.

Prefer npm trusted publishing from GitHub-hosted Actions with `contents:read`, `id-token:write`, exact repository/workflow and protected environment. Configure only the intended publish permissions. Initial package bootstrap may require an authenticated owner/2FA before a package-level trusted publisher can be registered; verify npm's current flow when executing the release task. Never copy a browser session credential into the repository or add long-lived publish credentials to CI as a convenience.

Current setup verifies organization ownership but publishes no package. Do not report npm readiness as an existing registry version or an end-to-end OIDC test. The release roadmap owns those actions and checks; ordinary roadmap execution cannot bypass the artifact gate.

## CLI

The CLI is a local-first editor client consuming a reviewed immutable engine revision or released crate. A distributed manifest cannot depend on `../core` or an uncommitted worktree. The [CLI contract](cli.md) defines local Markdown/literal-text editing, hosted document targets, source reconciliation, recovery and durability states. Use the shared Markdown parser and semantic commands; Markdown is the editing representation, while hosted CRDT identity/history remains intact. Local editing requires no account/network; hosted transport is optional and uses the qualified sync contract. Preserve format version and error/diagnostic semantics. Save the opened target atomically with stale-file checks; overwriting a different export destination requires an explicit option. CLI release is independent of browser release and native platform SDK support.

Sources: [Cargo workspaces](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/workspaces.html), [npm trusted publishers](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/), [npm package files](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-json/).

## Full-client packaging

Decision003 adds the requested public docs repository alongside core, architecture and cli. Shared session/diff/optional security crates and native SDK artifacts live in core; CLI/TUI distributions remain in cli. Portable module entrypoints and host-app MCP helpers are optional surfaces qualified before publication. Roadmap 20 qualifies the full base client matrix; roadmap 24 qualifies encrypted profiles separately. No new monolithic cloud product or mandatory standalone MCP daemon is introduced.

## Expanded extension delivery

Optional highlighting and conversion dependencies use justified companion modules/crates and documented SDK entry points; no heavy runtime enters minimum loading merely by installing core. Roadmaps25–28 define shared services,31–36 wire actual native/terminal clients, and37 qualifies the expanded release. The protected profile24 additionally qualifies private assets, conversion, resolver and cloud behavior. Public docs/demo publication belongs to29; architecture fitness and capability compatibility belong to30. PDF is export-only.

specs/native-sdk-parity.md.text:
# Native SDK delivery and semantic parity

This is the delivery contract for roadmaps 16–18, 22 and 23: iOS, Android, macOS,
Windows and Linux. Roadmap 09 remains preparation evidence. Completing a binding or a
toolkit probe does not complete a native editor. These tracks deliver embeddable
native editor components, native sample hosts, supported package artifacts, and
the platform evidence consumed by roadmap 20.

## Ownership and prerequisites

All clients use the qualified engine, module registry, shared client/session
contracts, change model and extension library from roadmaps 02, 07, 12, 13 and 21.
Mobile preparation gates are task-specific within roadmap 09: both require
`NAT-1.1` portable engine evidence and `NAT-1.2` bounded binding evidence. iOS
additionally requires `NAT-1.3` Swift headless and `NAT-1.5` iOS control evidence;
Android requires `NAT-1.4` Kotlin headless and `NAT-1.6` Android control evidence.
Each bootstrap verifies those individual task artifacts against the consumed
engine/binding revisions. Neither mobile track waits for the other platform,
the joined `NAT-1.7` follow-up, or completion of all of roadmap 09. See
[client contracts](client-contracts.md), [changes](change-diffs.md) and
[extension library](extension-library.md).
The shared session owns document identity, commands, durable updates, history,
capabilities and transport state. Native adapters own input, OS selection,
presentation, accessibility and host integration. Native text storage is a
projection; it cannot become a second authoritative document. The same command
and fixture must produce the same semantic result across clients, while native
controls retain platform-appropriate appearance and interaction.

An adapter consumes the shared native storage/session port rather than creating
another journal, sync protocol or reconciliation engine. Persisted/asynchronous
targets use stable anchors. Bridge buffers have explicit ownership and bounded
lifetime; UTF-16 boundary units are converted at toolkit boundaries. Keep handle
access serialized, callbacks outside Rust locks/transactions, and UI mutations
on the required UI executor. A failed command cannot leave accepted UI text that
disagrees with the semantic store.

macOS, Windows and Linux are separate branches. A missing Windows host does not
block macOS or Linux work, and one successful desktop build does not qualify the
others. Each OS must pass its own toolkit feasibility, implementation, packaged
consumer, input and accessibility gates. Cross-platform qualification records
each result separately; a missing mandatory target remains an open deliverable.

## Mandatory capability matrix

Every listed native platform must deliver the following semantics. Create the
machine-readable matrix in each `native/<platform>/capability.json` from the
shared client capability schema; start all delivery claims as unqualified.
Matrix entries separately record render/read, edit, selection/navigation,
clipboard, import/export and accessibility support, with fixture and evidence
references. The current task may qualify only the behavior its tests exercise.

| Capability | Required native behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Text and selection | Unicode paragraphs, headings, code blocks, quotes and line breaks; stable selection mapping; grapheme-safe user actions; bidi navigation and platform input behavior within the declared matrix |
| Rich marks and links | Engine-defined bold, italic, strike, inline code and links; mixed selections; validated link activation; equivalent semantic import/export |
| Lists | Engine-defined ordered, unordered and task lists, checked state, nesting and structural commands; native keyboard/touch operation and block moves |
| Tables | Render the bounded engine table; edit real cells, navigate/select cells, and invoke supported row/column commands; preserve cell identity and reject unsupported structure explicitly |
| Images | Visible native image presentation with alt text and metadata; accessible selection, replacement and removal; host-controlled asset loading and failure state |
| References | Persistent target ID and label, native display and invocation, explicit host resolver, cancellation and stale-result protection |
| Custom modules | Qualified data-only marks and atoms with native renderer hooks, command routing, selection, accessible labels and disposal; unknown versions preserve bounded source data |
| Read-only | Copy and navigation remain usable while every mutation route, including IME, paste, drop and host commands, obeys the shared capability/authorization state |
| History | Native menu, key and gesture actions call shared origin-aware undo/redo; local grouping and remote edits match engine fixtures; a parallel OS undo stack cannot mutate the projection independently |
| Change review | Accessible native read-only unified/semantic change presentation from the portable roadmap-13 model; revision and representation/profile labels, trusted or unknown attribution, range navigation, and explicit stale state; no independent diff algorithm or live-replica rewind |
| Offline and recovery | Local editing needs no account/network; the shared durable receipt controls the locally committed indicator; process-crash restoration retains committed document changes and pending updates |
| Collaboration | Native clients exchange the same qualified updates and receipts as web; reconnect, remote selection, authorization change and document/session switching preserve shared semantics |
| Input and accessibility | Real platform composition, autocorrect/dictation where supported, hardware input, focus, screen-reader text/structure and accessible editing actions on declared OS/device combinations |

Plain text, an image of a table, an inert attachment, or a source-code fallback
does not satisfy a mandatory rich editing cell. Toolkit-native child controls
may provide a table cell or attachment editor if their selection, focus, history
and accessibility remain integrated with the one semantic session. The host
must expose required commands through native controls or input actions; matching
browser toolbar layout, slash-menu visuals or pixels is unnecessary.

Unknown extension preservation is a distinct safe behavior. It cannot mark a
first-party mandatory table, image or reference as implemented. A failed
feasibility probe produces a smaller replacement design for that OS; it never
silently downgrades the matrix or introduces a WebView.

## Optional math and declared limitations

Math is separately reported as `preserve-source`, `edit-source` and
`typeset-render`. Source editing must retain the shared bounded LaTeX data and
diagnostics; typesetting needs an explicitly selected native renderer with
license, size, accessibility and malformed-input evidence. `edit-source` does
not imply typesetting. An optional unqualified renderer can remain unavailable
when disclosed, but its source fallback cannot satisfy mandatory rich features.
The platform reports source-only math honestly instead of advertising visual
math parity. Unsupported custom executable behavior is also declared separately
from supported portable module data.

## Native toolkit decisions and evidence

These are candidates for platform-specific feasibility gates, not a claim that
one stock widget supports every required structure. Pin the SDK, compiler,
toolkit and deployment range in each platform's bootstrap task using the actual
build host and official availability documentation.

| Platform | Candidate and constraint | Primary evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| iOS | UIKit `UITextView`/TextKit plus native attachment or cell views. Selected and marked ranges belong to the text-input lifecycle; a marked range contains provisional composition text. Table editing and custom attachments require their own feasibility fixtures. | [Apple text input and marked text](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/StringsTextFonts/Conceptual/TextAndWebiPhoneOS/LowerLevelText-HandlingTechnologies/LowerLevelText-HandlingTechnologies.html) |
| Android | `EditText`/`Editable`, spans and native child views; preserve `InputConnection` composing, selection and batch semantics. Standard styled text is not evidence of editable tables or custom atom parity. | [Android InputConnection](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/inputmethod/InputConnection) |
| macOS | AppKit `NSTextView` and its native text storage/layout system, with native attachments or cell views where required. Probe attributed ranges, tables and custom atom editing against the chosen TextKit path. | [Apple text system organization](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/TextFonts/Conceptual/CocoaTextArchitecture/TextSystemArchitecture/ArchitectureOverview.html) |
| Windows | WinUI `RichEditBox`/native text services as the initial candidate. Its `ITextDocument` exposes selection, text ranges and native history; adapt history to the shared engine and prove structured editing/IME integration before selecting the host. | [Microsoft RichEditBox](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/ui/controls/rich-edit-box) |
| Linux | GTK4 `TextView`/`TextBuffer` with tags and native child widgets. Character offsets must be converted to the shared UTF-16 contract; child-anchor support alone does not establish table editing or accessible structured navigation. | [GTK character offsets](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/method.TextBuffer.get_iter_at_offset.html), [GTK child anchors](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/method.TextView.add_child_at_anchor.html) |

None of these choices permits WebView/Electron rendering or a second custom
typography engine. A replacement candidate must still use real native text input,
native accessibility, a portable Rust semantic core, and the same capability gates.

## Verification and package delivery

Each platform bootstrap creates its actual build/test dispatcher and named suites
before later tasks invoke them. Dispatchers reject unknown suite names and zero
matching tests, propagate build failures, and record executed/passed/failed/skipped
counts. Commands in the roadmaps are future interfaces created by those tasks,
not claims that build projects or tests already exist. Missing SDKs, signing
identities, device access, display servers or accessibility tooling have an exact
host/owner/unblock condition; the affected gate remains unchecked.

Use shared deterministic semantic fixtures and mocked storage/network/asset
services for automation. Cover two views of the same session, remote updates,
mount/dispose, error/cancel, schema/version rejection, and native-origin history.
Preserve failures and skipped cases. No live service credentials or paid inference
are needed. A recorded real-device/manual OS session is separate from synthetic
event tests and is mandatory for supported composition and screen-reader claims.

Platform packages must work in a clean consumer without a sibling checkout:
Swift package plus the declared Apple binary slices; Android library with the
declared ABI artifacts; a native Windows SDK package; and a native Linux package
with a declared GTK/runtime baseline. Lock runtime/generator versions and record
bridge/schema compatibility, third-party notices, symbols and immutable artifact
hashes. Signing and public publication occur only under their explicit release
tasks; locally building a package is not registry publication.

The final epic of each native roadmap builds the package, verifies a clean
consumer and prepares exact qualification inputs. This establishes implementation
and package readiness. Roadmap 20 performs the actual OS/device, real-input and
screen-reader qualification against those source/artifact revisions. Until that
evidence passes, support remains unqualified. Full native delivery is incomplete
while any mandatory platform/capability is blocked, unsupported, untested or
represented only by a binding demonstration.

## Everyday interactions and optional assistance

Reuse [editor interactions](editor-interactions.md) and its [case catalog](../tests/editor-interaction-cases.md) for shared semantic expectations while retaining native visual navigation, text-input and accessibility policy. Browser event replays do not qualify a native adapter. Track 39 adds [assistive input](assistive-input.md) presenters in independently gated iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, Linux and terminal tasks; baseline OS dictation and screen-reader editing stay required without the extension.

specs/cli.md.text:
# Local-first CLI editor client

Status: development contract; editing and hosted connectivity are planned, not implemented by the current scaffold.
Scope: the `editac` client in `edit-ac/cli`, consuming the shared Rust engine and Markdown implementation.

## User workflow and targets

The CLI is an editor client for local text and online hosted documents. Markdown is the user-facing editable representation. Local editing requires neither an account nor a network connection; hosting adds synchronization to the same editing workflow.

The initial interaction opens a working text file in an explicitly configured editor, then `$VISUAL` or `$EDITOR`. A built-in terminal UI is a separately scoped follow-up. Run the configured executable with arguments and the file path; document configuration parsing and never interpolate document contents or targets into a shell command. Missing editor configuration, editor failure and cancellation return actionable results without committing changes.

The planned command surface is:

- `editac edit <path>` opens or explicitly creates a local Markdown document. An existing file is an edit target; creating a missing file requires `--create`.
- `editac edit <path> --format text` edits literal UTF-8 text without interpreting Markdown. `.txt` targets default to literal text; `.md` targets default to Markdown. Other suffixes require an explicit format.
- `editac edit <hosted-document-url>` opens an authorized edit.ac-compatible hosted document, or its existing local cache when offline. The configured service adapter resolves document identity; an arbitrary HTTP page is not a writable document API.
- `editac status <target>` reports local persistence, pending synchronization and remote durability separately.
- `editac sync <hosted-document-url>` explicitly retries pending work using the configured adapter. Local file editing never attaches a transport implicitly.

These names are planned contracts, not executable examples for the scaffold. Help advertises only implemented capabilities. Validation/conversion/inspection remain secondary operations; JSON and CRDT bytes are not the user's editing buffer.

## Markdown and shared state

Use the dialect, safety limits and diagnostics in [formats](formats.md). Literal text mode retains literal text and does not run Markdown typing shortcuts. One Yrs replica owns committed semantics during a session. The source buffer and parsed candidates are temporary input projections, as native text controls are in other hosts; there is no parallel writable editor model.

Keep the exact source baseline alongside semantic identities and stable anchors. Compare edited source with that baseline, prepare a bounded semantic change using the shared Rust parser/engine, validate it, then commit through the shared command/history boundary. A no-op preserves file bytes, whitespace and source spelling. Successful local source edits preserve the user's edited Markdown spelling; normalized Markdown serialization is an explicit export action. Importing a local file into a fresh session is permitted; re-importing a whole hosted snapshot on each save is not.

The shared source-reconciliation API must be qualified before advertising editing: source ranges alone do not prove stable identity mapping. Preserve unchanged nodes, marks and unknown module data. If a proposed Markdown change cannot retain unsupported semantics or map safely to current anchors, reject the commit with diagnostics and retain the edited source for recovery. A deliberate lossy export must be a separate explicit action. Invalid UTF-8, malformed input, resource-limit failures and rejected edits never partially mutate the live document.

Hosted exports use the deterministic Markdown representation, not the original author's source spelling. Retain the opening projection and its identity/anchor mapping as the edit baseline. Parse only user-edited source; received structured updates go directly into the existing replica. Source editing does not reinterpret remote updates as Markdown or reset collaborative history/epoch.

## Local files and recovery

Ordinary local text files are portable inputs and outputs, usable with other editors. Cache/journal files are recoverable session state, not a mandatory proprietary document container. New files remain local unless the user explicitly chooses a hosted destination; editing a local path must not upload content.

Capture target identity and content fingerprint when opening. Before publishing an edit, verify the baseline has not been replaced or changed. Use a cooperating client lock and same-directory temporary write, flush, atomic publication and the supported platform's directory durability mechanism. Refuse a detected external edit or replacement; retain both the user's candidate and current target for explicit resolution. Document the limit of conflict detection with non-cooperating external writers; an atomic rename alone is not a compare-and-swap. Do not silently follow a changed symlink or overwrite an unrelated destination. The normal save authorizes changes to the opened target; export to an existing different path requires an explicit overwrite option.

An unchanged buffer or canceled session leaves the original untouched. Failures before publication preserve the original and recoverable draft. Report local saved status only after the tested durability boundary, and report uncertain publication explicitly. Retain recovery data until that boundary succeeds. UTF-8/Unicode, line-ending policy, file permissions, missing/read-only targets, full disk and process interruption need deterministic fixtures.

For hosted documents, persist CRDT checkpoint, journal, pending update identities and bytes using a native adapter for [storage/sync](storage-sync.md). Keep drafts that have not yet passed semantic reconciliation separately from committed updates. Local Markdown export does not replace the checkpoint or outbox. Restore once with a distinct live replica/writer identity; subsequent network attachment must not initialize a second document.

## Hosted documents and concurrency

Use a configured service adapter with explicit endpoint, document ID, schema and epoch. Reuse saved credentials through the configured credential store; authentication and authorization remain service responsibilities. Keep tokens out of document files, working buffers and diagnostic output. No production service, new server protocol or automatic background daemon is implied by this client plan.

First open requires an authorized bootstrap; cached documents can be edited offline. Persist local changes before sending them, retain the outbox across exit/crash, and reuse the qualified sync protocol and receipt semantics. Authentication failure, revocation or unavailable service leaves local work recoverable and exportable. An uncached offline target returns a clear unavailable result rather than an empty editable replacement.

While the editor buffer is open, remote changes may advance the replica. Revalidate source-derived changes against current anchors before commit. Disjoint proven mappings may merge through the shared engine; overlapping changes, deleted targets or ambiguous source mappings produce an explicit conflict with retained base/local/current representations. Never overwrite the hosted document with stale full-text Markdown or claim CRDT synchronization resolves an arbitrary whole-source replacement.

Expose at least locally saved, pending upload, remotely committed, remote durability unknown, conflict, authorization failure and incompatible schema/epoch. `remoteCommitted` requires the negotiated durable application receipt; socket delivery or a matching state vector is insufficient. Services without receipts may synchronize but cannot be reported as remotely saved. Schema/epoch mismatch requires an explicit supported transition and must not discard old offline edits.

## Delivery and qualification

Local editing depends on the qualified engine and Markdown contracts. Native persistence is implemented in the CLI track; browser IndexedDB code is not reused as a native filesystem adapter. Hosted tasks additionally require the qualified synchronization track at the current revision. These are staged gates so an unavailable host does not block local delivery. CLI release remains independent of browser package publication and native UI parity.

Use prepared fixtures, a fake editor executable and mocked service/auth/receipt transports. Cover local Markdown and literal text, no-op/cancel, source preservation, supported semantic changes, unknown content, stale file save, crash recovery, cached offline edit, concurrent hosted edits, reconnect, revocation and wrong/missing receipts. Record actual executed/passed/failed/skipped counts and preserved failures. No paid inference, live credential loading or production hosted writes belong in automated qualification.

## Full client follow-up

Roadmap 15 delivers the built-in TUI in [tui-client](tui-client.md), reusing this external-editor/local/hosted baseline and [shared client contracts](client-contracts.md). Both clients accept validated ac:// document locators through the same catalog/authority resolver; IDs are not bearer credentials. Diff preview uses [change-diffs](change-diffs.md). Host-app MCP is a separate adapter and is not required to use or release the CLI/TUI.

specs/engine.md.text:
# Shared engine contract

Status: development contract; the bounded foundation profile is locally qualified in [foundation evidence](../evidence/foundation.md). Production engine behavior remains subject to its own gates.
Scope: web editor release, with portable Rust interfaces for later native adapters.
The initial roadmap's full native SDK parity requirement is deferred by the current project scope.
This document describes required behavior; it does not assert that the engine is implemented.

## Ownership and dependency boundary

- Yrs is the only writable authoritative document state, including offline single-user sessions.
- Rust owns committed content, schemas, semantic commands, relative anchors and local history.
- DOM, native attributed strings, read indexes and exports are derived projections.
- Adapters may retain temporary composition state under the browser/native input contract.
- React owns the host lifecycle; it never owns a second document tree.
- Yjs is used in interoperability fixtures. Do not mirror production state into a second `Y.Doc`.
- Core code has no DOM, React, IndexedDB, socket, UIKit or Android dependencies.
- Persistence and synchronization consume immutable update bytes and metadata through ports.

## Compatibility profile

Start the compatibility spike with Yrs 0.28.0, Yjs 13.6.33 and y-protocols 1.0.7.
These exact pins are qualified for the bounded foundation profile; upgrades require new interoperability evidence.
Enable Yrs `small-client` for the stable Yjs 13 line; the 0.28 default is different.
Set `OffsetKind::Utf16` explicitly in a single document-construction path.
Use update encoding v1 for the baseline; v2 requires a separate qualified profile.
Record schema version, document identity and session/epoch separately from transport identity.
Generate a distinct client ID for every independently editing live replica, including tabs.
Never restore one persisted writer ID into two simultaneously active writers.
Freeze root shared-type names and types with the schema decision.
Pin dependency versions and options in fixtures; upgrades rerun the compatibility suite.

The foundation freeze specifies exact roots and bounded ownership in
[schema-v1.md](schema-v1.md), and metadata/admission in
[protocol-v1.md](protocol-v1.md). FND-1.12 qualifies this exact fixed-pair mapping
with pinned Yrs/Yjs moves, deletion, overlapping edits, split/join ownership and
binary relative anchors from both languages; see
[structural exchange evidence](../evidence/foundation-schema-interop/README.md).
This is deterministic local interoperability evidence. The actual compiled fixture
WASM boundary is separately qualified by [loading evidence](../evidence/foundation-wasm/README.md)
for supplied-URL and local packed native ESM consumers, with SSR-safe import.
It uses the earlier XML/text fixture, not production registry commands.
Production commands, admission ports and persistence remain subsequent gates.

### Controller-qualified schema evolution

The frozen foundation supplies bounded interoperability, not every engine primitive.
[Versioned block metadata](schema-v2.md) defines the ENG-1.16 qualification mapping
for paragraph/heading state, including empty blocks and split owners. ENG-1.6 may
use it only after the exact profile/admission and Rust/Yjs evidence pass. Keep the
foundation contract, fixtures and historical receipts unchanged; new schemas are
explicit profile/epoch boundaries, not extra roots silently added to v1.

[Ownership evolution](schema-evolution.md) defines ENG-1.17's representation proof
and ENG-1.18's production integration for arbitrary, repeatable split/join. Existing
ENG-1.7 evidence remains the fixed-pair baseline. Downstream structural commands
depend on the new integration gate. Missing representation evidence must stay
unchecked; controller-authorized qualification work resolves the mapping, rather
than polling for an unspecified external decision or reducing acceptance.

[Nested structural profile v4](schema-v4.md) supplies the controller contract for
list/quote containers, numbering/check state, code/separator presentation,
versioned placement and reversible structural history controls. ENG-1.19 and
ENG-1.20 qualify the exact representation and code policy separately; ENG-1.21
integrates it before ENG-1.8/1.9. Preserve existing v3 receipts and recognize their
ordinary-block scope. The new profile is explicit qualification work, not an
external schema wait or permission to weaken the remaining parents.

[Stable presentation v5](schema-v5.md) resolves ENG-1.9-F1: split/join command
eligibility captures immutable preparation witnesses, so later valid formatting
does not replay an established join as losing or resurrect its absorbed owner.
ENG-1.22 qualifies that separately versioned rule; ENG-1.23 integrates it before
full ENG-1.9 acceptance. Preserve v4's mapping and historical guard/failure
evidence; do not call a presentation-conflict rejection positive conversion proof.

## Positions and anchors

- Public text offsets are UTF-16 code units with documented start/end affinity.
- Reject positions inside a surrogate pair before opening a live mutation transaction.
- Rust byte indexes and scalar counts are internal details; conversion must be explicit.
- Grapheme-aware movement/deletion must cover combining marks, ZWJ emoji, flags and RTL.
- Do not redefine a grapheme as a UTF-16 code unit or a Rust `char`.
- Asynchronous commands, selections and remote cursors use stable relative anchors.
- Resolving an anchor returns a position or an explicit deleted/unresolvable result.
- A deleted target never silently redirects an asynchronous insertion to the document end.
- Each fixture records the original string, UTF-16 range, expected text and anchor result.

## Prepare, validate, commit

1. Parse arguments and resolve dependencies before acquiring a mutable Yrs transaction.
2. Resolve target anchors against the current revision and validate the entire command.
3. Prepare the complete mutation plan, including resource and schema checks.
4. Check that the prepared preconditions still hold immediately before applying it.
5. Apply one non-fallible semantic mutation phase with an explicit origin.
6. Emit a revision, dirty ranges, immutable update bytes and operation metadata.

Yrs commits when its mutable transaction is dropped. Error returns do not roll it back.
Never catch a partial mutation error and report the document as unchanged.
Validation failures must leave content, state vector, history and journal enqueue count unchanged.
`can(command)` uses preparation/validation without mutation or subscriber side effects.
A command chain validates all document mutations before any of them changes the live store.
Host focus/menu side effects are outside the atomic document mutation contract.
Reentrant adapter callbacks cannot mutate a document while a transaction is active.
Revision numbers are local observation tokens, not globally comparable CRDT timestamps.

## Atomic heading-end Enter

WEB-1.14 owns the engine/WASM prerequisite for WEB-1.8. Add the prepared Rust editor command `HeadingEnd { owner, at }` and the packed command `{ type: "headingEnd", owner, at }`, using the existing engine-owned stable anchor token and editor request envelope. This is an additive command API on the qualified v5 replica; it does not change the persisted schema or peer update protocol.

Prepare this command only for a nonempty heading whose resolved cut is its current text end. Earlier text deletions in the same prepared batch may produce that end cut; qualify both selected replacement and cross-block selected replacement without live intermediate mutations. Preserve the original heading identity, level, remaining text and marks. Create one empty paragraph immediately after it under the same parent. Preserve unrelated blocks and remote edits. Resolve the right-biased cut to the resulting paragraph at offset zero; expose a stable result through the existing anchor/result contract rather than guessing generated owner IDs in the adapter.

Stage the split and destination paragraph attributes together before one live mutation, with normal resource/schema/stale checks. `can` and rejected preparations leave content, state vector, history, updates and journal effects unchanged. Admission/read-only/disposed/stale rejection uses the existing boundary policies. One successful local command produces one update and one explicit semantic undo group. Undo/redo restores/reapplies the original heading and paragraph while retaining unrelated remote edits. Empty-heading Enter remains conversion of that owner to a paragraph; interior-heading Enter remains ordinary split; code, lists and quotes retain their existing contextual policies.

Qualify actual Rust semantics, packed WASM dispatch/types, UTF-16 anchors and independently authored undo/redo/peer outcomes before the browser switches from its explicit rejection. Full browser heading-end mechanics remain WEB-1.8 acceptance; neither a planned API nor filtered keyboard successes pass that parent.

## Structural representation gate

Implement disposable fixtures for conventional Yrs XML and stable block identities with placement metadata.
Use the same corpus and comparison outputs; do not implement two production engines.
The winning representation must preserve rich-text identity during semantic moves.
A registry candidate should test one replacement placement tuple rather than independently merged parent/order fields.
This candidate is not a promised wire schema; the spike must prove its behavior first.

The decision record must define:

- Ordering, winning concurrent placement and tie-breaking independent of arrival order.
- Cycles, orphan nodes, invalid references and duplicate placements.
- Delete/edit policy and recovery of concurrent content hidden by deletion.
- Split/edit and join/edit behavior, including marks and selections.
- Nested list moves and invalid ancestor/descendant operations.
- Unknown node/mark retention without fetching or executing extension code.
- Version admission, upgrade policy and rollback/recovery constraints.

No renderer or serializer may invent a structural repair by emitting platform-specific writes.
Projection must be deterministic and converge semantically on every supported replica.
Freeze the schema only after permutation/replay fixtures pass and the ADR names the choice.
Downstream production structural commands depend on that decision; standalone input spikes do not.

## Undo and redo

Use Yrs selective history with explicitly tracked local origins.
Exclude remote updates, restore replay, checkpoint loading and presence from local history.
UndoManager groups by capture interval and origin; one transaction is not automatically one undo item.
Place explicit history boundaries around paste, formatting, structural move and composition groups.
Define typing coalescing separately; selection changes alone do not create content history.
Include newly created shared text in history scope when the chosen representation requires it.
Undo must preserve unrelated remote edits and produce ordinary persisted/synchronized updates.
Bound history memory; clearing history must not change current document content.
Cross-restart restoration of the full undo stack is outside the initial release contract.

## Persistence and synchronization ports

Updates carry document/session identity, writer identity, sequence and schema version.
Restore CRDT state and its journal tail; JSON/Markdown imports create a new explicit document/session.
Do not initialize a recovered document again while waiting for a network response.
Duplicate/reordered updates must be harmless; origins prevent adapter echo loops.
`localCommitted` follows successful storage transaction completion, never enqueue time.
`remoteCommitted` requires an identified durable service receipt, never a generic synced event.
Retain unacknowledged local updates and recovery content on failed or unauthorized upload.
Publish checkpoint coverage transactionally and retain the prior recovery point until safe replacement.
Storage errors are observable state; no false saved indicator is permitted.
Apply bounded decoding/resource checks to untrusted updates before admission.
Invalid schema/version input requires an explicit rejection or preserved recovery state, not silent repair.

## Required deterministic evidence

- Three replicas with operation reordering, duplicate delivery, disconnection and replay.
- Rust-to-JS and JS-to-Rust fixtures using the exact same edit-ac schema.
- Every structural race listed above, including all distinct arrival permutations in small cases.
- Invalid-command tests proving no partial content/history/persistence change.
- Unicode boundary, relative-anchor and undo-after-remote-edit fixtures.
- Crash/fault injection at journal, checkpoint and receipt commit boundaries.
- Fresh initialization versus restored/empty-but-existing document cases.
- Bounded resource behavior for malformed updates, deep content and fragmented marks.

Record failures and skips. Prepared fixtures establish deterministic correctness, not provider quality.
All tests remain local or use deterministic transports; no paid inference belongs in this engine.

## Primary references

- [Yrs compatibility and transaction lifecycle](https://docs.rs/yrs/latest/yrs/)
- [Yrs UTF-16 configuration](https://docs.rs/yrs/latest/yrs/types/text/trait.Text.html)
- [Yrs selective history](https://docs.rs/yrs/latest/yrs/undo/struct.UndoManager.html)
- [Yjs update contract](https://docs.yjs.dev/api/document-updates)
- [IndexedDB durability](https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/)

## Full-client compatibility contract

Follow-up [client contracts](client-contracts.md) build on these primitives for every native/terminal/host-agent client. Stable identities, prepared commands, anchors and update ports must remain usable without DOM, MCP or a particular store. Revision validation must account for deletions; a state vector alone is not an exact content token. Companion revision/history/security modules remain optional boundaries. The existing foundation roadmap is unchanged; new follow-up entry gates verify the frozen implementation before claiming compatibility.

specs/client-contracts.md.text:
# Shared local-first client contracts

Status: planned portable interfaces, delivered by roadmap 12. Reuse engine, source reconciliation, storage/sync and CLI contracts. This document is an interface contract, not an implemented API.

## Document addressing

Document identity comprises opaque document ID, epoch/session and schema profile. Source identity is separate: a filesystem path, cached document, or configured authority locator can refer to the same document. Moving a file does not silently clone its collaboration identity; copying/importing creates a new explicit identity unless the host intentionally links it.

Proposed input forms are `ac://<document-id>` for catalog resolution and `ac://<authority>/<document-id>` for a configured authority. Freeze escaping, ID case, Unicode, reserved separators, normalization and optional version query semantics in fixtures before publishing the URI API. A short hash-looking ID is not promised collision-free or content-addressed. Support allowlisted HTTPS app links only through the same resolver.

Resolution returns local/cached/hosted/locked/unavailable/unauthorized/incompatible outcomes. A locator contains no password, token or encryption key. Resolving arbitrary hosts or file paths cannot bypass host allowlists, path permissions or SSRF policy. Displaying or importing a link never performs an implicit network fetch. Launching an OS deep link requires host registration/activation policy; it cannot execute a shell command from URI text.

## Local-first session

Provide a portable session companion to the engine with LocalStore, Transport, SourceResolver, AuthorizationPolicy and optional HistoryStore ports. IndexedDB, native transactional storage and CLI recovery implement the same journal/checkpoint/outbox conformance cases, without forcing a database crate or browser runtime into the semantic core. Promote CLI/native duplicated lifecycle logic into this shared boundary.

Opening a cached document first restores local state, then enables editing and optionally attaches networking. Creating a local document is offline and idempotent; subsequent hosting assigns an explicit authority mapping rather than re-importing content. An uncached offline hosted target returns unavailable. Local commands, undo/redo and readonly views never wait for a socket.

Expose restoring, ready, unsaved/pending local, locally committed, pending upload, synchronized-but-durability-unknown, remotely committed, conflict, locked and recovery-required states. Connectivity is orthogonal to durability. A completed local transaction is not an upload receipt. Native suspend/termination and browser tab close use the same recovery contract, without relying on an unload handler.

Sharing a database is not live synchronization. Cross-tab/process adapters exchange committed updates with distinct writer/client IDs and echo suppression. Test a pair of offline local clients plus reconnect to a hosted peer. Backpressure bounds memory and preserves an outbox rather than dropping acknowledged edits.

Hosts define offline authorization policy/leases. Offline revocation cannot retroactively remove already acquired plaintext. An expired policy may block further writes while retaining recovery data; a host cannot promise both unrestricted offline writes and instantaneous remote revocation. Upload always rechecks server authorization. Readonly is enforced by every mutation entry point, including MCP and imports, not just controls.

## Revision and edit admission

Return opaque revision tokens bound to a specific document/epoch/schema/profile and immutable observed state. A Yjs state vector alone is insufficient because deletions can change visible state without advancing the same clocks. Choose and test a persisted generation/content-state validator including deletion effects; tokens are not globally ordered wall clocks.

Compare expected revision and prepared preconditions within the serialized commit boundary. Equality protects the endpoint's observed state; it is not a global lock against offline peers whose updates arrive later. Surface subsequent merged changes normally. No direct `replaceDocument(markdown)` shortcut is allowed to defeat source reconciliation.

The shared editor service exposes read snapshot/capabilities, prepare semantic commands or source changes, preview, apply, observe changes and receipt lookup. It uses FMT-1.12's exact baseline/source-to-identity mapping. Unsupported or ambiguous mappings return recoverable base/proposed/current data.
