Capability checks include document permissions, module support, readonly/history mode and resource limits.

A post-commit persistence failure enters recovery mode: freeze further mutation admission and outbound synchronization until ordered durable recovery succeeds. Keep reads and labeled recovery exports available; bound queued incoming updates. Later human edits, checkpoints or full-state synchronization must not publish an unjournaled predecessor. When the predecessor is an agent request, its durable dedup receipt belongs to the same publication barrier; see the host-agent contract.

## Operation identity and history

Each admitted operation has a request/operation ID, authenticated actor supplied by the host, origin, affected identities and observed before/after revision. Actor metadata from document prose or a client-supplied display name is not trusted attribution. CRDT client IDs alone are not authenticated authors.

History origin policy separates local human gestures, other humans, agent operations, imports and replay. Agent operations can be reviewed/reverted as authorized new changes without becoming unintended human typing undo groups. Cross-client operation records feed diff/history views, but are not described as a tamper-proof audit ledger without additional evidence.

## Readiness evidence

Run identical prepared command/recovery fixtures through web, headless native and CLI session adapters. Require no-network local startup, empty existing document vs new document, multi-writer delivery, crash boundary recovery, quota/full-disk errors, disconnected auth failure, wrong epoch, stale revision and locked-document cases. No paid model calls or production account access is needed.

Implementation patterns and limits: [research](../evidence/followup-research.md). Related contracts: [storage/sync](storage-sync.md), [CLI](cli.md), [diffs](change-diffs.md), [host agents](agent-editing.md).

specs/extension-library.md.text:
# Public extension library contract

Status: development contract extending the qualified first-party modules.

The library exposes the existing [portable module contract](modules-native.md)
through stable, documented entry points and conformance fixtures. It consumes
the [shared client contracts](client-contracts.md) and [Markdown contract](formats.md).
It does not recreate the existing slash/reference/reorder/image/table/math
implementations or turn document data into executable plugin code.

## Public entry points and registration

Publish supported Rust descriptor/command/codec interfaces from their owning
crate and browser integration from documented package exports. Use the existing
`@edit-ac/core` and `@edit-ac/web` boundaries unless a measured, independently
consumed feature justifies another package. Internal source paths are not public
import contracts. Pin fixture consumers to immutable packages/revisions.

Each descriptor names a namespace, type, version, content shape, bounded
attributes, applicable built-in commands, Markdown codecs, fallback policy and
supported host capabilities. Validate descriptors before attaching a document;
duplicate/incompatible registrations fail without partial mutation. Freeze a
session's registry according to the existing schema/initialization contract.

Data-defined marks and atoms using qualified schema/command primitives register
without rebuilding the Rust engine or its WASM/native bindings. This does not
promise arbitrary new editing semantics without engine work. A host may supply
its own renderer implementation through a typed interface; renderer callbacks,
code and downloaded executable plugins never live in document state. Unknown
types and versions retain their bounded original payload and explicit fallback.

## Conformance and evolution

The reusable conformance suite accepts a descriptor plus fixed fixtures and
checks validation, deterministic serialization, supported Markdown round trips,
copy/export behavior, command applicability/preparation/commit, undo grouping,
origin handling, subscription filtering, disposal and unknown-version retention.
It compares canonical semantic outcomes rather than raw CRDT byte equality.
Every claimed capability has a test or an explicit external qualification owner.

Codecs preserve unknown/disabled module data or produce recoverable diagnostics
before mutation. A codec cannot silently reinterpret arbitrary source into an
unsupported module. Source-reconciliation fixtures must show that edits elsewhere
retain module identity and content. Literal-text input bypasses Markdown codecs.

Descriptor/schema evolution declares compatible reads, supported migration paths
and unsupported versions. Migration operates on validated candidate data and
commits through the existing schema/epoch transition protocol when required; no
automatic in-place rewrite may invalidate offline updates. Failed migration keeps
the original data recoverable. Qualification includes old/new/unknown versions,
interrupted migration and delayed updates. Module version numbers alone do not
authorize a document-wide schema transition.

## Presenter and host interfaces

Presenters receive stable node identity, validated content, selection/capability
state and bounded incremental patches. They request edits through shared prepared
commands and expose idempotent update/dispose/cancel behavior. They do not own
another writable document or invoke callbacks under engine transactions. Async
results carry request identity and are ignored after cancellation, disposal or
target revision change. UI actions respect the host's read-only capability.

Define separate browser, terminal, Swift/iOS, Kotlin/Android and desktop adapter
contracts for focus, input/composition ownership, accessible labels/actions,
clipboard/Markdown representation, selection/atom boundaries and theme/lifecycle.
Use headless conformance adapters here. Full platform renderers and real-device
evidence belong to their platform tracks; this track supplies their fixtures and
acceptance hooks without depending on those downstream implementations.

## Built-in capability obligations

| Module | Shared obligation | Presenter obligation |
|---|---|---|
| Slash | Local trigger invokes one registered command/history group | Accessible menu and focus restoration; remote edits never open it |
| References | Persistent target identity/label, host resolver, cancellation | Honest unresolved label and accessible explicit activation |
| Reorder | Identity-preserving semantic move and stable selection | Keyboard action on each editable host; pointer handle when supported |
| Images | Bounded metadata, alt text, host asset policy, preserved source | Accessible image or declared fallback; no implicit upload |
| Tables | Bounded rectangle and shared simple-cell commands | Selection/navigation and clipboard behavior or a declared nonediting fallback |
| Math | Bounded source and safe codec, invalid-source retention | Qualified renderer or explicit source fallback; no inferred typesetting parity |

The machine-readable matrix distinguishes data preservation, view, edit, copy,
Markdown, accessibility and optional rendering for every supported host/module
combination. Mandatory product parity cells are explicit; unsupported cells need
an owner and delivery gate rather than disappearing from the matrix. Source-only
fallback meets preservation, not a richer rendering/editing claim. Platform tracks
consume these obligations, and final cross-client qualification verifies them.

Reference lookup/activation uses host-controlled catalog/authority capabilities,
including configured `ac://` resolution. A reference is an identifier, never
credentials or proof of immutable content. Opening/rendering a document does not
implicitly fetch reference targets or images, launch commands, read arbitrary
files or grant remote editing authority. Prepared host-resolver tests cover
revocation, delayed/out-of-order results, forbidden targets and stale anchors.

## Loading, examples and publication boundary

Optional browser presenter assets load only when explicitly enabled/needed.
Minimal bundles omit disabled presenter code/assets; stored data remains readable
through fallback. Record actual JS/WASM/CSS/asset contributions and pinned build
settings. Native/TUI manifests identify optional dependencies and renderer assets;
do not equate a source feature flag with measured binary-size savings.

Provide a third-party tutorial for one data-defined mark and one atom, using only
public imports and the conformance harness. Its clean consumer fixture must work
with unchanged engine artifacts, survive absent renderers, preserve data through
Markdown/source editing, and dispose resources. Show where a genuinely new
editing semantic requires core work. These documentation examples are validated
consumer artifacts, not merely copied implementation snippets.

Build/pack/consumer qualification belongs here; publication follows the release
policy. No marketplace, downloaded plugin execution, remote service deployment
or provider inference is required to demonstrate the library.

## Rich ecosystem delivery

Baseline07/21 contracts remain the foundation. [Rich content](rich-content-extensions.md) adds portable code highlighting, table formatting, assets/embeds and interaction upgrades. [Link resolution](link-resolution.md) separates public metadata from principal-scoped internal references; [conversion](document-conversion.md) provides optional document formats with PDF export only. Roadmaps31–36 integrate actual clients and37 qualifies the expanded profile. Heavy providers remain optional and permission checks stay host-owned.

## Assistive input extension

Track 39 uses these same registration/presenter/conformance interfaces for [assistive input](assistive-input.md). Its descriptor exposes optional command/status/host-transport capabilities without a persisted transcript, second editing model or built-in speech provider. Baseline keyboard, native dictation and accessibility remain usable without the descriptor. Native integrations have task-specific SDK gates and actual platform evidence.

## Mobile web presenter obligations

[Mobile web](mobile-web.md) supplies minimal shared browser focus/viewport/capability ports; [track 41](../roadmaps/41-mobile-web-extensions.md) qualifies existing extension presenters on touch devices. Each presenter declares gesture/focus/scroll ownership, reachable tap controls, cancellation, capability fallback, loading trigger and per-instance resources. Disabled registration causes no feature import/evaluation, listeners/observers, assets, worker or network work. Native selection/scroll/zoom and baseline command access stay usable without enhanced mobile UI.

specs/schema-v4.md.text:
# Nested structural editor profile v4

Status: controller-authored development contract; ENG-1.19/1.20 qualification and ENG-1.21 production integration are required. This is not a passing interoperability, persistence or release claim. Preserve the qualified v1/v2/v3 layouts, fixtures and receipts.

## Envelope and roots

Schema `editac.registry.editor.v4`, profile `editac.yrs-yjs.editor.v4`; protocol version 1, update encoding 1, UTF-16 offsets. Keep Yrs 0.28.0 with small-client, Yjs 13.6.33, y-protocols 1.0.7 and the pinned toolchains. Use the exact external protocol-v1 envelope, initialized flag and fresh independent writer identities. Admission checks the exact profile/schema/document/epoch before live mutation. No optimistic v3 acceptance, new roots in an old profile, automatic migration or reseeding restored empty documents. A future explicit migration retains the old checkpoint and creates a new epoch.

All ten roots are `MapRef` / `Y.Map`. Preserve v3's retained original-text and operation semantics except the explicitly specified v4 extensions below:

| Root | Exact values |
| --- | --- |
| `registry-parents` | Original source `n:<writer>:<counter>` to immutable `block`; container `c:<writer>:<counter>` to immutable `list` or `quote` |
| `registry-texts` | Original source ID to its single persistent nested `XmlTextRef` / `Y.XmlText`; containers have no text entry |
| `registry-placements` | Original source/container ID to its immutable initial `[parentId, order]` tuple; integral order 0…4294967295 |
| `delete-probe-tombstones` | Original/derived owner/container ID to permanent boolean true |
| `registry-block-attributes` | Original/derived text owner to one complete block-presentation tuple, specified below |
| `registry-ownership-ops` | Unique operation ID to one immutable split/join/place operation tuple |
| `registry-owner-origins` | Each original text source to true; no container or derived owner membership |
| `registry-container-attributes` | List container to `["unordered"]`, `["ordered", start]` or `["checklist"]`; quote container to `["quote"]` |
| `registry-list-item-attributes` | Original/derived text owner to `["check", boolean]`; absence means unchecked |
| `registry-entity-controls` | Original/container/operation ID to `["enabled", boolean]`; absence means enabled |

Array values are atomic `Any::Array` / plain JavaScript arrays, never nested independently merged shared arrays. Writer/counter grammar and bounds match v3; `c:` is a separate namespace allocated monotonically with no reuse. Containers never acquire source texts; splits never clone texts or create registry source entries. Creation reserves immutable kind, initial placement, original-text/origin membership if applicable, and required initial metadata in one prepared transaction. Initial roots/rows establish base versions and are retained thereafter.

Only `@root`, lists and quotes can be parents. Container attributes are stored independently of text length. Ordered start is an integral number 1…2147483647. List mode and start replace as one tuple; concurrent tuple writes use the pinned map conflict rule, not independently merged type/start fields. Checklist state applies to a direct editable child of a checklist container; outside that context retain it dormant without rendering a checkbox. List numbering is derived from current visible direct editable children in sibling order, starting at the tuple's start, with no numbering writes during projection. Nested containers do not increment their parent's editable-child ordinal. Malformed known tuples reject admission; valid unknown JSON discriminants stay opaque with safe retained fallback and cannot be semantic command targets. No extension fetch/execution.

Unknown immutable kind strings retain the same namespace/text/origin membership shapes: an original keeps its text in a read-only safe fallback; an opaque container retains its children, which project at root because it is not an allowed parent. Local creation/structural edits support only the named known kinds. Nonstring kinds or incompatible shared types reject admission; opaque retention does not grant execution or a guessed structural role.

## Ownership, placement and hierarchy

Keep v3 split/join tuples, binary source-relative cuts, dependency graph and total operation ranking (depth, numeric writer, numeric counter). Add:

`["place", targetId, targetVersion, parentId, parentVersion, beforeSiblingId, beforeSiblingVersion]`

`beforeSiblingId` and its version are both null for append. For `@root`, parent version is `"base"`. Other version fields are `"base"` or an operation ID. All non-base versions are graph dependencies. The operation ID is a version token; only split operations create a derived text owner with that ID.

Initial sibling order is initial numeric placement order, then namespace ASCII and numeric writer/counter. Read valid initial nested placements, detach the smallest canonical ID in each cycle, and project missing/unknown/noncontainer parents at root. Retain the raw placement without repair writes. Enforce iterative bounded traversal. Containers own no characters. Each text owner has one effective parent and sibling position; project the resulting tree in preorder.

Replay starts from that base tree. Split inserts the derived right owner immediately after left under the same parent and retains the existing span/cut/version semantics. Join requires two adjacent visible editable owners with the same parent; it preserves left identity/placement/metadata, absorbs right and concatenates retained original spans. It cannot join a container or separator; code joins require matching code language tuples. Endpoint/empty and split-after-join behavior remain required. Both operations retain immutable source identities and all losing intentions.

A place operation applies only if dependencies succeeded; target/current versions match; parent is visible, enabled and an allowed container (or root); target is visible and not tombstoned; and the proposed parent is neither target nor its descendant. Remove target from its current siblings and insert before the named visible sibling under the new parent, or append. The before sibling must exist under that parent, match its version and differ from target. Consume only the target version, replacing it with the operation ID; container children retain their identities and internal order when their parent moves. Local invalid/cyclic/depth-exhausting targets reject the complete preparation before mutation. A remotely conflicting/ineligible operation remains a losing/recoverable intention under deterministic replay, not a guessed repair. Missing binary/version dependencies remain dormant under v3's rules.

Two operations on different targets can coexist; overlapping target versions and stale parent/before versions follow the documented replay eligibility and ranking. Concurrent move/move, move/edit and moves forming a potential cycle must converge under duplicate/reordered delivery. A hidden/absorbed/disabled parent causes its otherwise live children to project at root; their content is not silently swallowed. Tombstones and disabled original owners retain hidden source spans as recovery. Explicit subtree deletion, if implemented by a later command, names its complete prepared target set; a container tombstone alone is not implicit cascading deletion.

Block metadata on a derived split owner inherits the live left-owner tuple until explicitly overridden, as in v3. Checklist state differs: a new split owner defaults to unchecked; splitting a checked item retains left's check and gives right an unchecked default. Absorbed right state remains retained. Unknown and losing owner metadata stays dormant; it cannot duplicate character ownership.

## Code and separators

Extend the atomic block-presentation tuples to `["paragraph"]`, `["heading", level]`, `["code", language]`, and `["separator"]`. Heading level remains integral 1…6. Language is an ASCII string of at most 64 bytes matching `[A-Za-z0-9+._-]*`, including empty. Unknown valid JSON discriminants retain v3's opaque fallback; malformed known tuples reject complete admission/preparation.

Code is presentation on an editable owner, not a replacement original rich text. Preserve whitespace, blank lines, original characters, anchors and unknown attributes. Render existing rich marks dormant in code. New literal edits explicitly insert unmarked runs without inheriting adjacent marks; rich-format commands reject code targets before any partial mixed batch. Converting back to paragraph exposes the retained marks. Newline edits inside code remain literal text, not an automatic split into rich blocks. Code split/join is explicit and preserves matching language, original spans and identity; mismatched-language joins reject without mutation. Code-language changes are metadata-only atomic tuples.

A separator is a noneditable presentation on an empty owner. Conversion of nonempty text rejects rather than dropping/hiding user text. Preserve that owner's original identity and empty span; text/mark/split/join targeting the separator returns a typed unsupported-target result. Insert/delete/convert commands must prepare an accessible adjacent paragraph when no visible editable text owner would remain, reserving its fresh identity in the same transaction. Reject resource/identity failure before any live write; no partially committed separator that traps the document. Empty ordinary paragraph/heading/code owners count as editable.

## History, deletion and retained state

Immutable source registrations, nested text identities, container registrations and operation tuples are never removed/replaced to implement undo. `registry-entity-controls` permits reversible local history intents: an atomic enabled tuple hides/reactivates an original/container or disables/reactivates an operation. Permanent tombstones always win over enable. Disabled operations do not replay; their dependent intentions remain retained losing/dormant. Disabling a source preserves its original content as recovery; disabling a container follows the hidden-parent rule; re-enable restores visibility only when valid under the remaining graph. Unknown-yet-valid IDs in controls are retained dormant within the resource bound. Projection never writes enable flags.

Control conflicts use the pinned map tuple rule. Qualification covers disable/enable/duplicate/restore/concurrent control and dependency cases, including edited original content and stable anchors. This proves the history primitive, not selective history grouping. ENG-1.11 must exclude remote/restore/initialize origins, use explicit command group boundaries, limit text/metadata undo scopes so immutable registry/operation rows survive, and use these controls for structural creation/operation history. Undo after remote changes preserves the remote bytes and resolves affected content through the qualified projection; no pretend history by reseeding or copying a document.

## Admission and functional envelope

Retain v3's staging, exact-root/shared-type, immutable-row, binary decode and external recovery policy. Validate all new tuples, namespaces, container/text/origin membership, operation/control shapes and bounds before applying to the live replica. Replacement/removal of immutable original/container registrations, initial placements or operation tuples rejects. Mutable presentation/check/control tuples may change or become absent under their documented defaults. Known incompatible kinds/tuple shapes are not unknown extension data. An unresolved but valid parent/dependency retains its raw intent as specified; malformed values do not gain a fallback pass.

Retained originals plus containers total at most 4096; operations at most 4096; spans at most 8192; controls at most 8192. Hierarchy and dependency depth at most 128, iterative edge visits at most 16777216. Keep v3 limits for source UTF-8/UTF-16 totals, update/checkpoint bytes, JSON/binary depth, structs, IDs, cuts and allocation clocks. Typed resource-limit/recovery is atomic; no omitted nodes or partial mutation. These are functional ceilings, not performance qualification. List indentation accepts root depth zero through depth 128 and rejects a complete batch if any moved descendant exceeds it.

## Qualification and consumption

ENG-1.19 creates `core/fixtures/schema-v4/` and `core/crates/editac-core/tests/structural_profile.rs`: exact ten-root construction, descriptor and Rust/Yjs exchange; nested list/quote/container placements; ordered starts/modes/check state; original/derived owners; empty nodes; place/split/join interactions; hierarchy/cycle/orphan/deleted-parent behavior; mark/anchor identity; control history primitives; malformed/profile/epoch/resource rejection; both directions, seeded replicas, duplicate/reordered delivery and restore. Coverage compares visible tree, recovery, metadata and source identities, not merely binary agreement. Preserve and reuse ENG-1.8-P1's read-only validation evidence; adapt quote/container validation under this profile rather than treating it as persistence proof.

ENG-1.20 separately qualifies code/separator tuples and the complete literal-mark/whitespace/blank-line/conversion/empty-editable-neighbor matrix with the same exact descriptor and real Rust/Yjs exchange. Test invalid languages/levels/nonempty separator targets, code join compatibility, mixed-batch atomic rejection and concurrent metadata/remote edits. Its command-policy fixture is deterministic; no live provider calls.

ENG-1.21 integrates the exact qualified v4 profile in production create/restore/admission, hierarchical projection, anchors and shared prepared place/text/format/structural primitives. It reruns both qualification suites and required legacy/regression families with exact hashes/counts. It does not finish list/quote behaviors (ENG-1.8), code/separator command behaviors (ENG-1.9), move acceptance (ENG-1.10), or history grouping (ENG-1.11). Those parents use this contract and still meet every original criterion. Lists/quotes and code/separators cannot use an unqualified descriptor; the profile is not declared supported until both qualification receipts and the production integration pass. A failed or oversized boundary requires a precise controller repair/split proposal, not an unspecified request for another schema.

specs/schema-v5.md.text:
# Stable retained-structure presentation v5

Status: controller-authored correction for ENG-1.9-F1; qualification ENG-1.22 and production integration ENG-1.23 are pending. Preserve schema-v4, its descriptor/mappers and historical passing/failing evidence unchanged. This document does not assert compatibility or feature acceptance.

## Profile and version boundary

Schema `editac.registry.editor.v5`, profile `editac.yrs-yjs.editor.v5`; protocol version 1, update encoding 1, UTF-16 and the same pinned Yrs/Yjs/toolchain pair as [schema-v4.md](schema-v4.md). Retain v4's exact ten roots, value shapes, namespaces, bounds, containers, presentation/check/control metadata and immutable original-source identities, except the split/join tuples and replay rule explicitly changed below. The tuple change requires a new profile; no implicit v4 mutation, automatic migration, reseeding restore or mixed-epoch update. V4 readers reject the v5 envelope before live mutation. Legacy v4 presentation guards remain until an explicit separately authorized migration, which retains the old checkpoint and uses a new epoch.

## Immutable preparation witnesses

V5 ownership-operation values are:

- Split: `["split", leftOwner, leftVersion, spanIndex, sourceId, binaryRelativeCut, leftPresentation]`.
- Join: `["join", leftOwner, leftVersion, rightOwner, rightVersion, leftPresentation, rightPresentation]`.
- Place: the unchanged seven-field v4 tuple.

Presentation witnesses are complete immutable `Any::Array` / plain JavaScript array snapshots of the effective presentation observed by validated preparation: `["paragraph"]`, `["heading", level]` or `["code", language]`, with v4's exact known-value bounds. Separator, unknown/opaque or malformed witnesses reject; code join witnesses must both be code with identical language, otherwise both must be paragraph/heading. No independently merged witness fields, pointers to mutable metadata, or reconstruction from final presentation values. Operation records/witnesses remain immutable and consume the existing binary/JSON resource limits.

Local split/join preparation resolves current owner identities, versions, relative cuts, effective presentation and the whole command batch before mutation. It captures these witnesses and rejects separator/opaque/nonvisible/deleted/stale targets; newly incompatible code joins reject the whole batch. Preparation against current code presentation still obeys literal insertion and formatting rules. A later metadata-only command must never rewrite earlier witnesses or consume a structural version merely to preserve an existing operation.

Admission validates tuple arity, ID/version/cut shapes, witness values and witness compatibility, along with the existing root/graph/binary/resource constraints. It does not compare historical witnesses to current mutable block tuples: a checkpoint or reordered update can legitimately contain presentation changes authored after or concurrently with the operation. A witness is the operation's authored preparation declaration, not a cryptographic provenance proof. Transport/authorization cannot infer a historical local command snapshot from final CRDT metadata.

## Presentation-independent structural replay

Replay retains v4's deterministic operation ranking, dependency/version eligibility, enabled controls, tombstone policy, same-parent adjacency, container roles, source-relative cuts, hierarchy and span/recovery rules. Split/join editability and code compatibility are evaluated from the immutable witnesses, not current `registry-block-attributes` or inherited live tuples. Place eligibility uses structural identity/hierarchy, not presentation style. Malformed current metadata can still reject admission or require recovery; valid presentation changes do not retroactively change ownership.

An eligible join stays applied when its surviving owner changes code language, becomes paragraph/heading or acquires valid opaque presentation later. The absorbed owner's original text, dormant metadata and marks remain retained; it does not reappear merely because left's presentation differs. An applied split likewise survives later presentation changes on either owner, including empty-owner separator conversion when v4's command safeguard passes. Current presentation still controls rendering and future command admission. Controls, tombstones, structural version conflicts, newly arriving earlier-ranked structural intentions and unresolved/changed source cuts retain their qualified structural effects; this correction does not promise immutability against actual structural changes.

Converting a joined code owner to paragraph exposes its retained marks across all original sources without changing spans, parent, owner version, source identities or anchor routing. A code-language change is metadata-only. A mixed batch containing literal cross-source replacement/deletion and valid presentation conversion commits once after full staged validation. Newly incompatible split/join preparation or invalid metadata in that same batch rejects atomically. Do not satisfy positive conversion/language acceptance by returning PresentationConflict, skipping the joined-owner test or splitting/reseeding its text.

## Qualification and integration

ENG-1.22 creates `core/fixtures/schema-v5/` and `core/crates/editac-core/tests/retained_presentation_profile.rs`. Start from the preserved ENG-1.9-F1 production/Yjs reproducers. Prove both paragraph conversion and language change of joined multi-source code owners; dormant marks, literal LFs, cross-source replacement/deletion, parent/version/span/identity/anchor invariance; later presentation changes on split/derived/empty owners; unknown presentation retention; fresh mismatched-language/code-versus-ordinary/separator/opaque join rejection; malformed/forged-incompatible witness rejection; actual pinned bidirectional Rust/Yjs exchange, metadata-before/after/duplicate/reordered delivery, concurrent join/metadata, checkpoint restore and entity-control undo/redo. Preserve old v4 results as historical bounded behavior; neither rewrite its mapper nor label the old safety guard as positive acceptance.

ENG-1.23 integrates the exact qualified v5 envelope/tuple/admission/replay into production creation/restore and prepared editor commands. It reruns the original positive ENG-1.9-F1 test and complete blocks acceptance, plus qualification, editor profile, list/move/text/format/anchor/structural/history-primitive and legacy profile regressions. Scope the existing PresentationConflict regression explicitly to legacy v4; v5 must accept the qualified metadata-only cases while retaining whole-batch rejection for genuinely invalid/stale targets. Original ENG-1.9 remains unchecked until its full canonical suite and receipt pass in a subsequent bounded acceptance session. No new profile is advertised supported before exact source/descriptor hashes and zero-failure/zero-skip production evidence exist.

specs/modules-native.md.text:
# Extension modules and native preparation

## Portable extension contract

A registered module declares a namespaced type/version, validated attributes and content shape, commands, codecs and deterministic fallback. Freeze registrations before mounting a document. Dynamic JavaScript behavior is not portable Rust behavior; data-only custom marks and atoms must work without recompilation, while new editing semantics need shared engine work.

The document never contains executable callbacks, downloaded plugins or renderer code. Unknown type/version/renderer preserves original bounded data and displays a safe fallback. Invalid descriptors fail before any document mutation. Platform hooks render existing semantic content and do not own a second writable model.

Subscriptions filter changed kind/range/selection. Stable renderer views receive patches and dispose all owned resources. Asynchronous resolver results carry request identity and cancellation; a stale response cannot mutate the document. Modules do not scan the entire document on each transaction.

## First-party modules

| Module | Required behavior | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Slash | Local context trigger, accessible keyboard/touch menu, command invocation | Remote edits never open the menu |
| References | Host resolver, persistent target ID and label, cancellation | No implicit fetch merely from opening a document |
| Reorder | Keyboard and optional handle call one semantic move | Requires proven identity-preserving move policy |
| Images | URL/alt/dimensions metadata, host asset policy, fallback | Uploads/auth are host services |
| Tables | Bounded rectangle, simple cell editing and selection | No merged cells, spreadsheets or layout engine |
| Math example | Bounded LaTeX source, lazy safe renderer, error/source fallback | No full TeX or native typesetting claim |

Publish capabilities separately for read/edit/copy/Markdown/native. A source fallback is preservation, not a claim of native rendering parity. Disabled UI modules must be absent from minimal bundles; their data remains recoverable.

## Native preparation output

The first browser release does not require native SDK parity. The native roadmap proves the portable boundary and estimates the remaining work with evidence. Use a pinned UniFFI runtime/generator initially; measure copies and call count before freezing it. MPL-2.0 dependency licensing does not change the project's Apache-2.0 source license; retain required notices and review any modifications to dependency files.

ABI: opaque engine handle, explicit drop/dispose, batched commands and patches, stable UTF-16 units, relative async anchors, typed errors and cancellation, versioned schema/profile. Specify which executor/thread owns a handle; no arbitrary callbacks under a live transaction or lock. Expose owned buffers/snapshots, not borrowed Rust internals across FFI.

Build Swift and Kotlin headless fixtures using the same seed/snapshot corpus. Then use one real UIKit/TextKit control and one EditText/Editable control to probe range patching, selection and composition. Record unsupported mark/attachment behavior honestly. Never implement native support through a WebView.

Full native editor work remains a later separately scoped project: marked/composing text, autocorrect/dictation, OS keyboard, undo gestures, clipboard, accessibility, attachments, storage, lifecycle reconnect, packaging and real-device matrix. Binding generation alone proves none of these. Missing Xcode/SDK/device access has an explicit unblock condition and does not gate independent web tasks.

Sources: [UniFFI](https://mozilla.github.io/uniffi-rs/latest/), [UIKit TextKit](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/textkit), [Android InputConnection](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/inputmethod/InputConnection).

## Full native and library follow-ups

The preparation-only scope above applies to roadmap 09. Full requested SDK parity is delivered by [native-sdk-parity](native-sdk-parity.md) and roadmaps 16/17/18/22/23 for iOS, Android, macOS, Windows and Linux. [Extension-library](extension-library.md) and roadmap 21 supply portable public contracts and presenter conformance. Browser release remains independent, but the full-client milestone requires genuine mandatory native editing capabilities.

## Interaction and assistance follow-ups

The slash module follows [editor interactions](editor-interactions.md), qualified by INT-1.9 before browser release. Rich-content catalog-scale behavior remains in RCH-1.16. [Assistive input](assistive-input.md) defines an optional portable assistance descriptor and platform presenters in track 39; baseline accessible editing and native OS dictation remain required when it is absent.

specs/link-resolution.md.text:
# Public URL metadata and private reference resolution

Status: planned portable host/backend and web contracts, roadmap 26. Consume shared client/extension interfaces; do not replace their resolver, authorization or source ownership. Actual native/TUI presenter wiring is qualified in roadmaps 31–36.

## Service and data ownership

Expose distinct public-URL metadata and private-catalog ports through documented Rust/browser APIs. The host owns authorization, egress, credentials, caches and approved endpoints. The semantic core receives validated bounded records and invokes prepared commands; it never fetches URLs inside a transaction. Browser helpers call host ports rather than assuming arbitrary cross-origin HTML is readable.

Each request includes a request ID, principal/tenant context supplied by the host, locator, initiating action, node/document/epoch/revision, policy version and cancellation token. Response variants include available, unavailable, forbidden, missing, locked, unsupported, canceled and stale, with bounded safe display fields and freshness. URI text or response metadata never supplies trusted actor identity or grants access.

Public metadata records contain the requested/validated canonical URL, title, optional description, icon/image asset references, provider identity and fetched/expiry metadata. These are untrusted descriptions, not executable markup or proven ownership. Private records carry stable host target identity, capability-scoped display data and activation capabilities; they are not interchangeable with public webpage fetches.

## Automatic enrichment policy

Hosts explicitly select disabled, automatic-on-local-paste/insert, or explicit-refresh behavior. An enabled local paste policy may request title/favicon without another per-link prompt; the setting and its network behavior remain visible to the host/user. Opening/rendering a document, remote edits, recovery replay and history inspection initiate no requests. Imported links may show existing safe fallback without enrichment.

Capture URL/node/revision/request identity before lookup; bound requests and cancel obsolete work. Results cannot replace user-edited labels, resurrect deleted links or write into another document/session. Metadata display caches update without CRDT writes by default. A deliberate metadata commit uses the shared authorization/revision/history contract and makes any shared-label disclosure explicit. No automatic full-document link scan runs on ordinary edits.

An offline lookup returns cached metadata permitted by current policy or an honest unavailable state. Never infer an empty title means a deleted target. Negative-cache lifetime and retry/backoff are bounded, and canceled failures do not create noisy repeated network requests.

## Public URL admission and egress

Accept only configured HTTP(S) locators after standards-based normalization. Reject credentials in URLs, unsupported schemes, malformed hosts, overlong input and disallowed ports. Keep query strings/paths out of ordinary logs because they may contain secrets. Allowlist targets where the host's business flow permits it; a permissive public-web policy still requires protected-address checks.

Public resolution uses a dedicated host transport with no browser session cookies, ambient authorization headers or forwarded client credentials. Apply explicit connection/total timeouts, response-byte/decompression/redirect limits, content-type checks and bounded HTML parsing. Disable redirects by default. A host-enabled redirect path revalidates every hop and the actual resolved connection address before sending another request.

Cover loopback, private, link-local, reserved and metadata-service addresses in IPv4/IPv6, unusual numeric forms, DNS changes/rebinding and allowed-to-forbidden redirects. DNS validation must bind to the address actually used for the connection; checking one resolution and letting another unrestricted lookup connect is insufficient. Network egress policy supplements application checks. Do not disable those protections to resolve private internal links.

Title extraction reads bounded inert metadata/text only. Prefer declared Open Graph/title fields according to a deterministic policy, normalize display length/control characters and retain the original URL as fallback. Canonical URLs are advisory until validated; a page cannot rename document identity. Favicon discovery uses validated icon links and an optional bounded favicon fallback under the same policy. Icons/Open Graph images are independent untrusted URLs and pass identical egress, media-size and credential checks.

Return safe metadata or host-managed asset references. Rendering must not turn a rejected remote icon URL into a new unchecked browser request. Avoid third-party favicon lookups by default because they disclose visited document URLs. `no-cors` is not a way to read protected cross-origin pages, and a browser CORS failure does not authorize a more privileged fetch.

## Private internal targets and disclosure

Use a separate host-authorized catalog resolver for `ac://`, task/user/document references and configured private app links. Resolve only configured authorities and require current principal capability for target lookup, title/icon/preview and activation. A permission to read the containing document does not imply permission to read its targets. Hidden/missing outcomes follow the host's non-disclosing policy.

Cache private results by principal, tenant, authority, target and relevant permission/policy revision. Never reuse another user's or tenant's title/icon cache entry. Expiry, logout, account switching, revocation and key-lock events invalidate or hide previously resolved private display data. Offline use respects the cached-capability/lease policy; it does not promise instantaneous remote revocation.

Keep fetched private titles, icons and previews in per-viewer presentation/cache state by default. The CRDT retains target identity plus a neutral or explicitly user-authored label. Automatically writing a secret title into shared node attributes would reveal it to all readers of that document. Sharing resolved metadata requires an explicit host disclosure decision; test the actual recipient/document scope. No subsequent revocation can guarantee erasure of text already authorized and copied.

Private fetch credentials remain inside the host adapter; no URL, document attribute, preview, log or MCP result carries bearer credentials. E2EE lookup/export follows the authorized plaintext endpoint model; an opaque relay cannot resolve encrypted private metadata. Resolver output is content, not an instruction to run tools or follow additional URLs.

## Activation and presenters

Web/native/TUI presenters receive safe text, bounded asset references, freshness and supported actions. They expose cancellation/disposal, accessible labels, focus restoration, offline/locked/forbidden fallback and explicit activation. Headless fixtures define the same contract for all platforms; roadmap 26 implements web consumers and portable ports, not native controls.

Opening a reference rechecks current host activation capability. External browser/deep-link launch uses a validated action object, never shell command interpolation. Users can copy a safe locator without copying credentials. Custom reference triggers reuse existing extension registration and menu behavior; read-only permits authorized navigation while denying document mutation. Stale asynchronous results cannot change which target a click opens.

## Test and performance contract

Prepared resolver/network fixtures are the default; no real private services, user credentials or paid providers are needed. Verify no-call-on-open/remote/replay, local-paste policy, duplicate/canceled work, revised labels/deleted targets, malicious page/icon URLs, every denied egress branch and response limits. Denied requests must produce zero outbound transport calls.

Use two principals and two tenants to test cache isolation, target revocation, same-ID/different-authority collisions and private title/icon disclosure. Verify shared CRDT snapshots contain no automatically fetched secret title. Keep user-authored shared text intact; policy cannot retroactively classify it as an unpublished cache.

Measure local policy/filtering, cache-hit presentation and network wait separately. Reuse existing input/menu targets: network lookup does not block typing, commit, persistence or focus. Set finite concurrency/queue/response/media limits in the host configuration and prove they apply under bursts. Record cold/warm p50/p95/p99, request counts, cancellation and cache memory at exact fixture/build revisions. Dispose leaves no live request/subscription or stale private display state.

## Primary references

- [Open Graph metadata fields](https://ogp.me/)
- [HTML icon links and fallback](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#rel-icon)
- [oEmbed security considerations](https://oembed.com/)
- [Fetch and CORS constraints](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Fetch_API/Using_Fetch)
- [OWASP SSRF prevention](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Server_Side_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html)
- [MCP resource URI/capability model](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/resources)

specs/schema-v1.md.text:
# Registry schema v1

Status: frozen foundation contract, locally reconstructible; structural Rust/JS exchange is a separate FND-1.12 gate. This is not a production command API or a Tiptap document format.

## Scope and authority

Schema identifier: `editac.registry.v1`. The selected [structural policy](../decisions/002-document-structure.md) and passing `core/crates/editac-core/tests/structure_conflicts.rs` supply its semantics. One Yrs replica owns all committed content. Projection never writes repairs. The machine-readable seed and language mapping are in `core/fixtures/schema-v1/`; protocol metadata lives outside the CRDT as defined in [protocol-v1.md](protocol-v1.md).

Version 1 supports ordinary retained nodes and exactly one optional ownership pair: first `block-1`, second `block-2`, derived split owner `block-split`. A pair cannot be rebound or overlap another pair. Arbitrary pairs, repeated transformations, restoration of tombstones, compaction and production undo are not qualified. A document needing these operations requires a separately qualified schema revision; it must not silently reuse this descriptor.

## Exact roots and values

Create these five named root maps before the first write transaction. Empty root maps contain no update items; every receiver must request them with these exact shared types, even when absent from decoded bytes. There is no XML document root and no second document tree.

| Root name | Rust / JS shared type | Keys and values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `registry-parents` | `MapRef` / `Y.Map` | logical node ID → immutable string kind; known kinds `list`, `item` |
| `registry-texts` | `MapRef` / `Y.Map` | same node ID → nested `XmlTextRef` / `Y.XmlText` |
| `registry-placements` | `MapRef` / `Y.Map` | same node ID → one immutable array `[parentId, order]` |
| `delete-probe-tombstones` | `MapRef` / `Y.Map` | deleted logical ID → boolean `true`; absence means not deleted |
| `probe-split-join` | `MapRef` / `Y.Map` | optional sole key `pair` → one immutable ownership array |

The historical probe root names are deliberate wire names. Do not rename them during construction. `parentId` is an ID or sentinel `@root`; `order` is an integral Number in 0…4294967295 (Rust `Any::Number`, JS number). Place a complete tuple in one map write, never nested independently merged parent/order fields. Missing/malformed placement is projected as `[@root, 0]` while the original raw value remains retained. Other malformed root/value shapes require preserved recovery rather than a partial projection.

Each registered node has one persistent nested rich text. Insert it once; moves, deletion, splitting and joining never replace/remove/clone it. Its integrated CRDT identity is distinct from its logical map key. All inserted content in this profile is text, with JSON-compatible attribute values; rich-text runs retain their original attributes. Known fixture marks are boolean `bold`, `italic`, `code`, `underline`. Unknown kinds are opaque string values: retain their text, marks and placement, render a safe fallback, and do not treat them as list parents. Unknown mark names/JSON values remain on their original characters without extension fetch or execution. Opaque retention is required; semantic commands for unknown extensions are unsupported.

## IDs and creation

Logical IDs use ASCII grammar `[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}`. ASCII byte lexicographic order is the universal ID tie-break. `@root` is a sentinel, never a registered node. `block-split` is reserved for the derived owner and must not be a text/kind/placement registry entry. `block-1` and `block-2` are reserved pair members when `pair` exists. Fixtures also use fixed aliases `a`…`e`, `left`, `right`; the latter section aliases belong only to older disposable probes, not the v1 seed.

New ordinary IDs are `n-<client>-<counter>`, where each component is lowercase hexadecimal without leading zeros (zero is `0`). Client is the independent Yjs-compatible writer ID; counter is a writer-local monotonically increasing allocation counter, persisted with that writer session and never reused in the epoch. Use a fresh writer identity on restore; do not share a writer ID across live replicas. Check ID absence before insertion and reserve the ID with its node/text/placement in the same prepared transaction. Never resolve a collision by replacing an existing rich text; reject local creation, retain incoming conflicting bytes for explicit recovery. CRDT map convergence alone cannot detect every competing logical creation: production admission/collision guards remain required downstream. Fixtures use distinct fixed client IDs, not a production random-ID allocator.

## Ownership arrays and anchors

`pair` values are exactly `["original"]`, `["join"]`, or `["split", cutBytes]`. `cutBytes` is `Any::Buffer` / `Uint8Array`, containing a v1 encoded Yrs StickyIndex / Yjs relative position in the **first original text** with left affinity (`Assoc::Before` / association -1). It is not a JSON byte-number array, absolute offset, or copied text. The whole array is replaced atomically. Only local commands from `original` may transform; concurrent split/join writes resolve to the single integrated map value under the pinned CRDT conflict rule. Do not merge descriptor fields or choose by arrival time.

Resolve and validate the cut before mutation: UTF-16 offset 0…text length, outside surrogate interiors, resolvable in the first text. A right-affinity growing endpoint uses a type-relative anchor (`StickyIndex::from_type(..., Assoc::After)` / type endpoint association 0). Selections retain original source identity and affinity; projected owner and offset derive from the resolved source span. A deleted/unresolvable async target yields an explicit result, never an insertion at document end. Binary anchor interoperability is not established until FND-1.12 passes.

Ownership is a read:

- `original`: each pair member owns its entire original text and placement.
- `join`: first owner keeps its placement and concatenates spans of first then second original text. Second owner is absorbed; both shared texts and raw placements remain.
- `split`: resolve cut n in first text; first owns [0,n), `block-split` owns [n,length), second remains unchanged. Derived owner inherits first's parent and order + 1; reject local split at maximum order before mutation. Inserts at the cut go right under left affinity. Character deletion resolves the relative cut according to the pinned anchor semantics, not a stored integer.

Every character has exactly one span owner before visibility, including retained hidden content. Empty texts/ranges retain identities. Malformed/unresolvable descriptor, unsupported mode, missing pair texts, or out-of-range derived order sends the document to explicit preserved recovery; no fallback ownership is invented. With no `pair`, each ordinary node owns its own full text.

## Deterministic hierarchy and visibility

1. Read every retained logical node and its one integrated placement. Missing parent, unknown/non-list parent or malformed placement projects at root. Resolve cycles by detaching the smallest ASCII ID in each cycle. Iterative traversal visits at most N² edges; no repair update is emitted. A late valid parent can restore the stored placement.
2. Compute ownership spans. A tombstoned owner hides every span it owns. A tombstoned original source hides that source's spans even after ownership transfer. Hidden spans form explicit recovery content with marks and original identities; deletion never removes registry entries or causes automatic resurrection.
3. Transfer resolved placement to projected owners, including split's order + 1. A visible child whose parent is hidden/absorbed projects at root. Recovery keeps pre-visibility placement. Traverse visible owners in preorder, sorting siblings by numeric order then ASCII ID. With an order tie, `block-2` precedes `block-split`; split does not promise adjacency.

Known-deleted targets reject local edits during preparation; stale/offline edits merge into retained recovery text. Tombstones are permanent within this profile. Unknown content receives the same retention/visibility rules. Existing hierarchy family fixtures qualify orphan/cycle/late-parent behavior; composed fixtures qualify deletion plus ownership plus hierarchy for the fixed pair. More general command coverage is not implied.

## Reconstructing the seed

The v1 seed has `block-1` and `block-2`, both kind `list`, root placements 0 and 1, texts `a😀b` and `cאבd`, respectively. Format UTF-16 [1,3) with `bold:true` in first and `code:true` in second. Set `pair` to `["original"]`; tombstones are empty. Use seed writer 11 in deterministic fixtures. `core/crates/editac-core/tests/schema_profile.rs` constructs these five maps and typed values explicitly and compares the selected composed projection. `core/fixtures/schema-v1/mapping.mjs` constructs the same values with Yjs and demonstrates origin/admission mapping. Restored peers apply the one initializer's update; they do not independently rebuild this seed.

Construction checks establish local mapping consistency. Earlier `interop` checks establish disposable XML/text exchange only. Moves/deletes/overlapping edits, retained identities and anchors in this frozen mapping must still pass FND-1.12 before cross-language structural compatibility is claimed.

specs/verification.md.text:
# Verification and supported envelope

## Evidence contract

Every task adds or identifies its named deterministic check before running it. Planned test files/scripts in task contracts do not exist until implemented; a missing check is a failure, not permission to skip. Record exact command, revision, fixture seed/hash, executed/passed/failed/skipped counts and artifact path in progress. Rust name filters must execute at least one intended test. No paid inference or external model transport belongs in any check.

Use built-in Rust tests initially, Node's deterministic test runner for compiled JS adapters, and pinned Playwright for automated browser mechanics. Real OS IME, accessibility, native keyboards, autocorrection and dictation need a separately recorded manual/device matrix. Synthetic key events and Playwright WebKit do not establish full Safari or real-device input support.

## Fixtures

Task: 20 blocks/~10 KiB text. Long: 2,000 mixed blocks/~1 MiB. Large: 10,000/~5 MiB. Aged: long after 100,000 seeded edits. Adversarial: 250 KiB paragraph, fragmented marks, emoji/ZWJ/combining/RTL, nesting limits and wide tables. Multi-editor: 50 static previews, separately 1 and 10 active editors. Commit generators, seeds and expected semantic snapshots; record text bytes and serialized CRDT bytes separately.

## Provisional targets

These are retained design targets from the proposal and have no measured result yet. Pin actual hardware, browser/OS versions, CPU/network profiles and capability parity before making comparisons.

| Metric (p95 unless stated) | Desktop | Mid-range phone |
|---|---:|---:|
| Task preset JS+WASM+essential CSS, Brotli | 400 KiB | same artifact |
| Runtime/adapter JS, Brotli | 35 KiB | same artifact |
| Core ordinary edit | 1 ms | 2 ms |
| Input to visible update, controlled 60 Hz | 16.7 ms | 33 ms |
| Warm task activation | 50 ms | 100 ms |
| Warm long actual editability | 200 ms | 400 ms |
| Warm large actual editability | 750 ms | 1,500 ms |
| Matching preview first viewport | 50 ms | 100 ms |
| 10 KiB Markdown paste to formatted frame | 50 ms | 100 ms |
| 100 KiB Markdown paste to formatted frame | 150 ms | 300 ms |
| Local slash menu after ready | one frame | two frames |

Measure transfer, decode, compilation, instantiation, CRDT restore, DOM adoption, first accepted edit, p50/p95/p99, long tasks, memory plateau, peak paste memory, journal amplification and remote bursts. Warm includes local persistence restore; cold includes uncached assets and document transfer. Emit raw samples; summaries alone cannot establish a regression.

Qualify Task and Long as initial supported sizes. Large and Aged remain diagnostic stress fixtures until qualified. Missing a target requires a recorded release scope/architecture decision and honest published envelope. Data loss, silent import loss, divergent states, broken supported IME, corrupt undo, unsafe paste and stale-target overwrite cannot be waived as performance tradeoffs.

## Matrix and lifecycle

Automated target: Chromium, Firefox and WebKit versions pinned by the browser test lock. Manual release matrix specifies actual current desktop Chrome/Firefox/Safari and mobile Safari/Chrome versions and devices; unsupported combinations are explicit. Starting support claims are provisional until evidence exists.

Reuse suitable dev servers. Track PID, launcher, workspace, port and log for every task-owned server/browser; stop verified unused processes, verify listeners disappear, preserve other tasks' services. Record free disk before/after substantial sessions; remove only reproducible artifacts produced by that session when several GiB accumulated or less than 50 GiB remains. Preserve evidence and source.

## Interaction-specific qualification

The [interaction case catalog](../tests/editor-interaction-cases.md) is planned coverage, not a test report. INT-1.1 creates its executable index; each behavior task creates/runs its cases; INT-1.14 records actual OS/IME/dictation/screen-reader/voice-control evidence, including extension-disabled operation. Every mandatory case must resolve to an executed assertion or an actual device observation before support is claimed. Track 39 adds independent optional-assistance lifecycle and platform qualification; a mocked recognition transport proves only the integration contract. Baseline and optional capabilities have separate published results.

## Mobile web evidence and cost

Tracks 40/41 use [mobile web](mobile-web.md), the [baseline cases](../tests/mobile-web-cases.md) and [extension cases](../tests/mobile-extension-cases.md). Record browser engine/version, device/OS, keyboard/locale, mode (tab/installed app/embedded host), requested/observed viewport policy and optional capabilities. Touch emulation and desktop WebKit are mechanical checks, not mobile support or phone-performance evidence. Compare identical packed baseline/disabled/enabled profiles, with incremental bytes, geometry work, startup/input/scroll costs and teardown counts. Preserve the existing total targets; freeze the proposed mobile allowance before measurement. Optional absent APIs require working fallbacks; required editing failures cannot be waived as optional API limitations.

## Editing suite architecture and oracles

[The suite contract](editing-regression-suite.md) separates plan validation, real semantic commands, sequence/history, property/interleaving, synthetic browser replay, actual browser actions and OS/device evidence. The [manifest](../tests/editing-suite/suite.json) indexes all 195 catalog cases, fourteen guards and twelve representative recipes; a covers link does not prove every variant of a case. Expected state must be independent of the implementation and include selection/pending marks plus attributable effects. Track 42 adds guard negative controls, fixed clocks, bounded quiescence and seeded failure minimization. Later feature/device owners retain their acceptance gates; fixture validation alone never closes them.

specs/schema-v2.md.text:
# Versioned block metadata

Status: development contract for ENG-1.16; not qualified until its receipt passes. Schema v1 and its foundation evidence remain unchanged.

## Profile and admission

Use schema `editac.registry.blocks.v2` and profile `editac.yrs-yjs.blocks.v2`. Keep protocol version 1, update encoding 1, UTF-16 offsets and the foundation's pinned Yrs/Yjs dependencies. A schema version is not a Yjs update-encoding version.

The immutable external envelope has the fields defined in [protocol-v1.md](protocol-v1.md). Require an exact supported profile/schema pair and matching document/epoch before any live mutation. A v1 replica must reject this profile, not ignore its extra root or interpret its blocks as opaque v1 content. Wrong schema/profile/epoch, malformed tuples and unsupported shared types leave content, state vector and history unchanged. Preserve rejected user-owned bytes for recovery under the existing admission/resource policy.

No automatic or in-place v1 upgrade is authorized. New v2 documents initialize once; restores, including empty documents, never seed twice and use fresh writer identities. Any future explicit migration uses a new epoch and retains the original checkpoint. Legacy v1 construction, projection and admission fixtures must continue to pass.

## Exact storage

Retain the five roots, shared types, placements, nested rich texts, tombstones and bounded ownership descriptor defined by [schema-v1.md](schema-v1.md). Add root `registry-block-attributes`, a `MapRef` / `Y.Map`. Its keys are logical block owner IDs; each value is one complete immutable array value (`Any::Array` in Rust, a plain JavaScript array, never a nested shared `Y.Array`) replaced in a single map write:

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `["paragraph"]` | Paragraph presentation |
| `["heading", level]` | Heading presentation; integral numeric level 1 through 6 |

Add known immutable registry kind `block` for ordinary editable text blocks. Creation reserves kind, persistent nested rich text, placement and initial block tuple together. Changing paragraph to heading never changes the registered kind, clones the rich text or stores block state on a character. Existing `list`/`item` structural kinds retain their v1 meaning; they do not become paragraphs by relabeling. Formatting unsupported or opaque kinds returns a typed unsupported-target result before mutation. This gate does not introduce list/quote/code/separator metadata; their own tasks must define and qualify their contract extensions before using them.

An ordinary `block` without a tuple reads as paragraph, without emitting a repair update. An absent tuple differs from malformed data: wrong tuple type/arity, invalid heading level or a tuple attached to an unsupported registered kind requires explicit recovery on untrusted restore/admission. Unknown tuple discriminants with a valid array/JSON value shape are retained opaquely with a safe fallback; local commands cannot edit them or execute/fetch extensions. Unknown mark attributes retain the existing character-level policy.

Block metadata persists independently of text length. Empty blocks can be formatted, checkpointed and restored. Metadata changes are observable projection changes even when visible text is identical. Prepared mixed text-mark/block batches validate every target, tuple, resource limit and current state before one explicit-origin transaction; one invalid or stale target rejects the entire batch. Preserve the marks implementation and its existing rejection guarantees.

## Bounded ownership and metadata

This profile still supports only the v1 fixed ownership pair and transformations from `original`. It must not advertise arbitrary pairs or repeated transformations. ENG-1.17/1.18 qualify and integrate those operations under a separate profile; block qualification alone does not unlock general structural commands.

For a v2 pair, both original members have immutable kind `block` and each keeps its own metadata tuple. A derived split owner has no registered text/kind/placement entry. Its effective tuple is the explicit `registry-block-attributes["block-split"]` override when present, otherwise the first original owner's current tuple (including the paragraph default). This is a live inherited value until an explicit override is committed. The first owner keeps its tuple. A heading split therefore initially produces two headings of the same level, including empty left/right ranges.

For join, the first owner keeps its metadata; the absorbed second owner's tuple and original text remain retained for recovery. A tombstoned or absorbed target rejects local formatting; metadata does not resurrect it. A concurrent split-owner override delivered before its split descriptor is retained dormant. It becomes effective only if that owner exists; losing/unsupported structural branches do not synthesize visible owners. Unregistered IDs other than the reserved derived owner are invalid metadata targets.

Concurrent writes to the same owner replace the entire tuple under the pinned Yrs/Yjs map conflict rule: never merge heading type and level independently. Concurrent writes to different owners coexist. Duplicate/reordered delivery must converge to the same tuple, visible/recovery content and stable anchor outcomes. Projection is read-only.

## Required qualification

ENG-1.16 creates `core/crates/editac-core/tests/block_profile.rs` and `core/fixtures/schema-v2/` with one seeded initializer, a machine-readable descriptor and a reproducible Yjs exchange mapping. Its receipt must cover paragraph/heading switching; levels 1/6; invalid 0/7/fraction/string/tuple shapes; empty restore; concurrent atomic tuple conflicts; split inheritance/override; absorbed/deleted targets; unknown retention; mixed-batch rejection and exact profile/epoch rejection. Exercise both Rust-to-Yjs and Yjs-to-Rust plus duplicate/reordered delivery with real prepared updates, not mocked convergence assertions.

Record exact commands, nonzero test counts, zero unresolved failures/skips, source/fixture hashes and profile envelope in `architecture/evidence/engine-block-profile/`. Rerun initialization, projection, anchors, text/format commands and existing v1 structural interoperability after admission/projection changes. Publish no profile compatibility claim before that evidence exists. ENG-1.6 consumes the qualified mapping and still requires its complete original mixed-format acceptance.

specs/rich-content-extensions.md.text:
# Rich content extension contracts

Status: planned portable and web delivery, roadmap 25. Reuse roadmap 07 implementations and roadmap 21 public interfaces; this work adds the named gaps rather than replacing qualified modules. Full native/TUI integration consumes these contracts in roadmaps 31–36 and is not an upstream prerequisite.

## Ownership and public boundary

Rust remains authoritative for content, schema, commands, validation, source reconciliation and history. Highlight tokens, table layout, decoded media, menus and drag geometry are derived presenter state. Platform caches may be discarded without changing the document. Optional processing/presenter dependencies are absent from minimal consumers when disabled.

Expose each feature through the owning Rust crate and documented `@edit-ac/core`/`@edit-ac/web` exports. Reuse existing extension descriptors, command preparation, scoped subscriptions and presenter lifecycle. A new crate/package requires an explicit consumption/size reason. Define versioned feature records and capabilities for data preservation, view, edit, copy, source, accessibility and optional network activation.

Portable presenter ports carry stable node identity, content revision, source/profile, selection/readonly capabilities and bounded patches. Results carry request identity/revision; stale, canceled or disposed results cannot mutate or repaint a replaced target. Define prepare/apply actions separately from derived appearance updates. Publish fixtures that Swift/Kotlin/desktop/terminal presenters can consume without browser types.

## Code blocks and highlighting

Persist literal code and a validated language identifier. Highlight spans, grammar/theme caches and syntax trees never become collaborative marks or another writable document. Preserve unsupported labels and provide immediate plain-code editing when a language is unavailable, loading, over budget or disabled.

Qualify a maintained Rust-capable backend and exact grammar/query versions before selection. Tree-sitter is an initial candidate, not a promise of performance or coverage. Test Rust, TypeScript and JSON initially; every additional language names grammar license/version, bounds and evidence. Optional browser-only alternatives may be compared, but do not imply portable native tokenization.

Own backend code, grammar dependencies, caches and compile probes in the optional `editac-highlighting` Rust companion crate. It is independently consumed by native hosts and optional browser worker bindings; the semantic engine has no dependency on that runtime. Small descriptor/offset/span records may remain public engine contract types. Reuse existing npm package exports for optional loading until measured consumption justifies another npm package.

The highlighting port accepts immutable block text/edits plus prior cache identity and returns validated token spans and a cache handle. Cache keys include block/revision/language/grammar/query/theme versions. Test UTF-8-to-UTF-16 conversion, overlapping/invalid spans and multiline state changes. Incremental output must equal the selected backend's full recomputation for the same input. Bound retained trees/tokens and invalidate on identity/language/profile changes.

Browser workers are optional scheduling adapters, not owners of document state. Record startup, transfer, processing and DOM-application costs separately; coalesce obsolete requests, bound queues and terminate owned workers on disposal. Highlighting never delays input, local persistence or collaboration. Rendering preserves selection and leaves the active composing subtree browser-owned until safe reconciliation. A highlighting failure remains a visible plain-code fallback, not lost source.

## Table editing, layout and source formatting

Keep bounded rectangular tables and simple cells; merged cells, spreadsheet formulas and a general layout engine remain outside this contract. Extend the existing module with explicit row/column insert/remove, header/alignment, cell selection, keyboard movement and cell-range copy/paste commands where missing. Record behavior when deleting the last row/column and for readonly/invalid targets. Every accepted operation has one intentional undo group.

Commands use stable table/row/cell identities and the frozen structural concurrency policy. Qualify concurrent row/column changes, cell edits and deleted destinations. Deterministic core projection resolves invalid remote structures; presenters do not emit their own repair transactions.

Cache geometry/indexes per table and invalidate only affected tables/cells. A cell edit must not scan or rerender every table in the document. Native/TUI ports expose cell rectangles/selection and semantic navigation separately from browser DOM geometry. Copy/export preserves hidden/unknown bounded content or reports a recoverable limitation.

The Markdown table formatter is an explicit selected-table source operation. Use the retained source baseline and revision-checked reconciliation; preserve surrounding bytes, code spans, escaped pipes, alignment, empty cells and final-newline policy. Record the Unicode display-width policy used for aesthetic padding. Formatting is deterministic and idempotent on its own output, with one undo group. It does not normalize an entire file or run automatically on every cell edit.

## Attachment and blob lifecycle

Define file/image/media descriptors with stable host asset identity, bounded filename/media type/size/hash metadata, alt text/caption where applicable and a safe fallback. Temporary object URLs and expiring signed download URLs belong to presentation, not persistent shared identity. A filename, MIME declaration or hash alone does not grant download rights.

The host asset port handles authorize, ingest, read/cache, publish, resolve URL, cancel and release-reference operations with explicit capabilities. Upload/account/storage products remain host responsibilities. Define local-only, queued, available, failed, missing, revoked and locked outcomes, including what other replicas display before bytes become remotely available. Asset commit and document update receipts remain distinct.

Journal resumable local work and bound blob/cache/outbox storage. Crash, full disk, auth expiry, offline reconnect and deletion during upload preserve recovery data without resurrecting deleted nodes. Idempotent host operation IDs prevent duplicate upload intent; transport retry semantics are explicit. Shared binary deletion/garbage collection requires host ownership/refcount policy rather than an editor deleting data on every removed node. E2EE ports preserve the security profile across originals, thumbnails, caches and exports.

## Image, file and embed presentation

Images enforce encoded-byte, decoded-pixel, dimension and concurrent-decode limits. Validate the actual media type under host policy; handle malformed/SVG/animated content explicitly. Render alt text and missing/offline/locked fallback. Dispose object URLs, observers, decoders and requests. External image loading requires host asset policy; parsing/opening a document does not authorize arbitrary URL fetches.

File attachments expose accessible filename/status/size and an explicit host-authorized open/download action. Clipboard/source export uses the declared stable identity/fallback and reports unavailable binary data. Native attachment view and terminal fallback records are part of the public presenter contract, not an assertion that those presenters already ship.

PDF export is a separate requested output capability. An attached PDF remains an opaque file asset; optional host preview is not PDF import, OCR or conversion into editable content. The semantic core requires no PDF reader. Do not add a PDF ingestion prerequisite to attachment handling.

Embeds store a bounded URL/provider identity and safe fallback, never executable HTML/code. Separate a metadata card from an activated interactive embed. Hosts register allowlisted presenter templates and an isolated/sandboxed activation policy; raw oEmbed/provider HTML never enters the editor DOM. Apply the [link resolver contract](link-resolution.md) to metadata and secondary media URLs. Roadmap 25 uses prepared resolver fixtures; actual resolver integration and native/TUI presenters are qualified downstream. Unsupported/offline/readonly modes retain identity and safe content.

## Slash, references and reorder

Extend the existing slash menu with explicit trigger context, code/literal exclusions, IME lifecycle, selection replacement and query-length/result-count bounds. Filtering is scoped to current input context. Focus restoration, escape, empty/error states, touch/pointer selection and screen-reader labels are tested; remote edits/replay never open the menu. Async providers follow the shared cancellation/revision contract.

Custom references retain stable target identity and user-authored fallback text. Their presenter consumes the host resolver's public/private/forbidden/missing/locked outcomes, without inventing target access or sharing private titles. Lookup, disclosure and cache policy live in [link-resolution.md](link-resolution.md). The feature supports configured `@`, `[[` or other bounded triggers through the existing registration interface, with plain-text fallback and explicit activation.

Block pointer reorder uses a derived drag session: threshold, hit testing, auto-scroll, valid destination, cancellation and current target anchors. Hover does not mutate CRDT state; final acceptance prepares one semantic move and one history group. Preserve content identity and selection under concurrent edits/deletion. Provide keyboard movement and a simple click/tap alternative such as Move before/after; keyboard alone does not replace the non-drag pointer alternative. Announce destination/result through platform accessibility ports.

## Measurement and qualification

Use production artifacts and fixed hardware/browser/toolchain profiles from [verification.md](verification.md). No numbers below are measured results. Retain failed samples and make a measured accept/revise decision before publishing support claims. Record p50/p95/p99, exact fixture hashes, 100 warm samples, separate cold loads, main-thread/worker/transfer/apply costs, bundle bytes and memory/DOM/token counts.

| Area | Fixture and initial acceptance target |
|---|---|
| Input | Preserve existing p95 visible-update targets of 16.7 ms desktop / 33 ms phone; optional presentation never gates a commit |
| Highlighting | 10/100 KiB code, 250 KiB long line, 100 small blocks and language/theme churn; proposed main-thread decoration slices <=4/8 ms; yield or plain-code fallback beyond qualified limits |
| Tables | 20x10 interactive and 100x20 stress tables, many unrelated tables, long/Unicode cells; input targets plus counters proving only affected table/cells are invalidated |
| Menus | 500 deterministic local commands/results; existing one-frame/two-frame p95 ready-runtime target; host lookup latency separately visible |
| Reorder | 2,000-block fixture with bounded geometry work and proposed 16.7/33 ms pointer-frame p95; no update during hover and one accepted move |
| Assets | Bounded request/decode concurrency, offline/failure fixtures and repeated disposal; no unbounded queues, object URLs or retained subscriptions |
