Measure full highlight/format latency separately from input. Attribute >50 ms long tasks in ordinary-edit fixtures. A worker is not proof of responsiveness. Minimal disabled consumers must exclude optional grammar/presenter assets and issue zero requests for them. Device IME/accessibility/native rendering requires downstream real-platform evidence.

## Primary references

- [Tree-sitter highlighting](https://tree-sitter.github.io/tree-sitter/3-syntax-highlighting.html) and [incremental parsing](https://tree-sitter.github.io/tree-sitter/using-parsers/3-advanced-parsing.html)
- [Shiki browser performance guidance](https://shiki.style/guide/best-performance)
- [ProseMirror table command/cache precedent](https://github.com/ProseMirror/prosemirror-tables)
- [WAI-ARIA suggestion pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/) and [non-drag pointer alternative](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/dragging-movements.html)
- [oEmbed response/security contract](https://oembed.com/)

## Mobile browser integration

Track 25 continues to own portable semantics and existing presenters. [Track 41](../roadmaps/41-mobile-web-extensions.md) adds the [mobile extension cases](../tests/mobile-extension-cases.md) after those capabilities exist: keyboard-open menus, native selection coexistence, touch table/code controls, cancelable drag/resize with tap alternatives, file/camera/share fallback and media resource teardown. Reuse [mobile web](mobile-web.md) ports from track 40; do not add viewport or gesture policy to Rust. The optional integration does not gate baseline mobile editing.

specs/schema-v3.md.text:
# General retained-source ownership v3

Status: locally qualified disposable representation for ENG-1.17; see [the matching receipt](../evidence/engine-ownership-profile/receipt.json). Production integration remains ENG-1.18. This is no performance, persistence, deployment or publication claim.

## Envelope and exact roots

Schema `editac.registry.structure.v3`, profile `editac.yrs-yjs.structure.v3`; protocol 1, encoding 1, UTF-16, Yrs 0.28.0 small-client, Yjs 13.6.33. Exact immutable protocol-v1 envelope with distinct document/epoch, externally stored initialized flag and fresh live writer IDs. No automatic migration, mutation of v1/v2, or reseeding restore.

Seven root Y.Map / MapRef types: `registry-parents` maps original ID to immutable `block`; `registry-texts` maps original ID to persistent nested Y.XmlText / XmlTextRef; `registry-placements` maps original ID to atomic `["@root", integral order]`; `delete-probe-tombstones` maps original/derived owner ID to true; `registry-block-attributes` uses the v2 immutable JSON-array tuples; `registry-ownership-ops` maps unique operation ID to immutable atomic array; `registry-owner-origins` maps original ID to true (explicit original-owner membership). No `probe-split-join` root in this profile. This qualification has ordinary block kinds only; future structural kind extensions require their own contract/qualification.

Original IDs are `n:<writer>:<counter>`, operation IDs `o:<writer>:<counter>`, with decimal positive integers without leading zero, writer <= 4294967295, counter <= 4294967295. Allocate counters monotonically in persisted writer sessions, never reuse live writer identity. Original and operation namespaces are separate. A split's new owner is its operation ID; no text/kind/placement is created for it.

## Atomic operations and deterministic replay

`["split", leftOwner, leftVersion, spanIndex, sourceId, binaryRelativeCut]` or `["join", leftOwner, leftVersion, rightOwner, rightVersion]`. Initial versions are `"base"`; a successful operation sets all surviving affected owner versions to its own ID. Split left survives; new right has that version. Join left survives, right is absorbed. Cuts use encoded Yjs relative position / Yrs StickyIndex, affinity Before (-1), attached to the named original text. spanIndex identifies an exact span in a multi-source owner, including empty spans. A split partitions that span at its current resolved cut, retains both empty sides, and distributes preceding/following spans. Join concatenates the adjacent visible owners' spans. No text writes, cloning or delete/reinsert implement structure.

Dependencies are all non-base version tokens. Validate the complete graph without recursion; reject cycles. Missing dependency records are retained dormant, not applied or repaired. Rank known records topologically: depth (base depth 1), then numeric writer, then numeric counter. Process that total order once. An operation applies only when all dependencies succeeded, its target versions match, targets exist, are not tombstoned, and joins are adjacent. Otherwise retain its ID and tuple as a losing/recoverable intention; descendants remain losing/dormant. Independent pairs commute. Concurrent overlapping intentions choose the first eligible operation in the documented order, never arrival order or a merge of tuple fields. A newly arrived earlier-ranked intention can change the read projection; the operation log and original content are retained.

A missing-source or unresolved cut (including absent binary dependency) is dormant/recoverable. A resolved cut in a different text, wrong affinity, surrogate interior or outside its identified span is invalid and rejects admission. Text deletion collapses relative boundaries; empty spans survive. Concurrent insertion exactly at a Before cut belongs to the right span; inserts before/after it route by the relative boundary. Structural content uses existing marks on the original shared text; projection slices attributed runs in UTF-16 and never writes repairs.

## Presentation, anchors, deletion and recovery

Initial owner order is `(placement order, numeric original ID)`; successful split inserts immediately after left; join requires adjacency. Original tuple default is paragraph. A derived owner uses its explicit tuple or recursively the live tuple of the split's left owner; inheritance terminates at an original. Join preserves left tuple, retains absorbed right tuple. Dormant/losing derived overrides remain retained. Unknown JSON tuple discriminants and original character marks stay opaque; no extension execution/fetch. Local formatting of unknown or nonvisible owners is unsupported.

Tombstones monotonically hide owner IDs. They do not delete texts or metadata. Replay refuses an operation targeting a tombstoned owner. A tombstoned derived owner still exists if its successful producing split exists; its spans are recovery content. A deleted original prevents its lineage operations, retaining the original source as recovery. Projection emits ordered visible owners and deleted owners with spans, plus original texts/tuples, complete retained operation intentions (binary cuts represented as byte arrays in JSON), and operation outcomes for recovery. Unknown tuples retain their raw value alongside an explicit paragraph presentation fallback. Absorbed owner metadata and losing intentions are retained, but do not duplicate character ownership. Every retained source UTF-16 character belongs exactly once to a visible or deleted/recoverable span; empty spans own no characters.

Anchors remain binary positions in the original text. Resolve first to original source/offset, then to current visible/recovery span owner. Interior points have one owner. At shared boundaries Before chooses the earliest span ending there; After chooses the latest span starting there, with deterministic owner/span order for empty ties. Return deleted for tombstoned ownership, unresolvable for missing identities, never silently redirect. Marks and structural changes preserve original integrated branch IDs.

## Admission and resource envelope

Check exact external envelope/initialized state before decoding. Reject >16 MiB update/checkpoint; stage on a disposable replica, validate exact root names and types, all atomic tuples/text types/IDs/placements/metadata/tombstones and operation graph, then apply once under explicit origin. Compare existing immutable original kinds/origins and operation values; replacement/removal is invalid. Missing Yrs binary dependencies require explicit recovery rather than live mutation. Retain rejected user-owned bytes/envelope externally; no unbounded attacker storage. No profile fallback or migration.

Bound projection/admission to 4096 original sources, 4096 operations, 8192 owner spans, 1 MiB UTF-8 source text total, 262144 UTF-16 units per source, graph depth 128, JSON tuple depth 32, 96-byte IDs and 256-byte cuts. Decode additionally caps nested binary Any depth at 32, each container at 8192 entries, total Any values and structs at 262144, and unsigned u32/usize allocation/clock fields at 2097152 before allocation; larger clocks are outside this probe envelope. Graph ranking is iterative O(operations squared), capped at 16777216 dependency visits; span coverage checking is bounded by these limits. Command preparation must consume these same limits and validate current versions/anchors before one explicit-origin commit (ENG-1.18). This is a functional resource ceiling, not a latency/performance claim. Exhaustion produces typed resource-limit/recovery, never partial state or silent omission.

## Alternatives

Copying rich text on each split loses integrated identity and concurrent edit routing. One global replacement descriptor gives atomic conflicts but cannot merge disjoint pairs or retain repeated branches. Independently merged per-owner span fields can overlap or orphan content. The selected operation log preserves source identity, serializes only overlapping intentions deterministically and retains losing intentions; it trades bounded replay/history cost for explicit recovery. Rejected alternatives are design comparisons, not falsely reported executed probes.

specs/web.md.text:
# Browser adapter contract

Status: development contract; real input support requires browser and device evidence.
Scope: framework-independent web editor plus a thin React lifecycle wrapper.
Public packages use the `@edit-ac` npm organization.
No full native editor parity is required for the initial web release.

## Mounting and state

- One editor handle owns one Rust/WASM document handle and one coherent editing surface.
- Use a continuous contenteditable text flow with semantic block/inline mappings.
- Do not create a separate editable root for every paragraph.
- The imperative adapter owns DOM patches, selection mapping and input listeners.
- React mounts/destroys the handle and subscribes to scoped state; it does not render the document tree.
- Ordinary edits stay on the browser thread with the authoritative engine.
- Workers may prepare large parsing/export jobs; they do not mediate every keystroke.
- Multiple mounts reuse WASM initialization where safe, while retaining distinct replica identities.

## WASM distribution

Use an explicit browser ES-module build and asynchronous initialization contract.
The initial candidate is wasm-bindgen 0.2.129 with matching CLI and wasm-pack 0.15.0.
Keep crate, generator and generated artifacts version-compatible and reproducible.
Ship the required `.wasm` file in the packed package and expose a host-controlled asset URL/init option.
Avoid implicit DOM access during module import so SSR hosts can load the package safely.
SSR import safety does not mean the editor can mount without a browser.
Test package exports/types and the packed tarball from an independent consumer directory.
Test a bundler host and direct browser asset loading; document CSP, MIME and CDN requirements.
Generated package metadata must not overwrite maintained public exports, license or publication settings.
Report complete JS, WASM and essential CSS bytes, including transitive editing dependencies.

## Lifecycle and loading

`visible` means a content projection has been displayed.
`ready` means authoritative recovery, input handlers, selection mapping and persistence attachment are complete.
`localCommitted` identifies an update whose local storage transaction completed.
`remoteCommitted` identifies an update with a durable service receipt.
These signals are distinct; showing a preview does not authorize editing it.

Restore a checkpoint plus bounded journal tail before accepting edits.
Adopt a preview only when its document/session, schema and revision metadata match recovered state.
If preview and recovery disagree, render recovered state before enabling input.
Never re-import initial Markdown/JSON into an existing document because the network is slow.
Initialization failure leaves an accessible read-only/recovery view with a visible error.
`flush({target: 'local'})` resolves after pending local commits or rejects with a typed storage error.
Destroy must settle or explicitly reject pending work and remove all listeners/observers/subscriptions.
Document whether failed persistence requires recovery export before a host discards the handle.

## Input routing

Handle `beforeinput`, `input`, composition events and a bounded MutationObserver fallback.
`beforeinput` is not always present or cancelable; check the actual event before preventing default.
Use semantic commands for structural operations and browser-native insertion where validated.
Maintain an origin/suppression mechanism for adapter-generated DOM changes.
Reconcile only the affected semantic range; one browser edit must not be committed twice.
Do not serialize the whole document or scan all formatting on the typing path.
Do not synchronously invoke networking, Markdown export or React document rendering from input handlers.
Honor read-only state in keyboard, paste, drag/drop, composition and command paths.
Selection-only changes emit scoped selection state without document updates.

Heading-end Enter uses the atomic `headingEnd` engine command qualified by WEB-1.14 under [the engine contract](engine.md#atomic-heading-end-enter). WEB-1.8 applies the resulting stable caret and qualifies the full keyboard suite. Separate live split/format commits or guessed generated owner IDs do not satisfy that behavior.

## Composition gate

The browser temporarily owns its active composing DOM subtree.
Remote updates may change the authoritative core, but must not replace the composing subtree underneath IME.
Capture composition anchors and the affected text/selection before it starts.
Reconcile committed composition against current core state using the proved anchor policy.
Do not convert intermediate IME events into independent typing/history groups.
If the target disappears, preserve composed text and report a recoverable conflict instead of redirecting it.
Define cancellation, blur, compositionend ordering and remote-overlap handling in the input ADR.
The ADR must specify whether intermediate composition is committed or buffered, with matching fixtures.
Do not select a policy by assuming all engines deliver the same event sequence.
No supported-IME claim is allowed until real OS input checks qualify the policy.

Required composition cases include Japanese/Korean/Chinese input, accents/dead keys, emoji and replacement selection.
Test remote insertion before/inside/after composition and remote deletion of its block.
Test paste, undo, blur, read-only transition and destruction during a composition.
Automated event fixtures cover regressions; synthetic events do not replace real-device evidence.

## Selection, navigation and DOM patches

Convert DOM positions to UTF-16 core positions through explicit mapping functions.
Preserve anchor/focus direction and affinity across incremental patches.
Use relative anchors across asynchronous operations and remote updates.
Test cross-block selection, empty blocks, hard breaks, inline atoms, lists and noneditable attachments.
Support keyboard navigation and screen-reader semantics through normal document structure.
Patch changed nodes/spans; do not replace the full editing subtree after every transaction.
Renderer caches are disposable derived data and must rebuild from core state.
Keep user selection stable when unrelated blocks change.
Avoid true viewport removal until selection, find, copy-all, accessibility and IME behavior are qualified.
Layout containment/deferred decorations must be measured and must not hide editable content from access tools.

## Clipboard and drag/drop

Follow the deterministic import precedence and safety policy in [formats.md](formats.md).
Paste prepares a single semantic edit and forms one explicit undo group.
Oversized preparation captures an anchor and supports cancellation/stale-target detection.
Pasting into code is literal; a visible plain-text paste command remains available elsewhere.
Drag/reorder UI invokes a semantic move only after the structural schema gate passes.
Cross-editor fragments are untrusted versioned input and use the same schema/resource checks as imports.
Do not execute embedded HTML handlers, document code or URLs during preview/import.

## Persistence and host events

IndexedDB adapter callbacks occur after transaction completion.
Surface quota/permission/closed-database errors and retain in-memory recovery content where possible.
Strict IndexedDB durability remains a hint; document its actual browser guarantee.
Do not depend on unload handlers for persistence or advertise universal power-loss survival.
Subscribers receive changed ranges, origin, revision/update metadata or selection state.
Full-document JSON/HTML/Markdown exports are explicit host actions, not implicit save callbacks.
Presence is throttled and ephemeral; it cannot delay local input or local persistence.
Attaching/detaching a transport must not replace the existing document or alter schema semantics.

## Browser qualification and performance

Record exact Chromium, Firefox and WebKit versions and OS/device versions in every release report.
Pin the automated browser toolchain separately from manual Safari/IME device evidence.
Measure first display and first accepted edit independently, including recovery and WASM startup.
Measure small/long/aged documents, paste peak memory, remote bursts and repeated mount/destroy.
Original roadmap budgets remain proposed targets until a reproducible report accepts or revises them.
Use feature-equivalent comparison fixtures and include optional-module bytes explicitly.
Keep failing/skipped evidence and a published supported/unsupported input matrix.
Close test browsers and temporary servers; preserve only explicitly requested previews.

## Primary references

- [Input Events composition/cancelability](https://www.w3.org/TR/input-events-2/)
- [Observed beforeinput browser constraints](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/beforeinput_event)
- [wasm-pack build targets](https://rustwasm.github.io/docs/wasm-pack/commands/build.html)
- [IndexedDB durability](https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/)

## Everyday interaction acceptance

[Editor interactions](editor-interactions.md) defines Enter/Shift+Enter, selected and pending formatting, contextual Tab, platform navigation, Unicode/whitespace, slash controls and non-keyboard replacement. Use its [case catalog](../tests/editor-interaction-cases.md) for browser input work. Track 38 closes this coverage before browser release; it does not replace the baseline tasks or their engine/storage prerequisites. Baseline OS dictation and screen-reader editing remain mandatory with optional extensions disabled. [Assistive input](assistive-input.md) adds optional host-controlled presentation through track 39.

## Mobile web and touch

[Mobile web](mobile-web.md) defines native touch selection/scroll preservation, mobile keyboard/replacement events, focus/command access, viewport/keyboard occlusion, capability fallbacks and the incremental cost gate. Track 40 and its [59 cases](../tests/mobile-web-cases.md) qualify the baseline before browser release. APIs such as VirtualKeyboard, keyboard layout/lock and EditContext are progressive or experimental capabilities with explicit fallback; they are not universal browser prerequisites. Track 41 qualifies richer extension presenters separately. Real mobile browser modes/devices remain distinct from emulation and native SDKs.

## Regression guard integration

Apply G01–G14 in [the editing suite](editing-regression-suite.md) when implementing input, selection, composition, patching and module event ownership. Correlate actual intents across notifications without deduplicating identical deliberate text; suppress only identified renderer echoes. Capture semantic selection/pending-mark intent before preparing a compound command, and publish callbacks after commit/lock release under a declared queue/rejection policy. WEB input implementation requires the qualified composition ADR from WEB-1.13's real-DOM/real-engine protocol probes, before WEB-1.4. Track 42 later reuses that evidence and proves the shared driver and guard assertions against the completed adapter before interaction qualification. Native IME/device support remains separately qualified.

specs/ecosystem-maintainability.md.text:
# Maintainable ecosystem contracts

Status: planned strengthening of the existing Rust-first architecture. This is a set of executable boundaries, not a new framework or runtime.

## Dependency direction and ownership

| Layer | Owns | May depend on | Must not import |
|---|---|---|---|
| Semantic engine | Schema, identity, prepared commands, anchors, incremental patches | Qualified CRDT and small deterministic primitives | DOM, OS UI, HTTP, host auth, MCP, cloud SDK, PDF/layout/highlighting runtime |
| Portable companions | Session/recovery, Markdown reconciliation, diff, extension descriptors | Engine contracts and explicit store/transport ports | A second authoritative document or platform globals |
| Optional services | Highlighting, conversion, link resolution, security profiles | Bounded snapshots/patches and declared host ports | Direct mutable engine internals or ambient credentials |
| Client adapters | Web/native/TUI input, view, permissions UI, file pickers | Public portable contracts and optional providers | Another platform's renderer or duplicated semantic policy |
| Reference cloud host | Membership/catalog, durable updates/assets, receipt service | Versioned wire and storage ports | Client UI or authority inferred from document content |
| Public docs/demo | Learning material and packed SDK consumers | Immutable public artifacts and release profiles | Private workspace imports or a second editor implementation |

A cloud host may run all service boundaries in one process. Split deployment only for measured operational need. Share deterministic contract fixtures, not cross-repository source aliases. Keep the existing three npm SDK boundaries until an independently consumed optional package earns a separate release surface.

## One compatibility and capability vocabulary

Define a small versioned `contracts/capabilities.schema.json` and `contracts/profiles/` registry in core. It records semantic schema, update/sync profile, extension descriptor versions, FFI/API version, source dialect, converter direction/fidelity, platform and qualified resource envelope. Each entry references immutable implementation/package and evidence revisions. These files describe versions; document content cannot install providers or enable privileged operations.

Distinguish available, enabled, authorized and qualified capabilities. Permission and principal-specific availability remain runtime host answers, never trusted from imported documents or peer advertisements. Fail unsupported writes explicitly and preserve bounded unknown data for reads/copy/export where possible.

Avoid parallel inventories: adapt existing `native/<platform>/capability.json` and release-profile checks to the shared schema, then generate public support tables and demo controls from the same reviewed release record. Manual qualification evidence remains explicit; a generated green table cannot manufacture it.

## Asynchronous service contracts

Every heavy service uses bounded inputs, stable document/session identity, expected revision or content hash, cancellation, deadline and a typed result. Apply only after permission and revision revalidation. Dispose workers/subscriptions and discard stale results. Highlighter spans, link metadata and conversion previews are derived caches; they cannot become competing writable state.

Set per-service concurrency, byte/item/decompression/pixel/depth limits, queue admission and recovery behavior. Measure preparation, transfer, apply and rendering separately. Worker execution does not remove copy cost or UI layout cost. Do not run expensive work merely because an unrelated block changed.

## Compatibility and release maintenance

Test exact supported previous/current combinations for schema, wire, extension descriptors, public JS/Rust APIs and native ABI. Reject unsupported versions with actionable recovery/export options. Upgrade and rollback fixtures must account for persisted data; reverting a package alone does not reverse a schema migration.

Build consumers from packed/released artifacts on clean workspaces. Check imports and Cargo feature graphs so disabled optional services and heavy dependencies do not enter minimum clients. Pin executable tooling/fixtures, retain licenses/notices and check known advisories at release without claiming that a clean advisory scan proves safety.

Keep dependency choices in short decision records with verified API, target, license, bundle and maintenance evidence. The choice gate must block on missing evidence, not silently choose an unqualified substitute. Avoid invented universal provider interfaces: the common ports are the actual repeated session, asset, resolver, conversion and lifecycle contracts.

## Performance, accessibility and diagnosis

Use the existing verification envelope plus feature-specific fixtures from roadmap25. Capture raw p50/p95/p99, long tasks, incremental invalidation size, memory plateau, active worker count and cold/lazy load bytes. Set reviewed release limits before advertising a profile; do not silently raise them after a failed run.

Require keyboard, touch, screen-reader and non-drag pointer paths where relevant. Platform appearance can differ while semantic capability remains test-equivalent. Record real device/OS input separately from deterministic fixtures.

Observability records bounded operation IDs, error codes, queue/durability state and timings. Redact document text, titles, URLs with credentials, tokens and keys. No live LLM/provider calls or synthetic paid inference are necessary for architecture fitness checks.

## Mobile web overhead boundary

[Mobile web](mobile-web.md) freezes an incremental baseline allocation within existing total limits; MWB-1.9 and MWX-1.8 own packed baseline/disabled/enabled cost evidence. FIT loading and budget checks consume these receipts where the mobile profile is claimed. The engine remains platform-neutral, optional APIs/dependencies load on demand, idle work is event-driven and per-frame geometry work is bounded. Budget failures require decomposition or an explicit recorded budget decision while preserving essential accessible editing.

## Editing boundary fitness

Track 42 tests [fourteen regression guards](editing-regression-suite.md) at existing command, input, renderer, history, normalization and lifecycle boundaries. Compound preparation, resulting selection and post-transaction notification are explicit capability gates; existing separate primitives cannot be silently composed into a purportedly atomic edit. Reuse production public boundaries with test-only instrumentation, maintain independent oracles and keep the harness out of shipped SDK bundles.

specs/mobile-web.md.text:
# Mobile web editing and platform capabilities

Status: development contract; device/API support and performance require qualification.
Scope: the web SDK on phones, tablets and touch-capable computers, including mixed touch/pen/mouse and hardware keyboards. This does not qualify the separate native SDKs. [Platform research](../evidence/mobile-web-platform-research.md) and [touch/extension research](../evidence/touch-extension-research.md) record sources and compatibility limitations.

Reuse [everyday interaction semantics](editor-interactions.md), [browser ownership](web.md), [extension contracts](extension-library.md) and [performance targets](verification.md). [Track 40](../roadmaps/40-mobile-web.md) adds the baseline mobile browser surface and release evidence. [Track 41](../roadmaps/41-mobile-web-extensions.md) qualifies richer optional presenters without making them prerequisites of basic mobile editing. The [baseline cases](../tests/mobile-web-cases.md) and [extension cases](../tests/mobile-extension-cases.md) are planned tests, not support claims.

## Keep the shared core small

| Layer | Required responsibility | Admission boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Rust semantic core | Prepared commands, stable anchors, command applicability, directional selection, Unicode boundaries, history and scoped patches | Add a primitive only for a missing reusable semantic operation; qualify schema/ABI changes first. Viewport, pointer, keyboard geometry and browser permission state stay outside Rust |
| Required web adapter | Native editable input/selection, minimal touch-safe focus/scroll integration, bounded event reconciliation, usable baseline controls and lifecycle cleanup | Reuse existing adapter exports and a single document model; avoid a separate mobile runtime, alternate CRDT or global gesture framework |
| Shared browser services | Disposable viewport/occlusion snapshots, overlay scheduling and focus/selection leases used by multiple presenters | Share a small service only when at least two consumers need it; otherwise keep the implementation local. Scope ownership to the mounted document/window, not a global singleton |
| Optional capability adapter | VirtualKeyboard geometry, host-requested keyboard facilities, richer pointer gestures and browser import/share services | Feature-detected and capability-gated; absent/denied/error paths retain baseline editing. Load implementation and dependencies only when requested |
| Optional extension presenter | Tables/code tools, slash/reference panels, asset/embed controls, reorder/resize and assistance UI | Own only transient interaction/presentation; call shared semantic commands. No disabled-extension listeners, assets, workers or requests |

The core does not need a new character model, persistent touch state, keyboard-height field or mobile-specific block type. Adding an API abstraction requires a demonstrated behavior/fallback need and a fixture; do not wrap every browser API preemptively. Device capabilities can change during a session: external keyboards, trackpads, stylus, split-screen and orientation. Coarse pointer/hover media queries and pointerType are hints, not exclusive device identities. Do not use user-agent names as the primary routing mechanism; a narrowly documented browser workaround needs an exact affected-version fixture and removal condition.

## Touch, selection and gesture ownership

Preserve native tap placement, double/triple-tap selection where provided, long-press selection handles, context menus, scroll momentum, pinch zoom and OS edge gestures. Use the actual Selection and input events to map the resulting semantic range. Rendering and remote patches must not replace the composing or actively selected subtree. Native handles/context menus may cover application controls; provide another reachable toolbar/command route rather than suppressing the native menu across the editor.

The editable root remains text-selectable and scrollable; do not set global `user-select: none`, disable zoom or apply `touch-action: none` to the editor/page. Prefer Pointer Events with a documented fallback for a claimed browser without them. A gesture handle may own a small declared touch-action region; declare it before the gesture begins. Use passive listeners when no cancellation is needed. `preventDefault` is local and conditional; synthetic event cancellation does not prove actual mobile scrolling behavior.

Optional drag/resize starts only on its dedicated handle after the declared activation threshold. Track pointer ID, capture owner and gesture state; ignore unrelated pointers. `pointercancel`, unexpected `lostpointercapture`, a competing second touch/pinch, native scroll takeover, unrecoverable orientation/zoom/host geometry change, blur, read-only and disposal cancel provisional work without a document mutation. Successful pointerup commits at most once; later click/capture-loss cannot duplicate or roll back the completed command. Release capture, auto-scroll and listeners on every terminal path. Owned gesture auto-scroll and ordinary reconcilable geometry updates refresh coordinates without self-canceling; stop only if the target/coordinate state cannot be safely revalidated. Temporary geometry and hover destinations are not CRDT updates. Each drag operation also has a tap-based action (for example Move before/after or an explicit size choice), plus a keyboard route; keyboard support alone is not the non-drag pointer alternative.

Controls meet applicable WCAG 2.2 target-size/spacing requirements; use 44×44 CSS px as the preferred touch target where practical, while documenting the 24×24 CSS px AA minimum and its exceptions accurately. Targets remain usable with browser zoom, large text and device scaling. Pen input is text/selection input unless a separate extension explicitly implements ink; pressure/tilt samples are not document text. Handwriting/Scribble and voice input use normal qualified replacement/composition paths.

## Mobile typing and keyboard controls

Virtual keyboards may omit keydown, report `Unidentified`, batch/delete/replace text and deliver noncancelable or missing beforeinput. Reuse the existing input/DOM fallback and composition ownership; do not translate every key into a second edit. Test prediction acceptance, autocorrection, double-space punctuation, swipe typing, emoji panels, dictated corrections, handwriting, selection replacement, CJK/Indic/RTL input and mixed hardware/virtual keyboards. Preserve platform-produced characters rather than guessing or undoing autocorrection from key history. Automatic Markdown/slash triggers require the conservative eligibility contract; ambiguous replacement input remains literal and explicit commands stay available.

`inputmode`, `enterkeyhint`, `autocapitalize`, `spellcheck`, `lang`, `dir` and supported `autocorrect` controls are hints with browser-specific results. Use a host-declared prose/code/command-search profile. Keep rich prose multiline; an Enter label of Done/Go/Send does not itself authorize form submission or change Enter semantics. Code remains literal; hints may suppress correction where supported, but the engine must preserve the text actually committed by the platform. Changing hints must not remount the editable root, interrupt composition or forcibly reopen the keyboard. Avoid numeric-only keyboards that make ordinary document characters unreachable.

Mobile users may have no Shift, Escape, Tab, modifier keys or visible undo. Expose reachable soft break, undo/redo, formatting, list/code indent/outdent, link, plain-text paste and command discovery actions. A supported command is not accessible solely through a desktop shortcut, slash keystroke or hover. Hardware keyboards retain the platform bindings in the interaction contract; connecting one must not leave an obsolete keyboard inset or select a different document model.

Capture semantic selection before a toolbar action; internal control focus/pointer transitions preserve the intended range. Restore focus only for a current user action whose editor/session is still active. Do not steal focus back after the user navigates elsewhere. Async completion cannot force a keyboard to reappear. Menu/dialog controls may intentionally own focus and require their own native keyboard; distinguish these from formatting buttons that preserve the editor selection. Programmatic focus or keyboard show is a request, not proof that a browser displayed the keyboard; respect user-activation restrictions and recover when it declines.

## Viewport, scrolling and keyboard occlusion

Start with the browser's ordinary scrolling/keyboard behavior. Use CSS layout and a `VisualViewport` adapter when available to keep the active caret and essential controls inside the visible region; use window/scroll-container resize/scroll fallbacks otherwise. Do not infer keyboard presence solely from `innerHeight` changes: browser chrome, zoom, rotation, split-screen and floating keyboards also change geometry. Coordinate viewport offsets/scale, root bounds and scroll-container coordinates explicitly; never blindly divide every pointer coordinate by device pixel ratio or viewport scale.

Qualify dynamic/small/large viewport units and safe-area insets for the host layout. Avoid fixed `100vh` assumptions, double safe-area compensation and toolbars behind the home indicator. `interactive-widget` is a host document viewport policy; the SDK reports requirements and accepts a declared mode rather than rewriting the page's meta viewport. Record both requested and observed viewport modes: unsupported or ineffective metadata remains a request, and compensation follows observed geometry rather than a presumed support boolean. New browser implementations and release versions need direct verification; neither an umbrella bug status nor a landed patch establishes stable support.

With native resize behavior, follow the visual/layout viewport actually delivered. Keyboard-overlay mode is opt-in and must supply correct occlusion handling; do not compensate twice if both browser resizing and VirtualKeyboard geometry are active. Floating/split keyboards may not be represented by a full-width bottom inset. Keep a scroll/focus/manual reposition fallback when exact occlusion data is unavailable, and record residual limitations. Toolbars and suggestion panels reposition or become reachable sheets when space is too small; do not obscure the caret or trap the user's only dismissal/format action.

All overlays consume one coordinate convention and bounded scheduled measurements. Coalesce viewport/scroll/resize notifications into at most one geometry-read batch and one write phase per active window per animation frame; stop when no dirty visible surface needs work. Register scroll sources for the actual host root, including nested containers and same-origin iframe ownership. Do not probe or control a cross-origin parent's viewport. Repositioning must not emit selection/content changes, continuously call scrollIntoView or fight browser scroll anchoring. Follow the caret after a local edit/focus request; remote edits and passive layout changes must not drag a reader to another block.

## Browser capability policy

| API or feature | Default and fallback |
|---|---|
| Selection, Pointer Events, beforeinput/input/composition | Required adapter behavior with qualified event fallbacks; actual OS selection/IME evidence remains mandatory |
| VisualViewport, viewport units and safe-area CSS | Progressive positioning/layout; preserve ordinary scroll and usable static controls if absent or incomplete |
| VirtualKeyboard and keyboard inset variables | Optional geometry/host keyboard policy; feature-detect, check applicable context, handle errors and restore document-global overlay policy through a host-owned lease. No automatic show/hide on every render |
| Keyboard `getLayoutMap` | Optional shortcut-label aid; handle absence, rejection and layout changes. Labels do not redefine semantic keys or override AltGraph/IME |
| Keyboard lock | Disabled for ordinary editing. An explicit host fullscreen/kiosk capability may request it only in a supported context, with an accessible escape and release on cancel, focus loss or teardown |
| EditContext | Experimental alternative input adapter only after a separate measured feasibility decision. Retain the contenteditable fallback; do not add it to the default bundle or assume it provides rich rendering, selection UI, clipboard or accessibility |
| Clipboard, file input, File System Access, Web Share | Prefer user-initiated capabilities; handle unavailable/denied/canceled/unsupported MIME paths. Native paste, file input and explicit copy/download fallbacks remain available |
| Screen orientation/fullscreen/window segments | Optional host features, never required for editing; rotation/reflow works without orientation lock or segmented-window APIs |

Feature presence is not successful authorization or correct behavior. Guard secure-context, user-activation, permissions-policy and embedding constraints per API; never prompt on mount or repeatedly after refusal. Metadata and browser support tables are planning inputs; record actual tested versions/capabilities at release. A host owns page-global policy across multiple editors; destroying one editor cannot reset another's active lease or the host's settings. No new service, microphone provider or paid API is introduced.

## Clipboard, browser lifecycle and recovery

Preserve the existing import precedence, literal mode, whitespace and safe parsing contracts. Cover long-press Copy/Cut/Paste, native share/paste sheets, image/file clipboard items, delayed permissions and cross-application rich text. Read each chosen payload once, bound preparation, and capture session/anchors before asynchronous work. Cancellation or failed cut retains the original text. If scripted clipboard reads are unavailable, expose native paste guidance and normal editing rather than an unusable disabled editor.

File pickers/camera capture/share sheets may suspend or blur the page. Treat their results as asynchronous user actions with stable targets; cancellation is harmless. The `capture` attribute is a hint, not guaranteed camera availability. Backgrounding, pagehide/pageshow, BFCache restoration, process eviction and connectivity loss need explicit recovery checks: suspend disposable observers/gesture state, validate the recovered session before accepting callbacks, restore durable state through existing storage, and prevent duplicate listeners. Best-effort flush is not an unload durability guarantee. Existing localCommitted/remoteCommitted semantics remain unchanged. Keep credentials, document text and clipboard payloads out of routine diagnostics.

## Extension conformance

Baseline modules expose touch-usable actions even with enhanced mobile presenters disabled. Rich extensions reuse the shared focus/viewport/capability ports and [extension case catalog](../tests/mobile-extension-cases.md): menus and references need a visible invocation path and bounded anchored results; tables/code need touch command access and scroll/selection coexistence; reorder/resize need cancellation and tap alternatives; assets/embeds need native picker/permission/recovery behavior; converters need import/export fallback and loss diagnostics; assistive presenters retain baseline OS input with the extension off.

A presenter declares pointer/focus/scroll ownership, loading trigger, per-instance resources, capability fallback, cancel/dispose behavior and tested web-device envelope. Registration does not start listeners, decoders, uploads, workers or geometry loops. Native SDK conformance remains in its existing tracks; a mobile browser pass cannot substitute for it.

## Overhead and evidence gates

Retain existing total-bundle, initialization and input latency targets. Proposed incremental baseline allowance for this work: at most **5 KiB Brotli JS** over a feature-equivalent packed baseline, inside the existing total adapter budget rather than added to it. MWB-1.1 records the baseline artifact/profile and confirms or explicitly revises this planning allocation before implementation measurements; an overrun requires a recorded decomposition/budget decision, not silent acceptance or removal of essential access.

Baseline admission also requires no new default third-party runtime dependency, worker, network request, polling timer or perpetual animation frame. Measurements/listeners scale with mounted/visible consumers, not document length; no full-document scans on key, pointermove or viewport events. For optional modules, absent/disabled means zero optional import/evaluation, assets, network, active listeners/observers and frame callbacks; enabled-idle means no continuous polling. Share only actual duplicate work and lazy-load expensive gesture, media, conversion or experimental API code.

Measure baseline/enabled/disabled packed consumers with identical documents and device profiles: raw and compressed bytes, cold parse/evaluation/startup, first usable edit, input-to-frame p50/p95/p99, geometry/layout counters, scroll/drag long tasks, memory after repeated mount/keyboard/rotate cycles, and resource counts after disposal. Existing phone input-to-frame and menu targets remain provisional until qualified; do not present emulated timing as phone performance. New support must meet the reviewed total limits and its incremental allowance; publish feature costs and retained failures.

Automated mechanics cover capability absence/rejection, event ordering, viewport transitions, pointer cancellation and semantic invariants. Real iOS Safari/iPadOS and Android browser/device runs cover actual keyboards, native handles/context menus, zoom, screen readers, focus activation and browser chrome. Record browser engine and mode (tab, installed web app or embedded host) explicitly; a Chromium-emulated iPhone is not Safari, and desktop WebKit is not iOS qualification. Reuse prior exact-revision cases where valid, but every new claimed combination needs evidence. Unsupported APIs may pass fallback cases; required editing capabilities cannot be marked unsupported merely to close the roadmap.

specs/assistive-input.md.text:
# Optional assistive input contract

Status: development contract; no dictation, voice-control or assistive-technology qualification is asserted.
Scope: an optional portable extension for discoverable editing commands, dictation status and host-supplied assistance. Baseline accessible editing and OS text input remain requirements when this extension is absent or disabled.

Read [editor interactions](editor-interactions.md) for ordinary editing, [web](web.md) for browser composition and selection, [native SDK parity](native-sdk-parity.md) for native text controls, and [extension library](extension-library.md) for registration and portable presenters. [Research evidence](../evidence/assistive-input-research.md) records source dates and platform limitations. This contract adds assistance without transferring committed document ownership from Rust/Yrs.

## Baseline and optional capabilities

Every editor surface retains its required keyboard, selection, composition, screen-reader and OS dictation behavior without installing this extension. Optional assistance cannot repair an otherwise inaccessible document or turn baseline support into an add-on feature. The terminal's qualified nonvisual command/text fallback remains available without a microphone or speech service.

The portable descriptor exposes named commands, applicability, presenter hooks, status, disposal and optional host transport capabilities through the existing extension interfaces. It adds no CRDT root, persisted raw/interim transcript metadata, executable document payload or parallel history. Use existing public package/crate boundaries; a separate speech package or provider is outside this track.

Distinguish these capabilities explicitly:

| Capability | Owner and qualification |
|---|---|
| OS text input, including dictation | Existing browser/native input adapter; actual OS/input-service evidence |
| Accessible editing commands | Shared semantic command plus platform presenter; available through ordinary controls without speech |
| Optional assistance status and controls | Extension presenter; advertise only operations the host actually exposes |
| Host-supplied recognition or transcript transport | Explicit injected host capability; deterministic mock qualification only in automated checks |
| Screen-reader document editing | Baseline editor/native accessibility implementation; real assistive-technology evidence |

OS input availability does not imply programmatic start/stop controls, microphone access, offline recognition or support for every language. If a capability is unavailable, provide an accurate disabled reason or ordinary text/command route. Do not install or select a speech provider implicitly.

## OS input is the default route

Receive committed text through the qualified `beforeinput`/`input`/composition and bounded DOM-reconciliation path, or the platform-native text-input contract. Dictation is not a sequence of synthetic key presses. Do not depend on a universal dictation-specific `inputType`, source flag or cancelable `beforeinput` event. When the OS does not expose dictation state, report ordinary editing state rather than inferred listening status.

The temporary composing subtree/native marked text remains owned by the input control under the existing composition gate. Keep intermediate alternatives out of the authoritative document unless the qualified baseline policy explicitly commits them. Each accepted edit passes the same prepare/validate/commit, read-only, selection and history rules as ordinary text. One input update must never be committed by both the OS adapter and the optional transport route.

The extension must tolerate ordinary typing, OS dictation and accessibility command activation while absent, enabled or being disposed. Preserve the chosen input route across focus changes; a provider result cannot start a new edit after the host has switched documents or destroyed the editor.

## Optional host transport lifecycle

Hosts may inject a bounded transport interface for an explicitly requested assistance session. No built-in speech provider, ambient credential discovery, automatic microphone request or Web Speech API fallback is part of this contract. Hosts expose start/stop/cancel and result/error callbacks only when those operations exist. Stopping requests completion under the declared final-result policy; cancellation rejects further results. The implementation task fixes the typed interface, size/time limits and version before consumers depend on it.

Capture document/epoch, a stable selection, session identity and request generation before asynchronous work. Provisional transcript text is disposable presenter state, visibly distinguished from committed content. Final results identify their session and result sequence; duplicate, out-of-order, cancelled and prior-generation callbacks cannot produce duplicate commits or reopen a session.

Define observable transitions for idle, starting, active, preparing, completed, cancelled, stale and failed. Permission denial, unavailable input, host disconnect and malformed/oversized results have typed recoverable outcomes. Cancellation is idempotent and revokes pending result acceptance before releasing resources. Abort/dispose on document switch, read-only transition or editor destruction; blur behavior is explicit and fixture-covered.

Resolve captured anchors against the current authoritative state before preparing the final replacement. Independent remote edits rebase through existing anchor rules. A deleted, incompatible or otherwise unresolvable target yields a stale result; preserve bounded recovery text in session memory for an explicit user action, never redirect it to the current caret or document end. A changed current selection alone does not silently change the captured target. Replacement selections, combining marks, surrogate pairs, ZWJ emoji, flags and RTL follow the shared UTF-16/grapheme contract.

Commit a final accepted result using the existing semantic command and intentional history boundary. Provisional updates and status changes create no document/history entries. Undo and redo preserve unrelated remote changes. Committing a final result consumes it exactly once, including when persistence reports a later recoverable failure.

## Accessible command presenters and status

Provide visible, named controls and a keyboard/nonpointer route for every assistance action. Visible labels and accessible names agree so voice-control users can invoke them by name. Respect platform shortcut conventions, editable focus and composition; do not intercept global printable-character shortcuts. Slash input is never the only way to find an editing command. Keep focus visible when panels, suggestions or on-screen keyboards appear.

Use the appropriate native accessibility roles/actions and the established web control pattern. A dedicated command-search field may implement combobox/listbox behavior; a menu button follows its own focus/keyboard contract. Opening a slash popup does not turn the entire rich document into a combobox. Preserve a stable editing selection while focus moves into controls, and restore focus predictably after commit, cancellation or dismissal without overriding a subsequent user focus change.

Present availability, permission errors, active assistance, cancellation, stale targets and recovery actions in perceivable text. Announce meaningful status transitions through platform status/live-region facilities without repeating every provisional token or stealing editing focus. Do not announce private transcript content by default. Respect host language, direction, zoom, contrast and reduced-motion settings. Keyboard-only and screen-reader routes reach cancellation and recovery controls.

## Privacy and resource ownership

Native input does not establish that recognition runs on the device. Document the OS/service mode actually tested and any known network or language restrictions. An optional host transport declares whether it receives audio or transcript text, its processing destination, permission ownership, retention policy and cancellation behavior before the user starts it. Unknown processing locality is shown as unknown.

The editor retains only bounded session state needed for editing/recovery. It neither stores audio nor sends document context by default. Credentials remain host-owned. Accepted final text becomes ordinary document content and therefore may appear in document updates and user exports. Audio and raw/interim/unaccepted transcript metadata stay out of document updates, logs and telemetry; test artifacts use only prepared or non-sensitive qualification text. Export of retained recovery text requires an explicit user action. Release listeners, streams, callbacks and host session handles on all terminal states; late callbacks are inert. Normal OS dictation follows OS permissions rather than an additional extension permission prompt.

Automated fixtures use prepared event sequences, fixed transcript results and mock transports. They never open a microphone, contact a speech/model provider, load `.secrets`, record fixtures from a live provider or spend inference credits. Real device runs validate OS input/accessibility with non-sensitive test documents and record only the minimum evidence. A separate host-provider dogfood workflow requires its own exact content scope, hard request/monetary cap and stop condition; this track does not authorize it.

## Platform obligations and qualification

Web, iOS, Android, macOS, Windows and Linux presenters call the same semantic operations. Each native adapter uses its qualified text control, UI thread and platform accessibility mechanisms. It may expose explicit unsupported assistance capabilities where the OS has no relevant API; the baseline native parity obligations remain unchanged. Terminal assistance uses explicit commands, readable status and pasted/text input; it does not claim native speech capture or infer voice commands from arbitrary text.

Maintain a capability matrix by OS/device, browser or native toolkit, input method/service, language, screen reader and tested version. Each cell distinguishes baseline editing, OS dictation, voice activation, extension controls and optional host transport. State whether evidence is deterministic, actual-device, unsupported or pending; a prepared transcript proves neither speech recognition quality nor actual device compatibility.

Deterministic cases cover extension absent/disabled, ordinary input during assistance, noncancelable/missing input events, selection replacement, composition overlap, remote insertion/deletion, final-result deduplication, cancellation, denied permission, read-only transition, blur, document switch, destruction and resource release. Assert semantic content, UTF-16 selection, origin/history, status/focus and unchanged state on rejection. Include accessible names and keyboard behavior; structural accessibility checks alone do not qualify screen-reader editing.

Actual-device cases cover the declared web/mobile and native surfaces with real dictation and accessibility tools where supported: text insertion/correction/replacement, formatting controls, structural commands, selection, cancellation/recovery, IME coexistence and RTL. Record exact OS, browser/toolkit, hardware, locale, input service, assistive technology, case outcomes and retained failure/skip reasons. Native task evidence is platform-specific; missing one native environment does not block portable implementation or another platform's work. It does block an unqualified cross-platform completion claim.

Capability aggregation checks evidence provenance and omissions; it does not substitute a metadata validator for behavior tests. Keep unsupported/pending rows visible, preserve failures and link actual device artifacts. No publication, new provider integration or paid-content qualification follows automatically from this roadmap.

## Mobile browser assistance

Baseline mobile OS input/accessibility is qualified by [track 40](../roadmaps/40-mobile-web.md) with the extension disabled. Claimed optional mobile-web controls reuse its focus/viewport/capability ports and are integrated in MWX-1.7 under [track 41](../roadmaps/41-mobile-web-extensions.md). AIN-1.2/1.3/1.10 remain the prerequisite web presentation/lifecycle/device work; no native assistance task is required to begin the mobile-web integration. Soft keyboard occlusion, VoiceOver/TalkBack navigation, provider-error/cancel controls and explicit user-activation behavior need actual device evidence.

specs/agent-editing.md.text:
# Host-app MCP and Markdown edit readiness

Status: planned shared adapter, roadmap 14. The embedding application's existing MCP owns authentication, transport, tool registration and authorization. edit.ac supplies portable editing services and optional adapter helpers. Neither a standalone MCP server nor a CLI MCP mode is required. No model provider belongs in the core.

## Planned service shape

The names below describe host-mappable operations, not a currently exported SDK:

| Operation | Inputs | Outputs |
|---|---|---|
| Read/export | Document locator, representation and optional revision | Markdown/source, observed revision, source hash, schema/dialect, capability and preservation diagnostics |
| Prepare | Expected revision/hash plus bounded Markdown patch, complete candidate Markdown, or anchored semantic edits | Validated proposal ID, semantic/source diff, affected identities, conflict/unsupported diagnostics |
| Apply | Proposal ID, expected revision and stable request ID | Operation/receipt ID, resulting revision, local durability and remote receipt state |
| Receipt lookup | Actor/document-scoped request ID | Original result, pending/unknown/not-found state |
| Observe | Authorized document and cursor/revision | Bounded change metadata, invalidation/resync indication |

A complete candidate Markdown upload is a proposal against its retained export baseline. FMT-1.12 maps it to bounded prepared semantic commands while preserving unchanged identities and unknown data. It is not permission to overwrite the live document wholesale. Chunked uploads use explicit size/checksum/session/expiry limits; partial uploads never mutate the document. Local paths, public URLs and uploaded content do not independently grant document authority.

## Mutation and retry contract

Recheck permissions, readonly mode, schema/capabilities, expected revision and anchors within the host's serialized commit boundary. Stale/ambiguous/deleted-target inputs return structured conflict with no preparation-time mutation. The base/current/proposed comparison is available for a new reviewed proposal. Authorization and capability metadata are not accepted from untrusted document text.

Bind each immutable proposal to the authenticated actor, document/epoch, base revision, schema/dialect profile and content hash. Scope idempotency by authenticated actor, document/epoch and request ID; store the payload hash and result. Apply first authorizes access to that request's outcome, then looks up its durable receipt and compares payload hashes. Same ID/same payload returns the original receipt, including after restart, even if the original proposal has since expired or its base revision is now stale. Same ID/different payload rejects. Only a new request proceeds to proposal ownership/expiry checks and the serialized mutation preconditions above. Retain entries for a documented retry window and return an explicit expired/unknown outcome rather than claiming indefinite exactly-once delivery.

Journal committed update bytes and dedup/result metadata in one durable host-store transaction before acknowledging durable success or releasing that remote request's updates to peers. The engine commit itself cannot roll back. If local persistence fails after mutation, return a pending/unknown-durability result and retain recovery state; never report a clean rejection and silently repeat insertion. Freeze further mutation admission and outbound synchronization for that replica until ordered journal recovery succeeds; bounded incoming updates may be queued without application. Reads and explicitly labeled recovery exports remain available. The barrier covers human edits, state-vector resynchronization, checkpoints and batched updates, any of which could otherwise leak the unjournaled operation. Durable publication always includes all causal predecessors and their required dedup receipts. No acknowledged durable operation may be repeated after crash/retry. Define queue visibility and recovery order in tests before exposing mutation tools.

Agent operations carry authenticated provenance and intentional history groups; they use the same engine, renderer patches, persistence/outbox and sync channel as human edits. Reverting an agent change is a new revision-checked authorized edit, not destructive rewind. Limits apply per request, document and pending queue.

## Realtime and read-only behavior

Open views receive ordinary engine updates without remounting; concurrent human changes are reconciled under the same policy. MCP resources/subscriptions or supported notifications advertise invalidation and bounded revision metadata, with capability-negotiated polling/resync fallback. MCP notification delivery is not the CRDT transport, guaranteed event history, or proof of durable storage.

Read-only means the mutation service denies every write regardless of UI or MCP annotations. Host permissions filter reads, source exports, history, attachments and receipt lookups too. Keep editing content distinct from instructions authorizing new tool actions. Tool response content is untrusted user data; it cannot expand scopes or fetch referenced resources automatically.

## Encryption and hosting

For E2EE, source export, diff and edit application run at an authorized endpoint with document keys. An opaque relay cannot offer plaintext Markdown tools. A server-side app MCP can edit only if that service is explicitly inside the decryption trust boundary; otherwise it routes to an available authorized local client or reports unavailable. No plaintext downgrade or hidden key upload is allowed.

Host integration qualification uses a prepared MCP client/server transport, fake authorization, fixture uploads and real shared engine calls. Verify duplicate retries after crashes, stale revisions, overlapping edits, readonly denial, bounded notifications and browser/native/TUI propagation. No live LLM calls, paid inference or production source uploads are needed for these tests.

Sources: [MCP tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools), [MCP annotations](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-03-16-tool-annotations/), [HTTP conditional semantics](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-13), [research](../evidence/followup-research.md).

specs/security-encryption.md.text:
# Security profiles and optional encryption

Status: planned optional profile, roadmap 19. Security applies to all modes; encryption is opt-in and must not expand the minimal core or silently change trust boundaries.

## Profiles

| Profile | What is protected | Remaining trust |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline | Authenticated/authorized access, safe imports, resource limits, transport confidentiality where networked | Host/services may process plaintext; local data follows host storage policy |
| Encrypted local store | Journal/checkpoints/history and attachment cache at rest | Authorized running client and any plaintext sync endpoint can read content |
| E2EE collaboration | Content encrypted before remote storage/transport, authenticated update envelopes | Authorized key-holding clients can read plaintext; relay observes declared metadata and availability |

TLS or disk encryption alone is not E2EE. Selecting E2EE must protect creation/restore, edits, backups, attachments, revision history, previews and recovery exports under a documented policy. Never upload an initial plaintext update before an encryption wrapper attaches. Metadata leakage (document IDs, sizes, timing, participants, routing) is explicitly listed.

## Design gate

Write a threat model, key/identity lifecycle and protocol selection ADR before choosing cryptographic dependencies. Use a maintained, reviewed implementation/protocol; do not invent primitives, nonce schemes or a bespoke group-key protocol. Compile and license/advisory-check the selected dependency on WASM and all native targets. A library's existence or passing round trip is not a security review.

Associate authenticated ciphertext with document/epoch/schema/key epoch and operation identity. Define tamper/replay handling, secure nonce uniqueness across crash/fork/restore, sender/write authorization distinct from decryption ability, membership/key rotation and attachment binding. Untrusted ciphertext cannot cause unbounded decode/allocation or be applied before verification. Design authenticated membership and writer signatures if the threat model requires them; a shared decrypt key alone must not be advertised as read-only enforcement against malicious peers.

## Keys and offline behavior

The host owns key acquisition, OS keystore/browser key wrapping, user unlock, backup/recovery, retention and deletion. Keys/passwords never appear in ac:// URLs, logs, crash diagnostics or MCP responses. Define locked, unavailable-key, revoked, recovery and incompatible-key states. Keep encrypted pending updates recoverable without plaintext fallback.

Offline revocation cannot erase keys/plaintext already acquired by a former reader. Define future-key exclusion and admission of offline writes from old epochs, including conflict/export/recovery paths. Do not silently discard acknowledged local work after rotation. Loss of all recovery material may make content unrecoverable; do not promise recovery without a retained authorized key path.

## Host and agent boundaries

A ciphertext-only server can enforce envelope size/rate/auth metadata and durably acknowledge stored ciphertext; it cannot validate plaintext schema, search it or generate plaintext previews/diffs. Authorized clients validate decrypted semantics. Hosted search, plaintext export and agent editing require an explicitly trusted decrypting endpoint or remain unavailable.

The application's existing MCP may expose Markdown tools only within that authorized plaintext boundary. Credentials and keys are not delegated merely because an agent can edit. Different encryption profiles cannot join the same session by silently downgrading; capability negotiation fails visibly.

## Qualification

Use deterministic prepared ciphertext/test keys and offline transports, never real secrets or paid model calls. Cover protected creation, wrong key, tamper, replay, crash before/after journal commit, rotation with an offline peer, revoked reader/writer, lost-key recovery, oversized inputs, encrypted attachments/history and unsupported peers. Search stored bytes/logs/exports for seeded plaintext leakage, while noting that such checks do not prove absence of all leaks.

An independent security review with a precise scope and resolved findings is required before claiming the encrypted profile production-ready. Unavailable review blocks that profile's claim, not ordinary unencrypted editor development. Neither profile offers a compliance certification.

Implementation examples and caveats: [research](../evidence/followup-research.md). Source for the protected-creation/opaque relay example: [Automerge Keyhive](https://automerge.org/docs/keyhive/ark-api-guide/); treat its actual protocol/API maturity as a selection-gate question, not a preapproved dependency.

specs/delivery-scenarios.md.text:
# Full-delivery scenarios and capability matrix

Status: qualification contract, not completed product evidence. Roadmap 20 qualifies the ordinary profile; roadmap 24 qualifies optional encrypted profiles after independent security review. The initial browser release is still independently gated by roadmap 10.

## Required scenarios

| Scenario | Concrete deliverable | Evidence required |
|---|---|---|
| PM ticket rich-text editing | Small host integration with text/marks/lists/links/checklists/table/image/reference preset, readonly/edit states and lifecycle disposal | Web/React plus genuine iOS, Android, macOS, Windows and Linux controls pass the same semantic corpus |
| Collaborative documents | Multiple platform clients edit the same identity online and offline, restore after local commit, reconnect and see converged content | Distinct live IDs, reorder/duplicate delivery, composition races, history and local/remote durability evidence |
| Agent edits through the app | Sample existing app MCP uses read/export, bounded Markdown upload/prepare/diff/apply and receipts while human views remain open | Prepared MCP requests, auth/readonly denial, stale conflict, crash-safe retries and realtime patches without remount |
| Local file and hosted terminal client | External-editor CLI plus built-in TUI edit Markdown/literal text, local files and configured ac:// documents | Exact source/no-op preservation, changed-on-disk detection, dirty buffer plus peer changes, recovery and reconnect |
| Review and change tracking | Web/native/terminal views of exact source/projected/semantic changes with available history | Byte-hash patch roundtrip, visible mark/attribute/move changes, unavailable-history handling and restore as new edit |
| Third-party extension | Portable custom mark, inline atom and host-authorized reference resolver using public documented entrypoints | No engine fork for data-only types; schema/codec/command/presenter conformance and full mandatory-platform editing |
| Optional protected documents | Explicit local-at-rest or E2EE profile with real key providers and authorized plaintext endpoints | Protected creation/history/attachments, tamper/replay/rotation/offline recovery, no downgrade and actual security review |

## Mandatory and optional capability rules

Mandatory rich-text semantics, selection, readonly, undo/redo, safe clipboard, composition, local persistence, collaboration, references/custom atoms and exact change model have a per-platform `capability.json`. Native table/image editing must actually work to satisfy parity; preserved fallback alone does not pass. All native desktop platforms were explicitly requested. Separate unsupported OS versions from supported configurations.

TUI is a Markdown/literal-source client. Terminal glyphs, source syntax and attachment placeholders need not reproduce graphical rendering, but edits must preserve supported shared semantics/unknown data and clearly reject unrepresentable changes. It does not implement a second CRDT or replace an entire hosted document on save.

Optional math typesetting, encryption and other extras have separate capability entries. Source preservation/editing is distinguished from typeset rendering. Optional absence never erases document data or silently changes the active security profile. A feature absent from one platform cannot be described as universal full parity.

## Test and release discipline

Commit deterministic cross-client fixtures and a machine-readable product manifest tying capability, implementation/package revisions, platform/toolchain/device, command/case IDs and resulting evidence. Production account data, live model providers and paid inference are not test fixtures. A sample host's mock auth is explicitly test infrastructure, not a production security deployment.

Run shared semantic/session/format/diff conformance plus each presenter adapter's focused tests. Then execute actual OS/device IME, keyboard/touch, screen-reader, clipboard and lifecycle cases. Missing device/toolchain evidence blocks that platform's qualified claim; it need not block independent implementation elsewhere. A completed package build alone does not prove parity.

Record performance against the declared enabled profile: minimal core versus task preset versus review or encrypted mode. Reuse the fixed Task/Long/Large/Aged corpus and honest visibility/editability/durability metrics. The extra clients do not justify silently dropping the earlier correctness or performance gates.

Full delivery requires the whole requested base matrix. Partial browser/iOS success may be released with its actual support table but cannot close the all-platform milestone. Encryption remains an additional profile with a separate completed roadmap; basic delivery can finish while its security review remains blocked.

specs/protocol-v1.md.text:
# Protocol profile v1

Status: frozen foundation admission contract; production transport, persistence and structural cross-language qualification remain separate gates.

## Exact profile and metadata

Profile ID `editac.yrs-yjs.v1`; schema `editac.registry.v1`; protocol version integer `1`; update encoding integer `1`; offsets string `utf16`. Qualified dependency candidates are exactly Yrs `0.28.0` with `small-client` and explicit `OffsetKind::Utf16`, Yjs `13.6.33`, y-protocols `1.0.7`. Rust/compiler and rustdoc are `1.97.1`; deterministic JS runtime is Node `24.19.0`. Update v2 or upgraded libraries require a new qualified profile, not optimistic acceptance. The dependency pair's existing XML/text interoperability is verified; structural qualification remains FND-1.12.

Document metadata is an immutable external envelope, stored alongside checkpoint/journal bytes, not additional CRDT roots: `{profile, schema, protocolVersion, updateEncoding, offsets, documentId, epoch}`. `documentId` and `epoch` are lowercase canonical UUID strings; assign independently when creating a new document. They identify logical document and lineage, never a Yrs/Yjs writer. The fixture uses fixed UUIDs. Neither identifier changes during restore, offline merge, or ordinary edits. JSON/Markdown import, explicit destructive reset or migration to incompatible schema creates a new epoch (and import creates a new document identity). Preserve the old lineage as recovery; never mix epochs by applying their bytes.

An update envelope additionally includes `writerId` (integer 0…4294967295), `sequence` (nonnegative JS-safe integer, monotonically increasing per writer/epoch) and opaque binary `bytes`. Duplicate/reorder tolerance comes from the CRDT; sequence supports journal/receipt bookkeeping, not a new LWW clock. State vectors and updates use v1 binary codecs; a vector is neither a durable acknowledgment nor an exact deletion-sensitive revision token. Metadata authenticity/resource limits belong to downstream admission ports. This freeze supplies no networking implementation.

## Initialization and restoration

The creator authorizes one initializer for an epoch. Initialize all roots and initial content once, publish its checkpoint and immutable metadata, then let independent writers apply that state. Never let peers independently seed the same logical text. Schema bootstrap, node IDs and seed are specified in [schema-v1.md](schema-v1.md). A fresh user document may be empty: initialize the five typed roots, with no pair until both reserved members exist.

Existing metadata is the authority for existence; empty state vector, empty visible content, no received network response, or absent root entries does not authorize initialization. Restore creates a replica with a fresh independent writer identity, requests the five root types, and applies checkpoint plus journal under restore origin. It never writes seed content again. Partial restore/missing initializer metadata is a recovery state; do not edit or seed while guessing whether the epoch already exists. Persist allocation counters with writer sessions, and never reactivate one writer ID in two tabs.

## Negotiation and unsupported inputs

Before any live mutation, exchange the complete immutable metadata. Require exact equality of profile/schema/version/encoding/offsets and the expected document/epoch. There is no fallback, highest-common-version negotiation, downconversion or automatic migration in v1. Unknown profile/schema or wrong encoding/offset/version: return `unsupported-profile`; document mismatch: `wrong-document`; epoch mismatch: `wrong-epoch`; malformed/missing metadata: `invalid-metadata`. A failed check must leave live content, history, state vector and journal unchanged. Empty-but-existing documents follow the same checks.

Keep rejected checkpoint/update bytes and their envelope in explicit recovery storage when restoring or recovering user content; never silently drop them, acknowledge them as committed, or project them as v1. Ordinary unauthorized inbound traffic may be rejected without storing unbounded attacker data. Decode and validate untrusted bytes on a disposable replica under bounded resource checks before admitting them to the live replica. Missing/invalid placements and parent references use schema-v1's retained read fallback; other malformed data or unsupported root/value/layout shapes return preserved recovery for user-owned state. The fixture admission function demonstrates metadata rejection before applying bytes; it is not a production binary validator or storage port.

Unknown node kinds and marks **within the valid v1 value shapes** are retained opaquely, with no extension download/execution. An unknown root/shared type or unsupported structural descriptor is not an extension mark: it requires explicit recovery, not a guessed schema. Offline known-profile updates remain recoverable on failed/unauthorized upload. Migrations and rollback are explicit new-epoch workflows retaining the old checkpoint; no in-place migration is qualified here.
