## Origins, offsets and delivery

Origins are local transaction metadata, not encoded update fields or peer identities. Rust uses explicit origins; JS passes an origin to `doc.transact` / `Y.applyUpdate`. Normative classes are `local:<command>`, `remote`, `restore`, `initialize`. Fixture origins `fixture:edit`, `fixture:move`, `fixture:split`, `fixture:join`, `fixture:delete` map to local commands; `fixture:remote` to remote; `fixture:init`, `fixture:second-text`, `fixture:compose` to initialization. Only tracked local commands enter selective history. Remote/restore/initialize, presence and checkpoint loading are excluded. Adapter echo suppression uses the local origin class; neither network origin strings nor writer IDs grant authority.

Public offsets and run formatting lengths are UTF-16 code units, not UTF-8 bytes or scalar/grapheme counts. Prepare whole mutations and reject surrogate-interior offsets, unknown/deleted targets and invalid hierarchy before opening a live write transaction. Relative anchors identify original shared text and start/end affinity, as specified in schema-v1. No asynchronous operation retains an absolute offset as its target. Failure to resolve is explicit; it cannot redirect to document end.

Apply v1 updates idempotently, including duplicate and reordered delivery, with no projection writes. Byte receipt, Yjs `synced`, transaction completion and state-vector agreement do not prove durable persistence. `localCommitted` requires completed storage transaction; `remoteCommitted` requires an identified durable service receipt. Neither is implemented by these fixtures. FND-1.12 must qualify this exact schema/anchor mapping in both directions; FND-1.13 supplies the compiled WASM boundary. No Tiptap, arbitrary extension, production durability, performance or deployment compatibility claim follows from the freeze.

specs/public-docs-demo.md.text:
# Public documentation and demo delivery

Repository: `edit-ac/docs`, public Apache-2.0. The initial repository contains Markdown guides, checked navigation and dependency-free CI. It is not yet a published documentation website or an editor demo.

## Public information architecture

Organize a clear landing page; getting started by web/React/native/CLI; local-first and collaboration guides; extension authoring and recipes; custom/internal links; import/export matrix; cloud host operations; host-app MCP; security profiles; generated API reference; troubleshooting, migration and release notes. Separate tutorials, task guides, conceptual explanations and reference tables. Keep internal tasks and architecture decisions in architecture, linked when useful.

Every API snippet is compiled/executed against named immutable artifacts. Mark conceptual contracts as such until the API exists. Generate versioned API pages from the owning packages and native bindings. Public feature tables consume the qualified capability/release profile. Show unsupported/experimental modes clearly, including **PDF export only**. Do not publish an install tutorial for empty placeholder packages.

The static site needs keyboard/screen-reader navigation, readable code and tables, responsive layouts, search, theme contrast, stable versioned URLs, a useful 404 and redirect/migration policy. Search indexes public docs only. Keep a plaintext/Markdown reading path available. Pin the selected maintained generator at its implementation gate; no custom documentation framework is required.

## Playground contract

Use the actual packaged editor. Keep the playground in this repository as a consumer, with editor semantics in core. Offer a PM-ticket preset, a collaborative document scenario, code/table/asset/reference examples, a read-only view, undo/redo, diff review and conversion actions supported by its exact version. Show enabled extensions and relevant profile limits. Include keyboard/touch paths and reset/export controls.

Default public mode uses redistributable fixture documents and local browser storage. Disclose local persistence and provide reset; do not imply browser data is permanent. Multi-view/tab collaboration uses real qualified local transport. A remote collaborative room is an optional deployment mode requiring the cloud service's qualified auth/retention/abuse configuration; the public static demo does not secretly depend on an unqualified backend.

No ambient credentials, private examples, live model provider or anonymous arbitrary URL proxy. Link-preview examples use approved public fixtures or a clearly configured host policy. Avoid arbitrary external embeds. Imported user data stays local unless an explicitly selected sharing mode declares its destination and authority. Conversion itself remains local-only in the qualified profile; remote conversion is out of scope. Bound conversion/highlighting work and show cancellation/recovery.

## Release and operation

Build, check local links/navigation, execute supported snippets/consumers, run browser accessibility/interaction checks and verify production base paths/CSP/WASM/worker assets before publication. Use existing organization GitHub Pages or another explicitly selected static destination; domain purchase and paid provisioning are not required.

Publish from immutable revisions with least-privilege CI and retained artifacts. Record public URL, SDK and docs revisions, smoke results and a tested previous-artifact rollback. A working build is not evidence that the deployment URL works. The final public demo task must verify the actual page and real edits.

A docs release can describe currently qualified web features while native implementation progresses. Native/format/cloud guides must state their maturity. Roadmap29 uses task-specific upstream gates for qualified examples/demo; it has no whole-track SDK prerequisite so documentation structure can proceed now.

## Candidate-to-publication ordering

EQL-1.9 publishes tested immutable prerelease artifacts after feature/platform qualification and before advanced DOC examples and demo publication. DOC-1.6/1.10/1.13 consume those recorded candidates, then DOC-1.14 supplies deployment evidence to EQL-1.7. EQL-1.8 promotes the same artifacts after public verification; it does not rebuild them. Roadmap37 therefore does not require all of29 at entry. This task-level gate prevents a docs/package publication cycle while keeping source-documentation work available early.

## Mobile support claims

Document touch controls, soft-keyboard alternatives, browser API fallbacks, embedding/viewport requirements and optional module costs from [mobile web](mobile-web.md). Claim mobile browser support only from reviewed MWB-1.11 evidence and optional feature support from MWX-1.8. Distinguish actual mobile browsers from emulation, installed-app modes and native SDKs; expose tested versions and known limitations in the public demo/profile.

specs/editing-regression-suite.md.text:
# Editing regression suite and prevention boundaries

Status: test/architecture contract; fixture validation is not editor qualification.
Scope: semantic commands, browser input, composition, selection, rendering, history, import and extension lifecycle. Reuse the existing interaction/mobile catalogs rather than building another editor or event framework. [Regression research](../evidence/editor-regressions-round2.md) and [testing methods](../evidence/editor-testsuite-methods.md) distinguish reported failures, confirmed fixes and proposed edit.ac tests.

The machine-readable [suite manifest](../tests/editing-suite/suite.json) indexes catalog cases, architectural guards and concrete step-by-step recipes. [Track 42](../roadmaps/42-editing-regression-suite.md) builds the real-engine test drivers and checks before track 38 consumes them. This repository's validator checks fixture/coverage integrity only. All recipes remain planned until their real adapters, assertions and evidence exist.

## Prevention boundaries

| Guard | Required boundary | Falsifying test |
|---|---|---|
| G01 Intent correlation | Each observed input intent has editor/document epoch, input/composition session, origin and a terminal disposition. keydown/beforeinput/input/observer notifications may refer to one intent; identical text alone is never its identity | Replay duplicate notifications, then a deliberate identical second insertion; one commit for each real intent |
| G02 Compound preparation | Selected Enter, marked typing, cross-block replacement, rich paste and input-rule transforms prepare and validate all text/marks/structure before one engine mutation | Reject the final sub-operation; content, state vector/revision, history, publication and journal enqueue remain unchanged |
| G03 Resulting selection | A prepared action supplies a stable semantic selection result/policy, including direction and affinity; distinguish text ranges, node/cell selections and before/after-node insertion anchors. Browser geometry stays in the adapter. Resolve against the committed state | Assert exact range and next typed sentinel after split/format/paste, including backward selection and unrelated remote updates |
| G04 Pending marks | Pending typing marks are editor-local transient state: null derives from context, an empty set explicitly disables marks, and a nonempty set overrides them. Apply text plus allowed marks together; recompute on selection-context change and validate before changing pending state | Toggle collapsed mark with zero content edits, type, split, revisit empty destination, and reject an incompatible mark |
| G05 Composition ownership | The browser/native control owns its composing subtree. A qualified input ADR fixes buffering/finalization/cancel policy before adapter implementation | compositionend before commit Enter with isComposing=false must not cause a split; the next deliberate Enter must work |
| G06 Coordinate units | UTF-16 boundary validity, grapheme boundaries and visual movement are different contracts. Preserve original code points and authored whitespace | Reject surrogate-interior command ranges separately from grapheme deletion; test NFC/NFD, ZWJ, flags, Indic and bidi without rewriting text |
| G07 Origin and history | History admission classifies local user edits, remote updates, imports, recovery and renderer work. One transaction does not automatically mean one undo group | Type → remote edit → paste → undo: only paste disappears; undo restores the stored selection, not a later caret |
| G08 Notification isolation | Commit completes and releases transaction/locks before notifying host/renderer. Subscriber exceptions cannot roll back a committed edit or trigger duplicate persistence | Subscriber throws, unsubscribes, destroys or requests another edit; verify the declared deferred/rejected command policy and single publication |
| G09 DOM reconciliation | Renderer patches have scoped generation/origin ownership. Suppress only identified renderer echoes, not every mutation in a time window; preserve active native input | Render echo and unrelated genuine input in the same turn; only the genuine input creates a new edit |
| G10 Normalization termination | Preparation normalizers have bounded work and a convergent canonical form. A valid committed state is stable under repeated normalization | Normalize twice, test interacting repair rules and resource limits; no oscillation, silent loss or endless repair transactions |
| G11 Async target/lifetime | Captured anchors, request generation, session/epoch and cancellation govern completion. Current caret is not a fallback target | Resolve after target deletion/editor switch/disposal; recover/reject without redirecting, refocusing or committing twice |
| G12 Event ownership | Nested editable controls, clipboard handlers and drag/drop presenters explicitly own or decline an event. A consumed inner-control event does not edit the outer document | Paste in a node-view input, drop once through multiple listeners, then use the outer editor; each acts only on its owner |
| G13 Identity and rendering | Block identity/selection are independent of DOM tag/view instance; replacement presenters release old resources and adopt qualified mappings | Heading/tag/custom-view rerender at a selected caret, delayed mount and another keystroke; no content loss or stale target |
| G14 Evidence integrity | Tests observe actual adapters/engine, independent expected outcomes and nonzero intended assertions. Fixtures, screenshots and receipt validators have distinct evidentiary scope | Corrupt expected content, range, origin/count and platform receipt; each required assertion fails rather than regenerating the golden |

Current separate text/format/structure primitives and their stale-plan checks are useful foundations, but do not establish G02/G03/G04/G07/G08. Do not emulate one atomic action by publishing several commits and undoing partial work after failure. The responsible engine task must qualify a complete prepared operation and semantic selection policy first; the suite marks dependent recipes blocked until that capability exists. This contract does not invent a storage schema or require viewport/DOM state in Rust.

## Input and command protocol

An adapter classifies input, captures a stable target and permitted marks, prepares the semantic operation, checks applicability/read-only/session state, commits once, applies its selection policy, and then publishes a scoped result. Record causality separately from payload. Terminal states include handled, native-pending, committed, canceled, rejected and disposed; a handled keyboard event cannot independently replay the same edit through beforeinput. A native edit awaiting reconciliation is not already an engine commit.

The operation-correlation strategy must be proved against observed event traces, including observer-first and missing/noncancelable beforeinput. Scope tokens to an editor root and generation. Do not identify intents by identical data, a blanket debounce/time window, or a fixed assumption about event order. Reconciliation cannot discard a later legitimate identical keystroke. Composition-session evidence must distinguish the IME commit key from subsequent intentional commands without indefinitely suppressing Enter.

Fix the composition ADR before WEB-1.4–WEB-1.7 implementation. WEB-1.13 owns this prerequisite: use the delivered engine/storage/renderer/selection boundaries to qualify a minimal real-DOM/real-engine protocol probe and record `decisions/004-browser-input-composition.md` with passing evidence in `evidence/browser-input-policy/receipt.json`. This mechanical qualification permits production routing implementation; actual OS/IME/device support still requires its separate qualification. RGS-1.4 later reuses the qualified ADR/probe and proves the shared driver against the completed production adapter; track 08/42 completion is not a prerequisite for WEB-1.13. The default desired model is temporary native composition followed by a prepared final edit; any qualified exception for observed platform behavior must state how intermediate commits/history/remote changes are handled and update the corresponding acceptance. An absent ADR is a prerequisite gap, not evidence that a particular buffering policy already exists.

Define subscriber behavior explicitly: queue a requested edit for a later dispatcher turn or return a typed reentrancy rejection; never mutate inside the still-live transaction or synchronously recurse through render/observer/command callbacks. A thrown callback is reported independently of commit success. Dispose invalidates queued ownership, while already committed state remains recoverable. Tests assert the selected policy rather than accept either outcome nondeterministically.

Normalization belongs to bounded preparation and validated projection. Prefer rejecting unsupported input with preserved source over repeatedly mutating the committed document to repair it. For necessary repairs, document the decreasing measure or bounded convergence argument. CRDT arrival orders must produce equivalent admitted semantic state without choosing winners by callback order. Test unknown-node/mark retention and schema profiles separately from presentation fillers.

## Test layers and oracles

| Layer | Exercises | Oracle and limit |
|---|---|---|
| Plan/fixture integrity | Case ownership, recipe structure, source links, offsets, required expected snapshots | May pass now; proves no runtime behavior |
| Pure semantic | Real Rust prepared operations, schema and UTF-16/grapheme helpers | Hand-authored snapshots/selection plus version-pinned official Unicode vectors; never call the implementation to generate its own expected output |
| Sequence/history | Real command dispatcher and history with fixed clock/origins; related operations and negative paths | Assert every checkpoint, explicit undo/redo outcomes, atomic rejection and attributable effect counts |
| Property/interleaving | Seeded valid command sequences, schema constraints, normalization and two-replica update schedules | Algebraic invariants and convergence of admitted semantics; shrinking preserves preconditions and writes the minimal failing trace |
| Browser mechanics | Real packed WASM/adapter, DOM mapping, event ownership, focus and rendering | Production handlers with observed state/commit instrumentation; prepared native-event delivery is labeled synthetic |
| Browser interaction | WebDriver/Playwright key, pointer, selection, clipboard and layout actions supported by the browser driver | Actual document/caret/focus/DOM observations; jsdom or untrusted dispatchEvent cannot establish native defaults |
| OS/device/AT | Actual mobile keyboard, native IME/dictation, selection handles, Safari and screen readers | Exact reproducible device observations; no emulator, receipt checker or recorded trace substitutes for this layer |

Screenshots support layout/focus evidence but cannot prove semantic preservation. HTML/text serialization alone cannot prove selection, pending marks, block identity or correct undo. Cross-editor differential testing may help reduce a bug, but differences between editors are not failures until edit.ac's explicit policy identifies the expected result. Normalize only irrelevant representation differences; never normalize away content, Unicode, marks or stale selection to make a comparison pass.

Use a fresh engine/session/history and clean DOM/clipboard state per isolated case. Shared fixture state, deleted-node retention, previous history and leaked listeners can mask failures. Multi-editor/replica tests create those peers deliberately. Instrument committed local/remote transactions, history boundaries, public updates and persistence enqueues separately; rejected/no-op actions assert zero attributable effects, without pretending independent remote edits or OS finalization did not happen.

## Fixture format and replay

Recipes use schemaVersion 1 with an ID, layer, catalog coverage, required capabilities, session context, initial state and ordered action/expected checkpoints. The JSON is a logical testing projection, not the CRDT schema, wire format or a second runtime model. Each expected state contains blocks/text/marks/hard-break offsets, directional selection/affinity and pending marks (null for context-derived, [] for explicit none). A hard-break offset points to an LF in a paragraph's flattened test projection; code LF remains literal. Public positions use UTF-16. The driver maps the projection to a qualified engine profile and fails explicitly when that profile cannot express it.

Initial logical block aliases are bound to actual stable IDs at fixture creation. Newly created aliases bind to the creating command's result; do not infer identity by searching final text. The adapter reports a canonical semantic snapshot using those bindings. Expected states are authored independently; do not update them from actual output automatically. Invalid command arguments are permitted in actions designed to reject, while every initial/expected state must itself be valid.

Within applyBatch, each later operation addresses the virtually updated state produced by preparing the preceding operations. For example, insert X at offset 1, then mark [1,2), marks the inserted X. Preparation must resolve and validate all operations without publishing intermediate mutations, then commit once. Rejection leaves the original state intact. This coordinate policy belongs to the action contract; the driver must never infer it from expect.state.

The initial JSON recipe profile covers paragraph/code text selections; node/cell selections and widget insertion anchors remain required catalog cases with an explicit later fixture-profile extension, not silently flattened text offsets. An action clockMs is a deterministic driver-clock advance used in history cases. Each step specifies its expected outcome and attributable local/remote commit counts. Full integration expands those into update, history and journal assertions at the relevant port; it cannot infer them merely from the number of commands. History recipes use explicit undo/redo states to expose grouping errors. The initial recipe set exercises representative existing cases and new failure patterns; it is not executable coverage for every catalog row. A recipe covers list is traceability to related cases, not a declaration that every variant of those cases is satisfied. Complete runtime bindings must enumerate and execute the missing variants separately. Catalog entries without a driver/test binding remain planned.

The nativeInsert recipe describes a controlled DOM mutation plus input/observer notifications with an explicitly missing beforeinput event. Its browser-replay driver must mutate the DOM, deliver the stated sequence and observe the real adapter; it must never write expected text directly into the engine. This replay proves the fallback mechanism, not actual keyboard/IME compatibility.

## Determinism, properties and sensitivity

Drive a fixed scheduler/clock for debounce, grouping and asynchronous providers. Await step-scoped quiescence: immediate engine/patch/reconciliation work has drained, required persistence for that step has settled, and selection has reached its acknowledged generation. A staged action such as beginPaste deliberately retains its declared pending request so later steps can interleave remote edits or cancellation. Require terminal disposition at complete/cancel/dispose or recipe teardown, not at the staging checkpoint. Teardown must report leaked requests rather than silently resolving them. Add a bounded timeout with diagnostics; avoid arbitrary sleeps, assuming one frame is enough, retrying until a test happens to pass, or waiting for unrelated network work.

Seeded generators admit only actions valid for the current schema/selection unless testing rejection. Required properties include atomic rejection; selection resolves after every accepted operation; UTF-16 boundaries remain valid; local undo preserves independent remote content; import/export preserves the declared semantic profile; normalization reaches a fixed point; duplicate/reordered delivery converges; canceled async work produces no local edit; and unrelated patches preserve caret/focus. Record seed, operation trace, Unicode/schema/tool versions and minimizer output. A passing random run is supplemental, not a replacement for the fixed regression corpus.

Before trusting a new assertion, run a targeted negative control: change one expected character, selection direction, retained mark, transaction count, pending-mark state or source/platform revision and prove it fails. Introduce a bounded fault at the final prepare check, post-commit subscriber, duplicate observer notification, stale async completion or cleanup path. Keep production instrumentation out of release bundles unless it is already a documented diagnostic port. Avoid broad mutation-testing infrastructure until specific guards need it.

## Coverage, execution and release

Every catalog ID maps to its existing implementation owner, layer, case revision and required profile. A binding reports one of planned, implemented-unexecuted, passed, failed, blocked or unsupported. Only actual nonzero assertions/device observations at matching revisions can report passed. Skips and unsupported optional APIs remain visible; required capability failures cannot be reclassified to pass.

Track 42 qualifies the common driver, representative recipes, guard sensitivity and reporting. Tracks 38/40/41 add their remaining behavior cases through that driver and maintain their existing device gates. `npm run check` in architecture validates planning artifacts only. Release evidence separately requires all mandatory mapped cases, guard checks and exact-version device rows. A stale result after a semantic, fixture, adapter or profile change is not reusable unless the owning task records why its dependencies are unaffected.

CI separates quick pure/command fixtures, browser mechanics, seeded bounded interleavings and scheduled/device qualification. All automated providers/transports are deterministic mocks and prepared data. No paid inference, ambient credentials, live recording or recognition-quality claims are part of this suite. Minimized field regressions use synthetic/nonsensitive content and retain source provenance without private documents.

It contains 42 roadmap files and 505 bounded parent tasks. These are development contracts, not claims of shipped capability; implementation status belongs in the runner’s separate progress and qualification evidence. The user selected public repositories and Apache-2.0. [Decision 001](decisions/001-web-first.md) resolves scope, ownership, naming and release conflicts. Check [setup evidence](evidence/setup.md), [dependency verification](evidence/dependencies.md) and the [full-delivery review](evidence/requirements-review.md). 2. Read [runner operation](operations/roadmap-runner.md), then the selected roadmap's entry gate. 3. Validate all sources with `npm ci --ignore-scripts` and `npm run check` in this repository. These commands do not execute workers or make inference calls. 4. Resume the designated runner using its recorded progress and immutable task source. Do not start a duplicate controller in an active checkout. # Requirement review and delivery mapping

Reviewed against the current docs on 2026-10-11. “Covered” below means planned contract/tasks, not shipped functionality. The existing scaffold does not establish editor behavior. The user's native desktop clarification includes macOS, Windows and Linux.

| Requirement | Existing coverage | Adjustment and delivery gate |
|---|---|---|
| First-class local-first/offline collaborative editing | 02 engine, 03 journal/recovery, 06 reconnect/receipts, 11 hosted CLI | 12 adds portable sessions, native stores, local channels, source catalog and offline policy; 20 verifies actual multi-client scenarios |
| Markdown/literal file editing and hosted CLI | Expanded 11 uses external editor; FMT-1.12 reconciles source | Preserve this work; 15 adds built-in TUI, ac:// routing, dirty-buffer conflicts and deterministic terminal qualification |
| Agent Markdown editing/uploads through embedding app MCP | Portable source reconciliation, commands/anchors and host auth responsibilities | 12 adds shared revision/policy/operation service; 14 adds host-tool schemas, prepare/diff/apply, durable retries and realtime observation; CLI MCP stays optional |
| Exact Git-like diffs and tracking | CRDT update/patch metadata only; no review/history API | 13 adds immutable representation-specific revisions, exact patches, semantic changes, review UI and restore-as-new-edit; native/TUI presenters consume it |
| PM ticket web/mobile/desktop embedding | Browser preset and React integration, native probes | 16/17/18/22/23 deliver real native editors; 20 qualifies the same mandatory ticket capabilities across all five native OS targets and web |
| Collaborative cross-platform documents | Browser/Rust fixtures; native future scope | Shared session/update profile and every actual client participate in 20 offline/crash/reconnect/composition tests |
| Native iOS/Android with same capabilities | 09 probes only | 16/17 deliver complete adapters, typed bindings, storage/sync, mandatory module UI and packaged consumers; actual device evidence closes in 20 |
| Native macOS/Windows/Linux | Not previously planned | Independent 18/22/23 platform tracks with toolkit feasibility, real native controls, bindings, package consumers and qualified support matrix |
| Readonly, undo/redo, custom references/extensions | Engine history and browser modules | Enforce readonly in shared mutation admission including MCP; qualify native/terminal histories and host-authorized reference hooks in every client |
| First-class extension library and thin core | Built-in browser modules and descriptors | 21 publishes coherent portable contracts, conformance harness, adapter hooks and third-party recipes; keep UI/network/MCP/crypto out of the semantic core |
| Optional encryption/private documents | Baseline safe import/auth only | 19 builds explicit local/E2EE profiles after threat-model/protocol selection; 24 gates real key providers, protected scenarios and independent review |

## Corrections to the proposed statements

- **Offline-first** includes cached/new local documents, supported crash recovery and explicit pending/rejected uploads. It cannot make uncached remote data available, prevent browser eviction, or erase a revoked user's already-held plaintext.
- **CLI/TUI collaboration** uses the same identity and command/recovery contracts. URLs resolve through configured hosts/catalogs; ordinary web pages and hash-looking strings do not confer edit authority.
- **MCP readiness** is a reusable host-app integration. Annotation hints are insufficient for permissions/idempotency; a Markdown candidate upload is revision-checked input to shared reconciliation, not a stale whole-document replacement.
- **Exact diff** names exact source bytes or a declared normalized projection and provides a separate semantic view. A Yjs state vector alone is not an exact revision token, and CRDT update bytes are not a review diff.
- **Native parity** needs actual editing/IME/accessibility/module evidence. Bindings and data-preserving fallbacks do not alone satisfy same-capability claims.
- **Encrypted mode** needs key/membership/rotation/recovery and a declared agent plaintext endpoint. An opaque relay cannot simultaneously decrypt Markdown or provide plaintext search/diffs.

## Why the planned core can support this

One portable authoritative replica, stable node identities/anchors, validated commands, origin-aware history, incremental patches and shared format reconciliation are the right prerequisites. New companion modules provide session/identity, revision/diff and optional security functions; presenters and MCP remain adapters. This is architectural compatibility by design, not proof that the future implementation meets every requirement.

The follow-up entry gates check the implemented schema/ABI and require a migration/compatibility decision if evidence contradicts the plan. The active foundation source/IDs remain untouched. Existing CLI amendments are preserved. See [decision 002](decisions/002-full-delivery.md), [scenario contract](specs/delivery-scenarios.md) and [primary-source implementation research](evidence/followup-research.md).

## Extension and ecosystem review — 2026-10-11

The user clarified that PDF is **export-only**. PDF import, OCR and PDF-reader dependencies are outside this plan. New format directions have explicit fidelity tiers; no “all document formats are lossless” promise is made.

| Requested addition | Existing baseline | Added delivery |
|---|---|---|
| Code blocks with fast syntax highlighting | Literal code/Markdown fences; no highlighting implementation track |25 portable optional highlighter/worker and performance fixtures;31–36 actual client wiring |
| Fast table formatting | Bounded rectangular table module |25 stable structural editing, cached layout, explicit Markdown formatter and stress/interactive envelopes |
| Images, attachments and embeds | Image metadata/host upload hook |25 staged blob lifecycle, bounded media, safe embed presenters;28 host asset service |
| Broad document interchange | Markdown, safe HTML and semantic JSON |27 DOCX/ODT/RTF/EPUB/CSV/TSV directions plus PDF export;31–36 client actions |
| Slash menu |07 local accessible menu |25 query lifecycle/large command catalog and no remote-open behavior; client integration gates |
| Drag/drop block editing |07 shared semantic move, keyboard/optional handle |25 pointer/touch/autoscroll/cancel and non-drag pointer alternative; native wiring |
| Customizable references |07/21 resolver and descriptor contract |26 typed host API, stable identity, caching, permission/cancellation, UI customization and documentation |
| Automatic URL title/favicon display | URL validation only |26 policy-enabled local-paste pipeline, safe metadata fetching and per-viewer display |
| Private/internal links | Host authority principle |26 principal-scoped API/cache, activation authorization, indistinguishable denial and no public-fetch fallback |
| Professional public docs repository | Architecture/internal specs plus planned API docs |Created public docs source repository;29 site generation, executable guides, versioning/search/accessibility and publication |
| Public demo | SDK consumer fixtures only |29 actual packaged-editor playground, local-first/multi-view scenarios, deployed URL verification and rollback |
| Cloud document-store readiness |06 test relay and12 store/transport ports |28 durable reference host with reusable storage adapters, tenant auth, asset finalization, recovery and deployment evidence |
| Maintainable ecosystem | Thin core and portable module model |30 executable layer, compatibility, capability, optional-loading, dependency and diagnostics gates;37 expanded qualification |

The baseline browser profile remains independently deliverable. Roadmaps31–35 preserve independent native implementation. Roadmap36 covers terminal representations without claiming graphical embed parity. Optional encrypted profile24 is extended to protect the new assets, converters, resolvers and cloud integration. Documentation site/demo publication and production cloud-provider qualification remain future tasks; a clean source repository is not evidence of a live editor deployment.

## Everyday editing and assistive technology

The October 11 interaction request is captured in [editor interactions](specs/editor-interactions.md), [targeted cases](tests/editor-interaction-cases.md), [research](evidence/editor-interaction-research.md) and [assistive input](specs/assistive-input.md). Coverage below means planned work; current browser packages are scaffolds.

| Requirement | Owner | Qualification |
|---|---|---|
| Enter/new blocks, Shift+Enter/same block, contextual code/list/table behavior | WEB-1.8; INT-1.2 | Semantic/caret snapshots, next typed character, storage/Markdown and undo |
| Selection formatting, toolbar focus, pending marks and alternate styles | INT-1.3 | Forward/backward/mixed/collapsed selections, explicit unsupported-format preservation |
| Backspace/Delete, graphemes, whitespace and special characters | INT-1.4, INT-1.8 | Unicode vectors, exact code points, boundary no-ops, valid UTF-16 and source recovery |
| Tab, Shift+arrows, cursor placement and platform keyboard controls | INT-1.5, INT-1.6 | Visual navigation, context focus escape, non-US layouts and native/AT shortcuts |
| IME, dictation, autocorrection, virtual keyboards and replacement | INT-1.7, INT-1.14 | Exactly-once deterministic traces plus actual OS/device observations |
| Slash-menu trigger, keyboard/pointer/AT controls and async results | MOD-1.4; INT-1.9; RCH-1.16 for scale | Stable query target, composition priority, focus retention, enabled results and undo |
| Paste flavors, literal mode, rich HTML, Markdown and parsing | INT-1.10, INT-1.11 | Pinned grammar, synthetic external-app payloads, safe atomic fallback and exact whitespace |
| History/races/read-only and accessibility baseline | INT-1.12–INT-1.14 | Zero-mutation rejection, independent remote history, real screen-reader/voice-control checks |
| Optional dictation/assistance extension and native integrations | AIN-1.1–AIN-1.11 | Shared descriptor, mocked lifecycle, independently gated native/TUI presenters and actual device evidence |

Track 38 is a prerequisite of browser release track 10; track 39 gates expanded ecosystem qualification 37. Basic accessible editing and OS dictation are baseline obligations, not optional-extension features. The catalog is a minimum regression set to grow with observed failures, not a promise to enumerate every possible browser/OS edge case.

## Touch devices and mobile web platforms

The mobile-web follow-up is captured in [mobile web](specs/mobile-web.md), [baseline tests](tests/mobile-web-cases.md), [extension tests](tests/mobile-extension-cases.md) and primary-source [platform](evidence/mobile-web-platform-research.md)/[touch](evidence/touch-extension-research.md) research. This is planned implementation/qualification, not a current capability claim.

| Requirement | Owner | Acceptance boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Native touch selection, long-press/context menu, scroll/zoom, stylus and mixed pointers | MWB-1.2 | Preserve OS editing, scoped gestures, cancellation, tap alternatives and accessible targets |
| Mobile typing, correction, swipe/handwriting, IME, repeated deletion and hardware keyboard changes | MWB-1.3 | Existing semantic/event contracts, exactly-once input and actual device observations |
| Keyboard occlusion, safe areas, viewport resize/zoom, rotation, split screens and embedding | MWB-1.4 | Observed geometry, stable selection/focus, bounded shared scheduling and fallback |
| Mobile command access and keyboard/browser API support | MWB-1.5, MWB-1.7 | Reachable controls without modifier keys; optional VirtualKeyboard/layout/lock and experimental EditContext with fallback |
| Mobile clipboard, picker/share blur, lifecycle/BFCache and recovery | MWB-1.6 | Stable targets, harmless cancellation, no duplicate callbacks or false unload durability |
| Small baseline core and bounded optional overhead | MWB-1.1, MWB-1.9; MWX-1.1, MWX-1.8 | No browser policy in Rust; frozen incremental/total budgets, lazy optional loading and measured lifecycle resources |
| Baseline modules on touch devices | MWB-1.8 | Native interaction preservation and visible command routes, even without enhanced presenters |
| Rich menus/references, code/tables, drag/resize, assets/embeds, conversion and assistive controls | MWX-1.2–MWX-1.7 | Feature-specific mobile edge cases through existing commands and host capabilities |
| Actual mobile web/platform support claims | MWB-1.10/1.11; MWX-1.8 | Mechanics separate from iPhone/iPad/Android device, keyboard, browser-mode and AT receipts |

Track 40 gates browser release 10 without requiring rich extensions or native SDKs. Track 41 gates expanded qualification 37; web assistance prerequisites are task-specific. Optional API absence is a tested fallback condition, not permission to drop required editing/accessibility behavior.

## Regression prevention and test-suite construction

[Round-two research](evidence/editor-regressions-round2.md) and [testing methods](evidence/editor-testsuite-methods.md) feed the [suite contract](specs/editing-regression-suite.md), [additional cases](tests/editor-regression-cases.md) and [machine-readable manifest](tests/editing-suite/suite.json). Coverage is specified for 195 cases; execution remains independently tracked.

| Requirement | Owner | Proof required |
|---|---|---|
| Consistent real-engine fixtures and selection/effect oracles | RGS-1.1/1.2 | Qualified logical-ID mapping, independently authored states, atomic text/mark/structure behavior |
| Undo grouping, transaction-entry selection and remote/rebase history | RGS-1.3 | Fixed-clock sequences including single-character paste/cut and mapped bookmarks |
| Exactly-once input, IME ownership and renderer echo suppression | WEB-1.13, RGS-1.4 | Pre-routing real-DOM/engine ADR qualification, then shared-driver production-adapter integration; correlated traces followed by deliberate identical edits; actual OS evidence stays separate |
| Normalization, Unicode and operation/interleaving invariants | RGS-1.5 | Version-pinned vectors, bounded seeds, convergence/fixed-point checks and minimized failures |
| Callback/async failure and disposal safety | RGS-1.6 | Fault injection at real ports, committed-state preservation and no late/refocused mutation |
| Custom views, widgets and nested clipboard/drop ownership | RGS-1.7 | Base then combined browser cases; exact identity/selection and one intended edit |
| Falsifiable coverage and CI qualification | RGS-1.8 | Negative controls, real assertion counts and matching revisions; no metadata-only passes |

Track 42 precedes 38, and thus the mobile/extension qualification tracks, without changing the native/browser ownership model. Engine compound-operation, selection-result, history and callback gaps are explicit prerequisites; sequential commits followed by repair/undo are not accepted as atomic editing.
